book_name: 终极单词(4) - 英语母语水平3000词

chapters.name: 英语词源拆解秘籍

words.ex: The sentence has ambiguity because it can mean two things.
words.ex_cn: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以有两种意思。
words.en: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: His ambition is to become a president.
words.ex_cn: 他的野心是成为总统。
words.en: An ambition is a strong desire to achieve something, typically requiring determination and hard work.

words.ex: He felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对接受这份工作邀约感到矛盾。
words.en: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, you mean that they have mixed feelings about it or are unsure whether they want it or not.

words.ex: The instructions are unambiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很清楚。
words.en: If you describe something as unambiguous, you mean that it is clear and cannot be misunderstood.

words.ex: The cardiac patient needs to rest daily.
words.ex_cn: 这位心脏病人需要每天休息。
words.en: Cardiac means relating to the heart.

words.ex: He runs every day to keep his cardiovascular system healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天跑步以保持心血管系统健康。
words.en: Relating to the heart and the blood vessels.

words.tr: v. 同意；继承；即位；加入
words.ex: He acceded to their request.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了他们的请求。
words.en: If you accede to someone's request, you do what they ask.

words.tr:
n. 前情；先行词；祖先（常复）
adj. 在 ... 之前的
words.ex: The word 'dog' is the antecedent of 'it' in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 在这句话中，'dog' 是 'it' 的先行词。
words.en: An antecedent is a thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.ex: The teacher gave precedence to students who arrived early.
words.ex_cn: 老师给早到的学生优先权。
words.en: If one thing takes precedence over another, it is regarded as more important than the other thing and is dealt with first.

words.tr: v. 后退；减弱；退出（某种活动）
words.ex: The flood waters begin to recede.
words.ex_cn: 洪水开始退去。
words.en: If something recedes, it becomes more distant or less noticeable.

words.tr: v. 退出组织；脱离团体
words.ex: The state decided to secede from the union.
words.ex_cn: 该州决定脱离联邦。
words.en: To withdraw formally from membership in a federal union, an alliance, or a political or religious organization.

words.ex: The police investigated the homicide case.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了这起凶杀案。
words.en: The act of killing another person, especially when it is considered a crime.

words.ex: Farmers use insecticide to kill bugs on crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用杀虫剂来杀死作物上的害虫。
words.en: A substance used for killing insects.

words.ex: He felt so sad that he thought about suicide.
words.ex_cn: 他感到非常难过，以至于想到了自杀。
words.en: Suicide is the act of deliberately killing oneself.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.tr: n. 要求者；索偿人；原告
words.ex: The claimant asked for money after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 索赔人在事故发生后要求赔偿。
words.en: A claimant is a person who makes a claim, especially in a legal case or for a state benefit.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.ex: He concluded that the experiment failed.
words.ex_cn: 他得出结论说实验失败了。
words.en: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

words.ex: The package includes a free book.
words.ex_cn: 这个套餐包括一本免费的书。
words.en: If one thing includes another, it has the other thing as one of its parts.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: He likes to seclude himself in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把自己 secluded 在森林里。
words.en: To seclude means to keep someone away from other people, or to keep something away from other things.

words.tr:
adj. 僻静的；隐僻的； 退隐的
v. 隔离；隔绝；隐居；“seclude”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is secluded in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋坐落在树林中，十分僻静。
words.en: A secluded place is quiet, private, and not near people or things that disturb you.

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.ex: The two countries reached a concord on trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上达成了一致。
words.en: Concord is a state of agreement or harmony between people or groups.

words.ex: The concordance of their opinions surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他们意见的一致性让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A concordance is an alphabetical list of the words in a text or corpus of texts, showing every occurrence of each word with its immediate context. It can also refer to agreement or harmony between people or things.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.tr: adj. 匆匆的；粗略的；仓促的
words.ex: He gave the report a cursory look.
words.ex_cn: 他粗略地看了看这份报告。
words.en: A cursory glance or examination is a quick one that is not very thorough.

words.ex: The army stopped the incursion at the border.
words.ex_cn: 军队在边境阻止了入侵。
words.en: An incursion is a sudden attack on or invasion of a place.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.tr: adj. 反复出现的；再发生的；
words.ex: He has recurrent headaches every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周都反复出现头痛。
words.en: Happening or appearing again or repeatedly.

words.ex: The king decided to abdicate in favor of his son.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定退位，让位给他的儿子。
words.en: If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen.

words.ex: He spoke with clear diction.
words.ex_cn: 他说话吐字清晰。
words.en: Diction refers to the choice and use of words and phrases in speech or writing, or the manner in which words are pronounced.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.ex: The prosecutor read the indictment in court.
words.ex_cn: 检察官在法庭上宣读了起诉状。
words.en: An indictment is a formal accusation that someone has committed a crime.

words.ex: The circumference of the circle is 31.4 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的周长是31.4厘米。
words.en: The circumference of a circle is the distance around it.

words.ex: He will defer his trip until next month.
words.ex_cn: 他将把旅行推迟到下个月。
words.en: If you defer an event or action, you arrange for it to happen at a later date, rather than immediately or at the previously planned time.

words.ex: He showed deference to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师表示尊敬。
words.en: Deference is a polite and respectful attitude towards someone, often because they are older or more experienced than you.

words.tr:
v. 献出；拿出；提供
n. 献出；拿出；提供
words.ex: He proffered a cup of tea to his guest.
words.ex_cn: 他递给客人一杯茶。
words.en: If you proffer something to someone, you offer it to them for acceptance.

words.tr: n. 参考；提及；介绍信；引用；
words.ex: Please use this book for reference.
words.ex_cn: 请使用这本书作为参考。
words.en: A reference is a mention of something or someone, or a letter or statement about someone's character or abilities.

words.ex: The police relied on an informant to find the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察依靠一名信息提供人找到了小偷。
words.en: An informant is someone who gives information to another person or organization, especially information that is secret or private.

words.tr: v. 表演；执行；履行；表现；“perform”的现在分词； adj. 表演的；演奏的；
words.ex: The children are performing a play at school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们正在学校表演一场戏剧。
words.en: The act of presenting a play, concert, or other form of entertainment. Also, the carrying out or accomplishment of an action, task, or function.

words.ex: The refugees lived in abject poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这些难民过着凄惨的贫困生活。
words.en: Abject means extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading.

words.tr:
adj. 沮丧的；低落的；垂头丧气的
v. 使…情绪低落；使沮丧；“deject”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt dejected after failing the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格后感到沮丧。
words.en: If you are dejected, you feel miserable or unhappy, especially because you have just been disappointed by something.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.tr: adj. 令人不快的；令人反感的；讨厌的
words.ex: The movie contains objectionable content.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影包含令人反感的内容。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as objectionable, you consider them to be extremely offensive and unacceptable.

words.tr:
n. 抛射物；射弹；发射物；自动推进武器
adj. 发射的；射弹的；推进的
words.ex: The boy threw a projectile into the air.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把一个抛射物扔向空中。
words.en: A projectile is an object that is thrown or shot forwards, such as a bullet fired from a gun.

words.ex: The teacher turned on the projector to show the video.
words.ex_cn: 老师打开投影仪来播放视频。
words.en: A projector is a machine that projects films or slides onto a screen or wall.

words.ex: He was neglectful of his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很疏忽。
words.en: If you describe someone as neglectful, you mean they fail to do everything they should do to look after someone or something properly.

words.ex: The mayor will reelect next year.
words.ex_cn: 这位市长明年将再次当选。
words.en: To elect someone again to a particular position.

words.tr: n. 年代学；年表；按年代次序的排列
words.ex: He wrote the chronology of ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 他写了古罗马的年代顺序。
words.en: Chronology is the arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence.

words.tr: n. 家谱学；系谱学；宗谱学；家谱（图）
words.ex: He is learning his family genealogy.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习自己的家族家谱。
words.en: Genealogy is the study of the history of families and the line of descent from their ancestors.

words.ex: The study uses a new methodology to collect data.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用了一种新的方法论来收集数据。
words.en: A methodology is a system of methods and principles for doing something, for example for teaching or for carrying out research.

words.ex: He is studying pathology to understand diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习病理学以了解疾病。
words.en: Pathology is the study of the causes and effects of diseases, especially the branch of medicine that deals with the laboratory examination of samples of body tissue for diagnostic or forensic purposes.

words.ex: He studies physiology to understand how the human body works.
words.ex_cn: 他学习生理学以了解人体如何运作。
words.en: The branch of biology that deals with the normal functions of living organisms and their parts.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.tr: n. 神学；宗教学；宗教信仰学
words.ex: He is studying theology at the university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习神学。
words.en: Theology is the study of the nature of God and religious belief.

words.ex: The teacher will announce the results tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天将宣布结果。
words.en: To announce something means to make it known publicly or officially.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.tr: v. 发音；宣告；“pronounce”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 显著的；
words.ex: He pronounced the word correctly.
words.ex_cn: 他正确地发音了这个单词。
words.en: Something that is pronounced is very noticeable or obvious.

words.tr: v. 声明放弃；与...断绝关系
words.ex: He renounced his citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年放弃了国籍。
words.en: If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you say and show that you no longer hold that belief or will behave in that way.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；无所不能的
words.ex: The god is omnipotent.
words.ex_cn: 这个神是无所不能的。
words.en: Having unlimited power, able to do anything.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.ex: Bears are omnivorous animals.
words.ex_cn: 熊是杂食动物。
words.en: An omnivorous animal or person eats both plants and meat.

words.ex: He entered a deep hypnosis during the therapy.
words.ex_cn: 他在治疗过程中进入了深度催眠状态。
words.en: Hypnosis is a state in which a person seems to be asleep but can still see, hear, or respond to things said to them.

words.tr: n. 神经症；神经衰弱症
words.ex: He has a neurosis about being late.
words.ex_cn: 他对迟到有一种神经症般的焦虑。
words.en: A neurosis is a mental illness that causes feelings of fear and worry, often leading to unreasonable behavior.

words.ex: He was diagnosed with tuberculosis last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被诊断出患有结核病。
words.en: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.ex: The accident caused paralysis in his legs.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致他双腿瘫痪。
words.en: Paralysis is the loss of the ability to move and sometimes to feel anything in part or most of the body, typically as a result of illness, poison, or injury.

words.ex: The teacher changed the parameter to make the test easier.
words.ex_cn: 老师更改了参数，使测试更容易。
words.en: A parameter is a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.ex: His paranoia made him believe that everyone was out to get him.
words.ex_cn: 他的多疑让他相信每个人都在算计他。
words.en: Paranoia is the unreasonable feeling that you are being threatened in some way, or that people are trying to harm you, without any evidence.

words.ex: He will depart tomorrow morning.
words.ex_cn: 他明天早上离开。
words.en: If you depart from a place, you leave it and start a journey to another place.

words.ex: He works in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售部工作。
words.en: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.tr: n. 个性；特性； 精确性；详尽
words.ex: He noted the particularity of her handwriting.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了她笔迹的特殊性。
words.en: The quality of being individual or unique; the state of being particular.

words.tr: n. 绝境；僵局；死路；死胡同
words.ex: The talks reached an impasse and no one could move forward.
words.ex_cn: 谈判陷入了僵局，没有人能继续前进。
words.en: An impasse is a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible, especially because of disagreement; a deadlock.

words.tr: n. 银行存折；南非共和国有色人种的身份证
words.ex: He checked his passbook to see his savings.
words.ex_cn: 他查看了存折来看他的存款。
words.en: A passbook is a small book containing a record of the deposits, withdrawals, and interest of a bank account.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.tr:
v. 非法侵入；侵扰；冒犯
n. 非法进入；冒犯
words.ex: He trespasses on private land.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自进入私人土地。
words.en: To trespass is to enter someone's land or property without their permission.

words.ex: He tried to dispel the fear with calm words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用平静的话语消除恐惧。
words.en: To dispel something such as a fear, belief, or idea means to make it disappear or to make people stop believing it.

words.ex: The danger impels him to act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 危险驱使他迅速行动。
words.en: If something impels you to do something, it makes you feel very strongly that you must do it.

words.ex: We use a repellent to keep mosquitoes away.
words.ex_cn: 我们使用驱虫剂来驱赶蚊子。
words.en: A repellent is a substance that is used to keep insects or animals away from something. It can also refer to something that is extremely unpleasant or disgusting.

words.ex: The decision is still pending.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定仍有待决定。
words.en: To hang or be suspended; to await a decision or resolution.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；迫在眉睫的； v. “impend”的现在分词；
words.ex: An impending storm made people stay indoors.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴让人们待在室内。
words.en: If an event or situation is impending, it is about to happen or is likely to happen very soon.

words.tr: adj. 互相依赖的；相倚的；
words.ex: The two countries are interdependent in trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上互相依赖。
words.en: If two or more things are interdependent, they depend on each other.

words.tr:
n. 垂饰；悬挂物
adj. 吊着的；悬垂的；悬而未决的
words.ex: She wears a silver pendant around her neck.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条银色吊坠在脖子上。
words.en: A pendant is a piece of jewelry that hangs from a chain worn around the neck.

words.ex: The pendulum swings back and forth in the clock.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆在钟里来回摆动。
words.en: A pendulum is a weight that is hung from a fixed point so that it can swing freely, especially a rod with a weight at the end that regulates the mechanism of a clock.

words.tr:
adj. 垂直的；笔直的
n. 垂直线
words.ex: The lines are perpendicular to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些线互相垂直。
words.en: At right angles to the plane of the horizon or a base line; vertical.

words.tr: n. 吊袜带；悬挂用的物体
words.ex: She wore a dress with white suspenders.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条带有白色吊袜带的裙子。
words.en: A suspender is a strap or band worn over the shoulders to hold up trousers or a skirt.

words.ex: He feels panic in small rooms because of claustrophobia.
words.ex_cn: 他因为幽闭恐惧症在小房间里感到恐慌。
words.en: A morbid fear of being closed in a confined space.

words.ex: He showed xenophobia toward people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人表现出恐外心理。
words.en: Xenophobia is a strong feeling of dislike or fear of people from other countries.

words.tr: v. 驱逐出境；使举止得体
words.ex: They will deport him for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 他们将因他违法而驱逐他。
words.en: If a government deports someone, usually someone who is not a citizen of that country, it sends them out of the country because they have committed a crime or because it believes they do not have the right to be there.

words.ex: The man faced deportation for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因违法而面临驱逐。
words.en: The act of expelling a person from a country, typically because they do not have the legal right to be there or because they have committed a crime.

words.ex: We arrived at the opportune moment, just as the meeting was starting.
words.ex_cn: 我们到达得很及时，正好会议刚开始。
words.en: If something happens at an opportune time or is opportune, it happens at the time that is most convenient for someone or most likely to lead to success.

words.tr: n. 入门；大门；入口网站
words.ex: This book is a portal to learning English.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是学习英语的入门。
words.en: A portal is a large and imposing entrance, doorway, or gate, or a website that provides access or links to other sites.

words.tr:
v. 声称；意指；意味着
n. 意义；要旨；主要意思
words.ex: The letter purports to be from the president.
words.ex_cn: 这封信声称是总统写的。
words.en: If something purports to be a particular thing or to do a particular thing, it claims or appears to be that thing or to do that thing, even though this may not be the case.

words.ex: He composes music in his spare time.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间创作音乐。
words.en: To compose something means to make it by combining parts or elements.

words.tr: v. 罢免；废黜；宣誓证明
words.ex: The people deposed the corrupt leader.
words.ex_cn: 人民推翻了腐败的领导人。
words.en: To depose someone means to remove them from a position of power or authority, especially a monarch or political leader.

words.ex: The children were exposed to cold weather without coats.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在没有外套的情况下遭受了寒冷天气。
words.en: To expose something means to uncover it so that it can be seen, or to make it known or public.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.ex: The file size is reduced by compression.
words.ex_cn: 通过压缩，文件大小被减小了。
words.en: Compression is the act or process of making something smaller or pressing it into a smaller space, or the state of being pressed or squeezed in this way.

words.tr:
v. 表达；表示；
adj. 明确的；
n. 特快列车；快件服务；
words.ex: He can express his feelings clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的感受。
words.en: If you express an idea or feeling, or express yourself, you show what you think or feel.

words.ex: He expressly told me not to be late.
words.ex_cn: 他特意告诉我不要迟到。
words.en: If something is said or done expressly, it is said or done in a clear, deliberate way.

words.ex: The king oppresses the poor people.
words.ex_cn: 国王压迫穷人。
words.en: If someone oppresses people, they treat them cruelly or unfairly and prevent them from having the same rights as other people.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: The volcano erupts suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 火山突然喷发。
words.en: If a volcano erupts, it throws out smoke, fire, and melted rocks.

words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.ex: The rupture in the pipe caused a flood.
words.ex_cn: 管道的破裂导致了洪水。
words.en: A rupture is a severe injury in which an internal part of your body tears or bursts open, or the act of breaking or bursting something.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.ex: He can describe the picture in one sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他能用一句话描述这幅画。
words.en: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

words.ex: He inscribes his name on the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在石头上。
words.en: To write, mark, or engrave (words, symbols, etc.) on a surface, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.ex: He found an old manuscript in the library.
words.ex_cn: 他在图书馆里发现了一份旧手稿。
words.en: A manuscript is a handwritten or typed document, especially a writer's first version of a book before it is published.

words.tr: v. 禁止；使失去法律保护
words.ex: The law proscribes selling alcohol to minors.
words.ex_cn: 法律禁止向未成年人出售酒精。
words.en: If a government or other authority proscribes a group or an activity, it officially forbids it or makes it illegal.

words.ex: The teacher will assign homework today.
words.ex_cn: 老师今天会布置作业。
words.en: To give someone a particular job or task; to allocate a resource or responsibility to a particular person or purpose.

words.tr: v. 委托；交付；托运；寄售
words.ex: He will consign the package to the post office.
words.ex_cn: 他将把包裹寄到邮局。
words.en: If you consign something to someone, you give it to them to keep or to sell.

words.ex: The shop sold the clothes on consignment.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店以委托方式销售这些衣服。
words.en: A consignment is a quantity of goods that are sent somewhere, especially in order to be sold.

words.tr: v. 辞职；使…顺从于（做）某事；
words.ex: He decided to resign from his job.
words.ex_cn: 他决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you resign from a job or position, you formally announce that you are leaving it.

words.ex: He assists his brother with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助弟弟做作业。
words.en: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

words.ex: She insists on going home now.
words.ex_cn: 她坚决要求现在回家。
words.en: If you insist on doing something, you keep doing it, even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: He tried to resist the temptation to eat sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抵制吃甜食的诱惑。
words.en: If you resist something such as a change, you refuse to accept it and try to prevent it.

words.ex: He works hard to earn his subsistence.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以维持生计。
words.en: Subsistence is the condition of just having enough food or money to stay alive.

words.tr: v. 戒绝；弃权；自我克制
words.ex: He abstains from eating sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他戒食糖。
words.en: If you abstain from something, you deliberately do not do it or have it, especially something you like or enjoy which might be considered bad for you.

words.ex: The box contains five apples.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子包含五个苹果。
words.en: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

words.ex: The containment of the fire took three hours.
words.ex_cn: 控制火势花了三个小时。
words.en: The act of keeping something harmful under control or within limits.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.ex: He is a strong contender for the championship.
words.ex_cn: 他是冠军的有力竞争者。
words.en: A contender is someone who takes part in a competition or tries to win something.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.ex: I intend to go to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我打算明天去公园。
words.en: If you intend to do something, you have decided or planned to do it.

words.ex: He attests that the document is true.
words.ex_cn: 他证明这份文件是真实的。
words.en: To attest something means to declare or affirm that it is true or genuine, often in a formal or legal context.

words.ex: He detests eating broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌吃西兰花。
words.en: If you detest something, you dislike it intensely.

words.tr:
v. 抗议；
n. 抗议活动；
words.ex: The students protest against the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 学生们抗议新的校规。
words.en: A protest is the act of saying or showing publicly that you object to something.

words.tr:
n. 证明书；推荐书
adj. 证明书的；表扬的
words.ex: She received a glowing testimonial from her former employer.
words.ex_cn: 她收到了前雇主的表扬推荐信。
words.en: A testimonial is a written statement about someone's character or abilities, or a thing given in recognition of service or achievement.

words.ex: The bright flowers attract bees.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的花朵吸引蜜蜂。
words.en: If something or someone attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them.

words.ex: His rude words detract from the beauty of the speech.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话贬损了演讲的优美。
words.en: If one thing detracts from another, it makes it seem less good or impressive.

words.ex: The extraction of coal harms the environment.
words.ex_cn: 煤炭的开采对环境有害。
words.en: The process of removing or obtaining something from something else.

words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.tr: n. 大片土地；体内管道；
words.ex: The farmer owns a large tract of land near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民拥有靠近河边的一大片土地。
words.en: A tract is a large area of land or a system of connected organs in the body.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.ex: She lives in a convent near the hill.
words.ex_cn: 她住在山边的一座修道院里。
words.en: A convent is a community of nuns living together under religious vows.

words.ex: He invented a new machine to clean the house.
words.ex_cn: 他发明了一台新机器来打扫房子。
words.en: To invent something means to design or create it, especially something that has never been made before.

words.ex: He drives a red convertible on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他周末开一辆红色敞篷车。
words.en: A convertible is a car with a roof that can be folded down or removed.

words.tr:
n. 性格外向者；爱交际的人
adj. 外向的
words.ex: He is an extrovert who loves talking to people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的人，喜欢和人交谈。
words.en: An extrovert is someone who is very outgoing, sociable, and enjoys being around other people.

words.tr: adj. 不注意的；疏忽的；非故意的
words.ex: He made an inadvertent mistake while typing.
words.ex_cn: 他在打字时不小心犯了个错误。
words.en: If something bad is inadvertent, it is done without realizing that it is wrong or that it could have bad consequences.

words.ex: He inadvertently dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他非故意地打翻了玻璃杯。
words.en: If you do something inadvertently, you do it without realizing it, or by accident.

words.ex: He tries to invert the numbers to find the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图将数字倒过来以找到答案。
words.en: To invert something means to turn it upside down or to reverse its position, order, or relationship.

words.tr:
v. 使堕落；误用；歪曲；使走邪路
n. 堕落者；性变态者；色狼
words.ex: He tried to pervert the truth with lies.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用谎言歪曲真相。
words.en: If you pervert something, you change it from what it should be or what it was originally intended to be into something that is wrong or harmful.

words.ex: He reverted to his old habits after the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 假期后，他恢复了旧习惯。
words.en: To return to a former state, practice, topic, etc.

words.ex: They tried to subvert the government.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图颠覆政府。
words.en: To subvert means to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.

chapters.name: Level 10 状态•存在类动词

words.ex: The coach changed his tactic to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 教练改变了战术以赢得比赛。
words.en: A tactic is a method or plan chosen to bring about a desired future, such as achieving a goal or solving a problem.

words.tr:
v. 回火；适得其反
n. 逆火
words.ex: The engine backfired when he pressed the gas pedal.
words.ex_cn: 当他踩下油门时，发动机回火了。
words.en: If a plan or project backfires, it has the opposite result to the one that was intended.

words.ex: The earthquake caused catastrophic damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: A catastrophic event or situation is one that causes great damage or suffering.

words.ex: The old man gave an enigmatic smile.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人露出了一个神秘的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as enigmatic, you mean they are mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.tr: n. 粗斜纹棉布；劳动布；牛仔布
words.ex: He wears blue denim jeans every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天穿蓝色牛仔裤。
words.en: Denim is a kind of cotton fabric, typically blue, used for making jeans, jackets, and other clothing.

words.ex: He was beset by problems at work.
words.ex_cn: 他被工作中的问题困扰。
words.en: If someone or something is beset by problems or fears, they have many problems or fears which affect them severely.

words.ex: The turtle moves in a sluggish way.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟移动得很缓慢。
words.en: If you describe something as sluggish, you mean that it is moving or working more slowly than usual.

words.ex: He is a drummer in a rock band.
words.ex_cn: 他是摇滚乐队的一名鼓手。
words.en: A drummer is a person who plays a drum or drums.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: He faced his adversary in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 他在决赛中对阵对手。
words.en: An adversary is someone who you are competing with, or who is opposing you or what you are trying to do.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr: phrase. 与……握手（表示问候、祝贺或达成协议）
words.ex: They shake hands with each other after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议结束后他们互相握手。
words.en: To clasp and move someone's hand up and down as a gesture of greeting, agreement, or farewell.

words.ex: The locust flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 蝗虫飞过了田野。
words.en: A locust is a large insect that lives in hot countries and flies in large groups, destroying crops.

words.tr: v. 将…分类；把…加以归类
words.ex: We categorize books by genre.
words.ex_cn: 我们按类型对书籍进行分类。
words.en: To categorize means to put people or things into groups according to their type or characteristics.

words.tr: adj. 濒临灭绝的；有灭绝危险的； v. “endanger”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The panda is an endangered animal.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫是一种濒临灭绝的动物。
words.en: An animal or plant that is endangered is in danger of becoming extinct.

words.ex: Pandas are endangered species.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫是濒危物种。
words.en: An endangered species is a type of organism that is at risk of extinction due to a rapid decrease in its population or a loss of its critical habitat.

words.ex: The clan lived in a small village for centuries.
words.ex_cn: 这个氏族几个世纪以来一直住在一个小村庄里。
words.en: A clan is a group of families or relatives who are connected by blood or marriage and who often share the same surname.

words.ex: Cats and dogs can coexist in the same house.
words.ex_cn: 猫和狗可以在同一个房子里共存。
words.en: To exist together at the same time or in the same place.

words.ex: The school is multicultural, with students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校是多元文化的，学生来自许多国家。
words.en: Relating to or containing several cultural or ethnic groups within a society.

words.ex: The aftermath of the storm left many trees down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，许多树被吹倒了。
words.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.

words.ex: The political turbulence caused many people to leave the country.
words.ex_cn: 政治骚乱导致许多人离开了这个国家。
words.en: A state of conflict or confusion; irregular atmospheric motion especially when characterized by up-and-down currents.

words.ex: The UN peacekeeping mission was crucial in maintaining stability in the region.
words.ex_cn: 联合国维和任务在该地区维持稳定方面至关重要。
words.en: Peacekeeping refers to the activities aimed at preventing or ending conflict, especially the deployment of international military and civilian forces to help maintain peace and security in areas of conflict.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: I have one apple.
words.ex_cn: 我有一个苹果。
words.en: One is used to refer to the first and lowest whole number, often used to indicate a single person or thing.

words.ex: The United Nations has called for an immediate ceasefire.
words.ex_cn: 联合国呼吁立即停火。
words.en: An international organization formed in 1945 to increase political and economic cooperation among its member countries.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

words.ex: Water causes erosion of the soil.
words.ex_cn: 水会导致土壤腐蚀。
words.en: The process by which the surface of the earth is worn away by the action of water, glaciers, winds, waves, etc.

words.tr: v. 到达…的顶点；达到高潮；告终
words.ex: The concert culminated with a loud fireworks show.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会以一场响亮的烟花表演结束。
words.en: If an event or series of events culminates in something, it ends with it, having developed until it reaches this point.

words.ex: The demise of the old king shocked the nation.
words.ex_cn: 老国王的去世震惊了全国。
words.en: The demise of something or someone is their end or death.

words.ex: The two countries are in the same bloc.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家属于同一个集团。
words.en: A bloc is a group of countries or parties with similar political interests, especially when they act together in international affairs.

words.ex: She wore a chic dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条别致的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as chic, you mean that they are stylish and fashionable.

words.tr:
n. 垂饰；悬挂物
adj. 吊着的；悬垂的；悬而未决的
words.ex: She wears a silver pendant around her neck.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条银色吊坠在脖子上。
words.en: A pendant is a piece of jewelry that hangs from a chain worn around the neck.

words.ex: The keys dangle from his belt.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙挂在他的腰带上。
words.en: If something dangles from somewhere or if you dangle it somewhere, it hangs or swings loosely.

words.tr:
n. 死亡
v. 死；死亡
words.ex: His decease was sudden and unexpected.
words.ex_cn: 他的去世突然且意外。
words.en: The death of a person.

words.ex: The coronation ceremony was a grand event.
words.ex_cn: 加冕典礼是一个盛大的活动。
words.en: A coronation is a ceremony in which a king or queen is officially crowned.

words.ex: The inauguration of the new bridge was celebrated with a parade.
words.ex_cn: 新桥的落成典礼以一场游行来庆祝。
words.en: The act of starting a new operation or practice; the formal admission of someone to office.

words.ex: He will defer his trip until next month.
words.ex_cn: 他将把旅行推迟到下个月。
words.en: If you defer an event or action, you arrange for it to happen at a later date, rather than immediately or at the previously planned time.

words.tr: adj. 模糊的；不确定的；无限期的
words.ex: He gave an indefinite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个不确定的答案。
words.en: If you describe something as indefinite, you mean that it has not been decided or defined clearly, or that it has no clear limit or end.

words.ex: The mirror deflects the light to the wall.
words.ex_cn: 镜子把光线反射到墙上。
words.en: If you deflect something such as criticism or attention, you act in a way that prevents it from being directed towards you or affecting you.

words.tr: n. 紫外线辐射；紫外光；
words.ex: The ultraviolet from the sun can hurt your skin.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的紫外线会伤害你的皮肤。
words.en: Ultraviolet light or radiation has a wavelength shorter than that of visible light but longer than X-rays.

words.tr:
n. 日灼；晒伤
v. 晒黑；晒伤
words.ex: He got sunburn after swimming all day.
words.ex_cn: 他整天游泳后得了日灼。
words.en: Sunburn is a condition where the skin becomes red, sore, and sometimes swollen and blistered as a result of overexposure to the ultraviolet rays of the sun.

words.ex: He wears a helmet to protect his head.
words.ex_cn: 他戴头盔来保护头部。
words.en: If you protect someone or something, you prevent them from being harmed or damaged.

words.ex: The accident disabled him for life.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他终身残废。
words.en: If an injury or illness disables someone, it affects them so badly that it restricts the way that they can live their life.

words.ex: He practices gymnastics every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上练习体操。
words.en: Gymnastics is a sport that involves exercises and movements that require physical strength, flexibility, balance, and control.

words.tr: n. 往返移动之物；航天飞机；
words.ex: The bus is a shuttle between the hotel and the airport.
words.ex_cn: 这辆巴士是酒店和机场之间的往返交通工具。
words.en: A shuttle is a vehicle that travels frequently between two places. In weaving, a shuttle is a device used to carry the weft thread back and forth across the loom.

words.ex: The old bridge will disintegrate if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人修理，这座旧桥会瓦解。
words.en: If something disintegrates, it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.

words.ex: He worked as a brewer in a local brewery.
words.ex_cn: 他在当地的一家酿酒厂做酿酒师。
words.en: A brewer is a person or company that makes beer.

words.ex: The company plans to diversify its products.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划使产品多样化。
words.en: To diversify means to make or become more varied or different. It often refers to the process of a company or individual expanding their range of products or activities to reduce risk or to explore new opportunities.

words.tr: n. 阵容，阵式；节目安排；全体参与人员；（指认）一排嫌疑犯（同 identification pa...
words.ex: The team has a strong line-up for the match.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在比赛中有一支强大的阵容。
words.en: A line-up is a group of people or things arranged in a particular way, especially for a specific purpose or event.

words.ex: The climbers found a foothold on the rocky wall.
words.ex_cn: 登山者在岩壁上找到了一个立足点。
words.en: A foothold is a secure position from which further progress or development may be made.

words.tr: n. 墓地；坟场；垃圾场；废物堆积处
words.ex: The old graveyard is quiet at night.
words.ex_cn: 那个古老的墓地晚上很安静。
words.en: A graveyard is an area of land, often near a church, where dead people are buried.

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.ex: The city hosted an exposition last summer.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市去年夏天举办了一场博览会。
words.en: An exposition is a detailed explanation or description of an idea or theory. It can also refer to a large public exhibition of art or trade goods.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

words.ex: The fire engulfed the old house.
words.ex_cn: 大火吞噬了那座老房子。
words.en: If one thing engulfs another, it completely covers or hides it, often in a sudden and unexpected way.

words.tr:
v. 齐射；齐发；迸发；截击
n. 齐射；齐发；迸发；截击
words.ex: The soldiers volleyed their guns at the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们向敌人齐射枪械。
words.en: A volley is a simultaneous discharge of a number of bullets, arrows, etc., or the act of hitting a ball before it bounces on the ground in sports such as tennis or volleyball.

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.ex: The termination of the contract surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 合同的终止让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The act of ending something or the end of something.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.ex: The penal system aims to punish criminals.
words.ex_cn: 刑罚制度旨在惩罚罪犯。
words.en: Relating to, used for, or prescribing the punishment of offenders under the legal system.

words.tr: v. 使平等；使均等；使相等
words.ex: The law aims to equalize opportunities for all people.
words.ex_cn: 法律旨在使所有人机会平等。
words.en: To make things equal in amount, size, or value.

words.tr:
n. 展示优点的场合（或机会）；
v. 展示…的优点；
words.ex: The competition was a showcase for her talent.
words.ex_cn: 这次比赛是她展示才华的机会。
words.en: A showcase is a setting in which someone or something is displayed to its best advantage, or a glass case used for displaying articles in a shop or museum.

words.tr:
adj. 就职的；开幕的；创立的
n. 就职演说
words.ex: He gave his inaugural speech last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚发表了就职演讲。
words.en: An inaugural event or speech is the first in a series planned to celebrate or introduce something.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.ex: The old castle is built from red sandstone.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡是用红色砂岩建造的。
words.en: Sandstone is a type of sedimentary rock composed mainly of sand-sized minerals or rock grains.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；高傲自大的
words.ex: He gave a haughty smile when he won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品时露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as haughty, you mean that they behave in a proud, unfriendly way, because they think that they are better than other people.

words.ex: The bureaucrat signed the paper slowly.
words.ex_cn: 这位官僚慢慢地签了那张纸。
words.en: A bureaucrat is an official who works in a bureaucracy, especially one who follows rules and procedures rigidly.

words.ex: The tree produces a sticky resin.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树会分泌一种粘稠的树脂。
words.en: A sticky substance secreted by some trees, used in varnishes, adhesives, and plastics.

words.tr:
v. （突然）烧旺；闪耀；突然爆发；张开；加剧
n. 旺火；亮光
words.ex: The fire began to flare up suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 火突然燃了起来。
words.en: A flare is a sudden bright light or flame, or a sudden increase in something such as activity or trouble.

words.tr: adj. 糟糕透顶的；恶劣的；卑鄙的
words.ex: He said a vile thing to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友说了句卑鄙的话。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is vile, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant.

words.tr:
v. 生气；用烟熏；冒烟
n. 烟雾；烟气；愤怒；烦恼
words.ex: He fumed when he saw the mess.
words.ex_cn: 他看到一团糟时生气了。
words.en: Fume refers to gas, smoke, or vapor that smells strongly or is dangerous to inhale. It can also mean to emit gas, smoke, or vapor, or to be very angry.

words.ex: The sign glows with bright neon light.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志发出明亮的霓虹光。
words.en: A colourless, odourless inert gaseous element occurring in minute amounts in the earth's atmosphere, used in fluorescent lights and illuminated advertising signs.

words.ex: The ad is on a big billboard near the road.
words.ex_cn: 广告牌在路边的大广告牌上。
words.en: A billboard is a large outdoor board for displaying advertisements.

words.ex: The candle's flicker lit up the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛的闪现照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: If a light or flame flickers, it shines unsteadily.

words.tr: v. 使牵连其中；涉及；暗示；指明起因
words.ex: The evidence may implicate him in the crime.
words.ex_cn: 证据可能使他牵连进这起犯罪中。
words.en: To show or suggest that someone is involved in something illegal or morally wrong.

words.ex: It was disgraceful to lie to your teacher.
words.ex_cn: 对老师撒谎是可耻的。
words.en: If you say that something is disgraceful, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or wrong, and that you find it completely unacceptable.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.ex: He missed three consecutive days of school.
words.ex_cn: 他连续三天没上学。
words.en: Consecutive events, numbers, etc. follow one after another without an interruption.

words.ex: The mistake will invalidate the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误会使结果无效。
words.en: To invalidate something such as a contract or an election means to make it officially not valid.

words.ex: Every worker has an entitlement to fair pay.
words.ex_cn: 每位工人都有获得公平报酬的权利。
words.en: An entitlement is a right to have or do something, often granted by law or policy.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；退款
v. 减少
words.ex: He got a rebate on his new TV.
words.ex_cn: 他买新电视时得到了一笔回扣。
words.en: A rebate is a partial refund to someone who has paid too much for tax, rent, or a utility.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；失误
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；失误；跌跌撞撞地走
words.ex: He made a big blunder in the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中犯了一个大错误。
words.en: A blunder is a stupid or careless mistake.

words.ex: Don't jeopardize your health by skipping meals.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为不吃饭而危及你的健康。
words.en: To jeopardize something means to do something that may destroy it or cause it to be lost.

words.tr:
adj. 秘密工作的；暗中做的
adv. 秘密地；暗中进行
words.ex: The police worked undercover to catch the thieves.
words.ex_cn: 警察卧底工作以抓捕小偷。
words.en: Involved in or relating to secret work within a community or organization, especially in the gathering of information.

words.tr: adj. 正在进行中的；航行中的；
words.ex: The project is underway.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: If something is underway, it is happening now.

words.tr:
n. 滞后；延迟；
v. 落后；缓慢移动；
words.ex: There is a lag between the signal and the response.
words.ex_cn: 信号和响应之间有滞后。
words.en: If one thing or person lags behind another thing or person, their progress is slower than that of the other.

words.tr: phrase. 一次经济复苏；指经济在衰退后逐渐恢复增长和稳定的过程
words.ex: The government is implementing policies to stimulate an economic recovery.
words.ex_cn: 政府正在实施政策以刺激经济复苏。
words.en: A period during which an economy improves after a period of decline or stagnation.

words.tr: n. 贸易保护主义；保护（贸易）主义
words.ex: The government uses protectionism to help local factories.
words.ex_cn: 政府使用保护主义来帮助本地工厂。
words.en: Protectionism is the policy of protecting domestic industries from foreign competition by taxing imports.

words.ex: The government will liberalize trade rules next year.
words.ex_cn: 政府明年将放宽贸易规则。
words.en: To make or become more liberal, especially by removing or reducing restrictions.

words.ex: She threaded a bead onto the string.
words.ex_cn: 她把一颗有孔的小珠穿在绳子上。
words.en: A bead is a small piece of glass, wood, or plastic that is used for decorating clothes or making jewellery.

words.ex: He wiped away the perspiration from his forehead.
words.ex_cn: 他擦去了额头上的汗。
words.en: Perspiration is the process of sweating, or the sweat itself, that occurs in humans and some animals as a way of regulating body temperature.

words.ex: She moistened the dry bread with water.
words.ex_cn: 她用水把干面包弄湿了。
words.en: To make something slightly wet.

words.tr: n. 工作服；罩衫；宽松式衬衫
words.ex: The painter wore a smock to protect his clothes.
words.ex_cn: 画家穿了一件工作服来保护他的衣服。
words.en: A smock is a loose garment worn over clothes to protect them while working or doing messy tasks.

words.ex: The rain necessitated staying indoors.
words.ex_cn: 下雨使待在室内成为必需。
words.en: To necessitate something means to make it necessary for something to be done or to happen.

words.ex: He follows a dietary plan to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循一种饮食计划来保持健康。
words.en: Relating to the diet or the kinds of food that a person, animal, or community habitually eats.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.ex: The city is predominantly populated by young people.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市主要由年轻人居住。
words.en: If something is predominantly true, it is true to a much greater extent than it is false.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.tr: n. 神学；宗教学；宗教信仰学
words.ex: He is studying theology at the university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习神学。
words.en: Theology is the study of the nature of God and religious belief.

words.tr: v. 授予圣职；命令；注定
words.ex: The priest will ordain the new pastor next Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 神父将在下个星期日任命这位新牧师。
words.en: To ordain someone as a priest or minister means to officially make them a priest or minister, usually in a religious ceremony. To ordain something means to order or command it officially.

words.ex: The vicar helps people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 牧师帮助村子里的人们。
words.en: A vicar is a priest in the Church of England who is in charge of a parish.

words.ex: He plans to travel the world after graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他计划毕业后环游世界。
words.en: After graduation refers to the period or activities following the completion of a course of study at a college or university.

words.ex: He is the beneficiary of his father's will.
words.ex_cn: 他是他父亲遗嘱的受益人。
words.en: A beneficiary is someone who receives money or other benefits as a result of something, especially a will or insurance policy.

words.ex: The benefits outweigh the risks.
words.ex_cn: 好处超过了风险。
words.en: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.

words.ex: The project cost overrun the budget.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的成本超过了预算。
words.en: If an army or a group of people overruns a place, they take control of it by force. If something such as a place or a piece of land is overrun by things or people, it is filled with them and they spread everywhere.

words.ex: He caught influenza last winter.
words.ex_cn: 他去年冬天得了流感。
words.en: Influenza is an infectious disease caused by the influenza virus, characterized by fever, sore throat, muscle pain, severe headache, coughing, and weakness.

words.tr:
adj. 如野兽的；残忍的；令人不快的
adv. 非常
words.ex: The beastly storm destroyed the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场如野兽般的风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: If you describe something as beastly, you mean it is very unpleasant or disagreeable.

words.ex: They celebrate midsummer with fireworks and dancing.
words.ex_cn: 他们用烟花和舞蹈庆祝仲夏。
words.en: Midsummer is the period in the middle of summer, typically around the summer solstice, the longest day of the year.

words.ex: The sun parched the land.
words.ex_cn: 太阳晒干了土地。
words.en: To make something very dry, especially by exposure to heat.

words.ex: He used too much jargon in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中用了太多行话。
words.en: Special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.ex: He is learning biochemistry at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习生物化学。
words.en: The branch of science concerned with the chemical processes occurring within living organisms.

words.tr: adj. 扭歪的；啼笑皆非的；挖苦的；讽刺的
words.ex: He gave a wry smile when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时露出了苦笑。
words.en: If someone has a wry expression, it shows that they find a bad situation or a change in a situation slightly amusing.

words.tr: adj. 极好的；令人震惊的； v. “stun”的现在分词；
words.ex: She wore a stunning dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件极好的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Extremely impressive or attractive.

words.ex: The ball rebounded off the wall.
words.ex_cn: 球从墙上弹了回来。
words.en: To bounce back after hitting something; to recover in value, amount, or strength after a decrease or decline.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉药；镇定剂；致幻毒品
adj. 麻醉的；催眠的
words.ex: He took a narcotic for his pain.
words.ex_cn: 他服了一种麻醉药来缓解疼痛。
words.en: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, relieves pain, and induces sleep. It can also refer to something that has a soothing or numbing effect.

words.ex: The venerable teacher has taught for over 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位值得尊敬的老师已经教书40多年了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as venerable, you mean that they are old and respected.

words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.ex: He was born a commoner but rose to become a respected leader.
words.ex_cn: 他出身平民，但最终成为受人尊敬的领袖。
words.en: A commoner is someone who is not of noble rank.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；不能理解的；无责任的
words.ex: The manager made unaccountable decisions.
words.ex_cn: 这位经理做出了无法解释的决定。
words.en: If someone or something is unaccountable, there is no way of explaining why they behave in a particular way, and it is often strange or surprising.

words.tr:
n. 带位员；接待员；门房
v. 引领；招待；做招待员
words.ex: The usher showed us to our seats in the theater.
words.ex_cn: 带位员带我们到了剧院的座位。
words.en: An usher is someone who shows people where to sit, especially at a formal event such as a wedding or a concert. As a verb, to usher means to show someone where to go or to lead them somewhere.

words.tr: v. 发慈悲；动怜悯心；缓和
words.ex: The teacher finally relented and gave the students more time.
words.ex_cn: 老师终于发慈悲，给了学生们更多时间。
words.en: If you relent, you allow someone to do something that you had previously refused to allow them to do.

words.tr: n. 举办地点；（比赛）地点；会场；
words.ex: The concert will be held at a new venue.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会将在一个新的举办地点举行。
words.en: A place where an event or meeting is held, such as a concert hall or conference center.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使糊涂；胡乱应付
n. 混乱；糊涂
words.ex: He muddled the instructions and got confused.
words.ex_cn: 他把说明搞混了，感到困惑。
words.en: If you muddle things or people, you get them mixed up, so that you do not know which is which.

words.ex: He reverted to his old habits after the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 假期后，他恢复了旧习惯。
words.en: To return to a former state, practice, topic, etc.

words.tr: n. 封建主义；封建制度
words.ex: Feudalism was common in medieval Europe.
words.ex_cn: 封建主义在中世纪的欧洲很普遍。
words.en: Feudalism is a social system that existed in Europe during the Middle Ages in which people worked and fought for nobles who gave them protection and the use of land in return.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.tr: v. 彻底变革；使革命化；
words.ex: The new technology will revolutionize how we learn.
words.ex_cn: 这项新技术将彻底变革我们的学习方式。
words.en: To completely change something, especially in a way that improves it.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: The doctor tested his urine for infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生检测了他的尿液是否有感染。
words.en: Urine is the liquid that you get rid of from your body when you go to the toilet.

words.ex: A snowflake falls gently from the sky.
words.ex_cn: 一片雪花轻轻从天空飘落。
words.en: A snowflake is a single ice crystal that has achieved a sufficient size, and may have amalgamated with others, which falls through the Earth's atmosphere as snow.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；发微光
n. 微光；闪光
words.ex: The lake shimmers under the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 湖面在月光下闪烁。
words.en: To shine with a soft, slightly wavering light.

words.tr: n. 罗勒属植物（用于调味）；斜刃面
words.ex: She adds fresh basil to the pasta.
words.ex_cn: 她把新鲜的罗勒加到意大利面里。
words.en: A herb of the mint family, used in cooking to add flavor to dishes, especially in Mediterranean cuisine.

words.tr: n. 肉汤；（鱼、肉或蔬菜）汤
words.ex: He is drinking hot broth for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他正在喝热汤当晚餐。
words.en: A liquid in which meat, fish, cereal grains, or vegetables have been cooked; it forms the basis of many soups and sauces.

words.tr:
v. 煨；用文火炖；充满；即将爆发
n. 炖；即将发作
words.ex: The soup is simmering on the stove.
words.ex_cn: 汤正在炉子上慢炖。
words.en: To cook something slowly at a temperature slightly below boiling point.

words.tr: n. 代码；编码；行为准则；密码；法典；
words.ex: He wrote a simple code to solve the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一段简单的代码来解决这个数学问题。
words.en: A code is a system of words, letters, figures, or other symbols substituted for other words, letters, etc., especially for the purposes of secrecy. As a verb, it means to convert (a message or other information) into a code.

words.ex: The fish spawn in the river each spring.
words.ex_cn: 鱼每年春天在河里产卵。
words.en: To spawn means to produce or deposit eggs, especially in large quantities, as fish, frogs, etc. do. It can also mean to give rise to or generate something.

words.tr: v. 发芽；长出；迅速成长；涌现；
words.ex: The seed will sprout in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这颗种子会在春天发芽。
words.en: If a plant sprouts, or if it sprouts something, it produces new leaves or buds.

words.ex: We walked along the promenade by the sea.
words.ex_cn: 我们在海边的步行区散步。
words.en: A promenade is a leisurely walk, especially one taken in a public place for pleasure or display.

words.ex: The knight held a long lance in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 骑士手中握着一支长矛。
words.en: A lance is a long weapon used in the past by soldiers on horseback, consisting of a wooden shaft with a pointed metal end. As a verb, to lance means to pierce or cut open with a sharp instrument, especially a lance.

words.tr:
v. 喷射；迸发；突然加速努力
n. 迸发；喷出；突然一阵
words.ex: The pipe spurted water everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 管道喷出了水，四处都是。
words.en: A spurt is a sudden burst of activity, speed, or growth. It can also refer to a sudden stream of liquid that comes out quickly and forcefully.

words.ex: He will subdivide the land into two parts.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地分成两部分。
words.en: If something is subdivided, it is divided into several smaller areas, parts, or sections.

words.ex: The legality of the contract is being checked.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同的合法性正在被检查。
words.en: The state or quality of being in accordance with the law.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；有问题的；不可靠的；
words.ex: The deal seemed questionable.
words.ex_cn: 这笔交易看起来可疑。
words.en: If you say that something is questionable, you mean that it is not obviously true or real, and therefore possibly not valid or reliable.

words.tr: adj. 富有魅力的；迷人的；
words.ex: She wore a glamorous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条富有魅力的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as glamorous, you mean that they are more attractive, exciting, or interesting than ordinary people or things.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.ex: His melodramatic crying made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他感情夸张的哭泣让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as melodramatic, you are criticizing them for acting in a way that is too emotional or exaggerated.

words.ex: The new policy undercut the company's profits.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策削弱了公司的利润。
words.en: To undercut means to sell something at a lower price than a competitor, or to weaken something or someone.

words.ex: The authenticity of the ancient painting was confirmed by experts.
words.ex_cn: 这幅古画的真实性得到了专家的确认。
words.en: The quality of being genuine or not corrupted from the original.

words.tr: adj. 无瑕疵的；无缺点的；
words.ex: Her performance was flawless.
words.ex_cn: 她的表演毫无瑕疵。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is flawless, you mean that they are extremely good and that there are no faults or problems with them.

chapters.name: Level 10 沟通类动词

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.tr: adj. 不可比拟的；无比的；无与伦比的；不能比较的；
words.ex: Her singing is incomparable.
words.ex_cn: 她的歌唱是无可比拟的。
words.en: If you describe something as incomparable, you mean that it is so good or great that nothing else can be compared to it.

words.ex: He told a long saga about his grandfather's adventures.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他祖父冒险的漫长故事。
words.en: A long, detailed story of connected events, especially one that is passed from one generation to the next.

words.tr:
n. 和平主义者；反战主义者
adj. 非战主义的
words.ex: He is a pacifist and refuses to fight in wars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名和平主义者，拒绝参与战争。
words.en: A pacifist is someone who believes that war and violence are unjustifiable and that disputes should be settled by peaceful means.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.ex: His main shortcoming is being late often.
words.ex_cn: 他的主要缺点是经常迟到。
words.en: A shortcoming is a fault or a failure to meet a certain standard, which means a person or thing is not as good as they should be.

words.tr: adj. 官僚的；官僚主义的；
words.ex: The bureaucratic process made it hard to get a permit.
words.ex_cn: 官僚程序让申请许可证变得困难。
words.en: If you describe a system, organization, or process as bureaucratic, you mean that it is complicated and inefficient because of a large number of rules and procedures.

words.ex: The study uses a new methodology to collect data.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用了一种新的方法论来收集数据。
words.en: A methodology is a system of methods and principles for doing something, for example for teaching or for carrying out research.

words.tr: adj. 多虱的；可鄙的；差劲的
words.ex: The dog had a lousy coat full of fleas.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗的毛发多虱子。
words.en: If you describe something as lousy, you mean that it is of very bad quality or that you do not like it.

words.tr:
n. 私生子；浑蛋
adj. 私生的
words.ex: He called his brother a bastard during the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵时称他哥哥是杂种。
words.en: A bastard is a child whose parents were not married to each other at the time of its birth. This term can also be used as an insult to describe someone who is considered to be despicable or unpleasant.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；吼叫；咆哮
n. 咆哮；怒号
words.ex: The bull bellowed loudly in the field.
words.ex_cn: 公牛在田野里大声吼叫。
words.en: If someone bellows, they shout angrily in a loud, deep voice.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.ex: His supposition is that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是明天会下雨。
words.en: A supposition is a guess or a theory that you have about something, which may not be true.

words.ex: The study found a causal link between smoking and lung cancer.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究发现了吸烟与肺癌之间的因果关系。
words.en: A causal factor or event is one that causes or leads to something else.

words.tr: phrase. 因果关系；表示一个事件（原因）导致另一个事件（结果）的关系
words.ex: Smoking has a causal relationship with lung cancer.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟与肺癌之间存在因果关系。
words.en: A causal relationship is a relationship between two variables in which one variable is the cause of the other.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.tr: adj. 无结果的；无成效的；
words.ex: The meeting was fruitless because no decisions were made.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议毫无结果，因为没有做出任何决定。
words.en: If an action or attempt to do something is fruitless, it is unsuccessful or produces nothing of value.

words.ex: The police caught the culprit who stole the bike.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了偷自行车的罪犯。
words.en: A culprit is someone who has done something wrong or illegal.

words.tr: v. 萦绕；“haunt”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The memory of his mistake still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 他错误的回忆仍然萦绕着他。
words.en: If a place is haunted, it is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.ex: They stayed at a motel near the highway.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在高速公路旁的一家汽车旅馆。
words.en: A motel is a hotel which is designed for people who are travelling by car, usually with parking spaces next to each room.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.tr: n. 不在犯罪现场证明；辩解；托辞
words.ex: He gave an alibi that he was at home.
words.ex_cn: 他提供了一个他在家的不在场证明。
words.en: An alibi is a form of defense used in criminal procedure wherein a defendant attempts to prove that he or she was in some other place at the time the alleged offense was committed.

words.ex: He wrote a treatise on ancient Chinese philosophy.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于中国古代哲学的专著。
words.en: A treatise is a formal and systematic written discourse on some subject, generally longer and more detailed than an essay.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: The instability of the bridge made people afraid to cross it.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的不稳定让人们不敢过桥。
words.en: Instability is the state of being unstable, especially in a political or economic context, where it refers to a lack of stability or the tendency to change or fail suddenly.

words.tr:
v. 声称；意指；意味着
n. 意义；要旨；主要意思
words.ex: The letter purports to be from the president.
words.ex_cn: 这封信声称是总统写的。
words.en: If something purports to be a particular thing or to do a particular thing, it claims or appears to be that thing or to do that thing, even though this may not be the case.

words.tr: adj. 决定性的；权威性的；确定的；
words.ex: The test results were definitive.
words.ex_cn: 这些检测结果是决定性的。
words.en: A definitive book, performance, or report is considered to be the best of its kind that has ever been done or that will ever be done.

words.ex: The piano duo played a beautiful song.
words.ex_cn: 这对钢琴二重奏演奏了一首优美的曲子。
words.en: A duo is a pair of people or things, especially musicians or performers, who work together or are associated in some way.

words.tr: abbr. 激光唱片；光盘；“Compact Disc”的缩写
words.ex: I bought a cd of my favorite songs.
words.ex_cn: 我买了一张我最爱歌曲的激光唱片。
words.en: A chemical element (symbol Cd) that is a soft, bluish-white metal, often used in batteries and pigments, and is toxic.

words.ex: He plays music on a compact disc.
words.ex_cn: 他用光盘听音乐。
words.en: A compact disc is a small plastic disc on which music or other digital information is stored in the form of a pattern of metal-coated pits from which it can be read using laser light.

words.ex: He likes to ramble about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢漫谈他的旅行经历。
words.en: To walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside, without a definite route or destination.

words.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
words.ex_cn: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。
words.en: A plight is a difficult or adverse situation, especially one that is hard to escape. It can also refer to a solemn promise or pledge.

words.tr: adj. 处于不利地位的；贫困的； v. “disadvantage”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The school helps disadvantaged children with free meals.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校为处境不利的孩子提供免费餐食。
words.en: People who are disadvantaged do not have the same opportunities or advantages as other people, often because of their financial situation or social position.

chapters.name: Level 10 动作类动词

words.tr:
adj. 极小的；特小的；微小的
n. 小的人；指小词缀；爱称
words.ex: The diminutive cat sat on the small mat.
words.ex_cn: 那只小巧的猫坐在小垫子上。
words.en: A diminutive person or object is very small.

words.ex: The hue of the sky changed at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空的色调发生了变化。
words.en: A hue is a particular shade of a color.

words.tr:
v. 落下；
adj. 点亮的；
words.ex: The bird alighted on the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟落在了树上。
words.en: If someone alights from a vehicle or if they alight, they get out of it after a journey.

words.ex: The cerebral cortex controls thinking and memory.
words.ex_cn: 大脑皮层控制思考和记忆。
words.en: Relating to the brain or the intellect.

words.tr:
v. 猛击；重打
n. 猛击；重击；盛会
words.ex: He bashed the door with his fist.
words.ex_cn: 他用拳头猛击门。
words.en: To hit someone or something very hard; a big party or celebration.

words.ex: The skull protects the brain.
words.ex_cn: 颅骨保护大脑。
words.en: The bony framework of the head that encloses the brain and supports the structures of the face.

words.tr:
n. 辫子；穗带
v. 编辫子；编织
words.ex: She wore a long braid down her back.
words.ex_cn: 她身后垂着一条长长的辫子。
words.en: A braid is a complex structure or pattern formed by intertwining three or more strands of flexible material such as textile fibers, wire, or hair.

words.tr: v. 招手示意；举手召唤；引诱
words.ex: He beckoned to the boy to come closer.
words.ex_cn: 他向那个男孩招手示意过来。
words.en: If you beckon to someone, you signal to them to come to you, usually by a gesture of your hand.

words.tr:
adj. 浅黄色的；黄皮革制的
n. 浅黄色；浅黄色皮革；爱好者
v. 用软布擦亮
words.ex: The buff walls looked warm in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 浅黄色的墙壁在阳光下显得温暖。
words.en: A buff is a person who is very interested in and knowledgeable about a particular subject.

words.ex: She bought a dress from a small boutique downtown.
words.ex_cn: 她在市中心的一家小型时装精品屋买了一条裙子。
words.en: A boutique is a small shop that sells stylish clothes, shoes, or jewelry.

words.ex: The magazine has a glossy cover.
words.ex_cn: 这本杂志有一个光滑的封面。
words.en: Something that is glossy is smooth and shiny.

words.ex: The bustle of the market filled the morning air.
words.ex_cn: 市场的喧哗充满了早晨的空气。
words.en: If someone bustles somewhere, they move there in a hurried way, often because they are very busy or excited.

words.ex: She placed the cutlery neatly on the table.
words.ex_cn: 她把餐具整齐地放在桌子上。
words.en: Cutlery refers to the tools used for eating or serving food, such as knives, forks, and spoons.

words.tr:
adj. 狂热入迷的；盲信的
n. 狂热者；盲信者
words.ex: He is a fanatic fan of soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他对足球狂热入迷。
words.en: A fanatic is a person who is very enthusiastic about and devoted to a particular activity, cause, or belief, often to an extreme degree.

words.tr: v. 扔；抛；丢掷；放弃；离职
words.ex: He chucked the old book into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把那本旧书扔进了垃圾桶。
words.en: To throw something carelessly or casually; to give up or stop doing something.

words.ex: The soldier threw a grenade into the enemy bunker.
words.ex_cn: 士兵把一颗手榴弹扔进了敌人的掩体。
words.en: A grenade is a small bomb that can be thrown by hand or launched from a rifle.

words.tr: n. 大破坏；大毁坏；大混乱；
words.ex: The storm caused havoc in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给这个小镇带来了大破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as havoc, you mean that it causes a great deal of disorder, confusion, or destruction.

words.tr:
v. （艰难地）爬上；攀登
n. （艰难地）爬；攀登
words.ex: The boy clambered up the rocky hill.
words.ex_cn: 男孩爬上了多石的山丘。
words.en: If you clamber somewhere, you climb there with difficulty, usually using your hands as well as your feet.

words.ex: The phone rung three times before she answered.
words.ex_cn: 电话响了三声，她才接起来。
words.en: A rung is one of the horizontal supports on a ladder for a person's foot.

words.tr: adj. 昏暗的；暗淡的；暗黑的
words.ex: The sky became dusky at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空变得昏暗。
words.en: Dusky is used to describe something that is dark in color or not bright, especially in a way that is attractive or mysterious.

words.ex: He turned the loft into a bedroom.
words.ex_cn: 他把阁楼改成了卧室。
words.en: A loft is a room or space directly under the roof of a building, used for accommodation or storage.

words.ex: The diary entries were fragmentary and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这些日记条目是不完整的，难以理解。
words.en: Consisting of small parts that are disconnected or incomplete.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.ex: The table is made of granite.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是花岗岩做的。
words.en: Granite is a very hard rock that is often used in building.

words.ex: The potter made a clay bowl by hand.
words.ex_cn: 陶工用手制作了一个陶碗。
words.en: A potter is someone who makes pottery, and to potter means to busy oneself in a desultory but pleasant manner.

words.ex: He engraves his name on the ring.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在戒指上。
words.en: To engrave means to cut or carve a design or letters into a hard surface, or to be strongly impressed in someone's memory.

words.ex: She wore a dainty necklace with tiny pearls.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一条小巧精致的珍珠项链。
words.en: If you describe something as dainty, you mean that it is small, delicate, and pretty.

words.tr:
v. 轻弹；轻击；轻拂；忽然摇动
n. 轻弹；轻拂；快速的轻打
words.ex: He flicked the light switch on.
words.ex_cn: 他 flick 了一下电灯开关。
words.en: To move or hit something with a quick, sharp movement.

words.tr: n. 烟蒂；屁股；枪托；笑柄
words.ex: He picked up the butt from the ground and threw it in the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起烟蒂，扔进了垃圾桶。
words.en: The end of a cigarette that is left after smoking; the part of the body that a person sits on; a person or thing that is a target for ridicule or criticism; to hit or push someone or something with the head or horns.

words.ex: He drank coffee from a large mug.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个大杯子里喝咖啡。
words.en: A mug is a large, deep cup with straight sides and a handle, used for hot drinks. It can also refer to someone's face or a foolish person. As a verb, it means to attack and rob someone violently in a public place.

words.tr: n. 吊袜带；悬挂用的物体
words.ex: She wore a dress with white suspenders.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条带有白色吊袜带的裙子。
words.en: A suspender is a strap or band worn over the shoulders to hold up trousers or a skirt.

words.tr:
n. 不成功；
v. 猛落；沉重地落下；
words.ex: The movie was a flop at the box office.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影在票房上失败了。
words.en: If something flops, it is completely unsuccessful.

words.tr: phrase. 拿掉；离开；起飞；脱下；突然成功
words.ex: Please take off your hat before entering.
words.ex_cn: 进入前请把帽子拿掉。
words.en: If an aircraft, bird, or insect takes off, it leaves the ground and begins to fly.

words.tr:
v. 乱摸；摸索；笨手笨脚地做
n. 摸索；笨手笨脚
words.ex: He fumbled for his keys in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中乱摸着找钥匙。
words.en: If you fumble with something, you try to hold, move, or find it with your hands in a clumsy way.

words.ex: She wears a ruby ring on her finger.
words.ex_cn: 她手指上戴着一枚红宝石戒指。
words.en: A ruby is a precious stone that is typically a deep red color.

words.ex: She hangs her clothes on the clothesline.
words.ex_cn: 她把衣服挂在晾衣绳上。
words.en: A clothesline is a rope or wire on which wet clothes are hung to dry.

words.ex: The doctor put a gag in his mouth to keep it open.
words.ex_cn: 医生在他的嘴里放了一个塞口物以保持口腔张开。
