words.ex: She has an affinity for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她喜爱绘画。
words.en: A natural liking for or attraction to someone or something.

words.tr: n. 对抗；对立；敌对状态（行为）
words.ex: There is antagonism between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有敌意。
words.en: Antagonism is a strong feeling of dislike or opposition towards someone or something.

words.ex: He has an aversion to spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶辛辣食物。
words.en: A strong dislike or disinclination towards someone or something.

words.ex: The movie shows the brutality of war.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了战争的残忍。
words.en: Brutality is cruel and violent behavior, or a cruel and violent act.

words.ex: He kept his composure during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试中保持了冷静。
words.en: The state of being calm and in control of your emotions.

words.ex: He lost his job because of dishonesty.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不诚实而丢了工作。
words.en: Dishonesty is the quality or an act of not being honest; it involves lying, cheating, or stealing.

words.tr:
v. 使烦恼；使不安
n. 不安；忧虑；烦恼
words.ex: The loud noise disquieted her.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让她感到烦恼。
words.en: Disquiet is a feeling of worry or anxiety.

words.ex: He spoke with fervor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Fervor is intense and passionate feeling.

words.ex: His fidelity to his friend never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: Fidelity is loyalty to a person, organization, or set of beliefs.

words.tr: n. 先见；预见；先见之明
words.ex: He showed foresight by saving money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他通过为未来存钱展现了远见。
words.en: The ability to predict or the action of predicting what will happen or be needed in the future.

words.tr:
n. 狂乱；狂暴；狂怒
v. 使狂乱；使狂怒
words.ex: The crowd went into a frenzy when the singer appeared.
words.ex_cn: 当歌手出现时，人群陷入了狂热。
words.en: A frenzy is a state of uncontrolled excitement or wild behavior.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.ex: He filed a grievance about the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因不公平的对待提出了不满。
words.en: A grievance is a feeling of resentment over something believed to be wrong or unfair.

words.ex: He felt heartache after his dog died.
words.ex_cn: 他的狗去世后，他感到心痛。
words.en: Heartache is a feeling of great sadness or distress.

words.tr:
n. 心碎；强烈的悲痛感
v. 使心碎
words.ex: He felt heartbreak after she left him.
words.ex_cn: 她离开他后，他感到心碎。
words.en: Heartbreak is intense sorrow or grief, especially caused by the loss of someone or something loved.

words.ex: The crowd fell into hysteria when the fire alarm sounded.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了情绪失控。
words.en: Hysteria is a state of extreme excitement, fear, or anger in which people cannot control their emotions or behavior.

words.ex: He accepted the job because of the financial inducement.
words.ex_cn: 他因为经济诱因接受了这份工作。
words.en: Something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.tr: n. 忘恩负义; 得鱼忘荃
words.ex: Her ingratitude after all he'd done for her was painful.
words.ex_cn: 他为她所做的一切换来的却是她的忘恩负义，这让他感到痛苦。
words.en: Lack of gratitude or appreciation.

words.ex: The medicine helps reduce inhibition of the immune system.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于抑制免疫系统的抑制。
words.en: Inhibition is a feeling that makes one self-conscious and unable to act in a relaxed and natural way.

words.tr: n. 学习；学问； v. 学习；“learn”的现在分词；
words.ex: Learning takes time and practice.
words.ex_cn: 学习需要时间和练习。
words.en: The acquisition of knowledge or skills through study, experience, or being taught.

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.ex: He had an outburst when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时大发雷霆。
words.en: An outburst is a sudden release of strong emotion, often in a way that is unexpected or uncontrolled.

words.ex: The math problem caused perplexity in the class.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题让全班都感到困惑。
words.en: A state of confusion or uncertainty.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；姿态；镇静
v. 使平衡；保持（某种姿势）
words.ex: The dancer maintained her poise on one foot.
words.ex_cn: 舞者单脚保持平衡。
words.en: If someone has poise, they are calm, dignified, and self-controlled.

words.ex: His smile gave me reassurance.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑让我安心。
words.en: If someone needs reassurance, they are very worried and need someone to help them stop worrying by saying kind or helpful things.

words.ex: The bridge collapsed due to resonance from the wind.
words.ex_cn: 桥梁因风引起的共振而坍塌。
words.en: Resonance is the quality in a sound of being deep, full, and reverberating.

words.tr:
adj. 尖叫的
n. 尖叫声
v. 尖叫；呐喊；“scream”的现在分词
words.ex: The audience burst into screaming laughter.
words.ex_cn: 观众爆发出尖叫般的笑声。
words.en: Making a loud, high-pitched cry or sound, typically as an expression of fear, pain, or excitement.

words.ex: The solemnity of the ceremony made everyone quiet.
words.ex_cn: 仪式的庄重让所有人都安静了下来。
words.en: The state or quality of being serious and dignified.

words.ex: His timidity made him afraid to speak in class.
words.ex_cn: 他的胆怯让他不敢在课堂上发言。
words.en: The quality or state of being timid; lack of courage or self-confidence.

words.ex: The entrance to the building is on the left.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的入口在左边。
words.en: An entrance is a way into a place, such as a door or gate. It can also refer to the act of entering a place or the right to enter.

words.ex: The lake at dawn offers perfect tranquility.
words.ex_cn: 黎明时分的湖泊带来完全的宁静。
words.en: A state of peace and quiet.

words.ex: He bought the car on a whim.
words.ex_cn: 他一时兴起买了这辆车。
words.en: A whim is a sudden desire or change of mind, especially one that is unusual or unexplained.

chapters.name: Level 10 名词 艺术•娱乐•出版

words.ex: The pianist is the accompanist for the singer.
words.ex_cn: 这位钢琴家是歌手的伴奏者。
words.en: An accompanist is a musician who plays a part in supporting a singer or another musician, especially by playing the piano.

words.tr:
n. 漫画；讽刺画；滑稽模仿
v. 画成漫画讽刺
words.ex: He drew a caricature of the teacher with big eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅老师大眼睛的漫画。
words.en: A caricature is a drawing or description of someone that exaggerates their appearance or behavior in a humorous or critical way.

words.ex: The pottery on display is his handiwork.
words.ex_cn: 展出的陶器是他的手工品。
words.en: Work done by hand; manual work.

words.tr: n. 现代主义；现代派；现代思想
words.ex: He likes modernism in art and design.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢艺术和设计中的现代主义。
words.en: Modernism is a style or movement in the arts that aims to break with classical and traditional forms.

words.ex: He is a modernist who loves abstract art.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位喜欢抽象艺术的现代主义者。
words.en: A modernist is someone who follows or supports modern ideas, styles, or methods in art, literature, or religion.

words.ex: The singer hit the high octave with ease.
words.ex_cn: 歌手轻松地唱到了高八度音。
words.en: An octave is a series of eight notes in a musical scale, or the interval between the first and last notes of such a series.

words.ex: He drew a flower with pastel.
words.ex_cn: 他用彩色粉笔画了一朵花。
words.en: Pastel can refer to a type of soft, colored chalk used for drawing, or to a drawing made with such chalks. It can also describe colors that are pale and soft.

words.ex: He loves the punk subculture.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢朋克亚文化。
words.en: A subculture is a group of people within a culture that differentiates itself from the parent culture to which it belongs, often maintaining some of its founding principles.

chapters.name: Level 10 名词 学术•宗教

words.ex: She loves the aesthetics of old buildings.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢老建筑的美感。
words.en: Aesthetics is a branch of philosophy dealing with the nature of beauty, art, and taste, and with the creation and appreciation of beauty.

words.ex: The antonym of 'hot' is 'cold'.
words.ex_cn: ‘hot’的反义词是‘cold’。
words.en: An antonym is a word that means the opposite of another word.

words.ex: The library keeps old newspapers in an archive.
words.ex_cn: 图书馆把旧报纸保存在档案馆里。
words.en: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.

words.ex: The baby had a baptism in the church.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿在教堂接受了洗礼。
words.en: Baptism is a Christian sacrament of initiation and adoption, almost invariably with the use of water.

words.ex: He used a cliche to describe the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个陈词滥调来形容日落。
words.en: A cliché is an idea or phrase that has been used so much that it is no longer interesting or effective.

words.tr: n. 开始；毕业典礼；学位授予典礼
words.ex: The commencement of the class was at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程的开始时间是上午9点。
words.en: The commencement of something is its beginning.

words.ex: He sat in contemplation of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他凝视着日落。
words.en: Contemplation is the act of thinking deeply about something.

words.tr: n. 概论；普遍性；一般性；通则
words.ex: The book gives a generality of modern physics.
words.ex_cn: 这本书对现代物理学做了概论。
words.en: A generality is a statement that is very general and not specific, often used when the speaker does not want to give details or when the details are not known.

words.ex: He checked the glossary for the meaning of new words.
words.ex_cn: 他查阅了术语表以了解新词的含义。
words.en: A glossary is a list of terms in a particular domain of knowledge with the definitions for those terms.

words.tr:
n. 殉道者；殉教者；烈士
v. 处死；折磨
words.ex: He became a martyr for freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他为自由而成为烈士。
words.en: A martyr is someone who is killed or made to suffer greatly because of their religious or political beliefs, and is admired and respected by people who share those beliefs.

words.ex: He goes to the mosque every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五去清真寺。
words.en: A mosque is a building where Muslims go to worship.

words.ex: He noticed the nuance in her voice.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了她声音中的细微差别。
words.en: A very slight difference in meaning, sound, color, or someone's feelings that is not usually very obvious.

words.ex: He challenges the orthodoxy of traditional teaching.
words.ex_cn: 他挑战传统教学的正统观念。
words.en: Orthodoxy refers to the quality of conforming to established doctrines or practices, especially in religion.

words.tr: n. 圆括号；插入语；插入成分；附带
words.ex: Put the numbers in parenthesis.
words.ex_cn: 把数字放在圆括号里。
words.en: A word, clause, or sentence inserted as an explanation or afterthought into a passage that is grammatically complete without it, in writing usually marked off by round or square brackets.

words.tr: n. 个性；特性； 精确性；详尽
words.ex: He noted the particularity of her handwriting.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了她笔迹的特殊性。
words.en: The quality of being individual or unique; the state of being particular.

words.tr: n. 朗诵；朗读；背诵；逐个叙述
words.ex: The boy did a recitation of the poem in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在课堂上背诵了这首诗。
words.en: A recitation is the act of saying a piece of poetry or literature that you have learned to an audience.

words.ex: The reviewer checked the paper carefully.
words.ex_cn: 审稿人仔细检查了这篇论文。
words.en: A reviewer is a person who writes reviews, especially of books, films, or music.

words.ex: He wrote the note in shorthand.
words.ex_cn: 他用速记法写了这条笔记。
words.en: A method of rapid writing by means of abbreviations and symbols, used especially for taking dictation.

words.tr: n. 怀疑论者；怀疑宗教主张的人；无神论者
words.ex: He is a skeptic about new health claims.
words.ex_cn: 他对新的健康说法持怀疑态度。
words.en: A skeptic is a person who questions the validity or authenticity of something purporting to be factual.

words.ex: The synthesis of ideas helped solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这些想法的综合帮助解决了问题。
words.en: The act of combining different ideas, influences, or objects into a new and coherent whole.

chapters.name: Level 10 名词 时间

words.ex: The continuance of the drought has caused severe water shortages.
words.ex_cn: 干旱的持续导致了严重的水资源短缺。
words.en: The continuance of something is its continuing existence or presence.

words.ex: The kids are watching the countdown to New Year.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们正在观看新年的倒计时。
words.en: A countdown is the counting aloud of numbers in reverse order before something happens, especially before a spacecraft is launched.

words.tr: n. 中午; adj. 正午（发生或出现）的（同 midday）
words.ex: The noonday sun was scorching.
words.ex_cn: 正午的太阳炙热难耐。
words.en: Noonday refers to the middle of the day; noon.

words.ex: The onset of winter brought heavy snow.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的开始带来了大雪。
words.en: The onset of something is the beginning of it, especially something unpleasant.

words.ex: At the outset, he was unsure about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 在开始时，他对这个计划并不确定。
words.en: The outset of something is the beginning of it.

words.ex: The new law was passed during peacetime.
words.ex_cn: 新法律是在和平时期通过的。
words.en: A period when a country is not at war.

words.ex: He starts his new class in the fall semester.
words.ex_cn: 他在秋季学期开始他的新课程。
words.en: A semester is one of the two periods that the school or college year is divided into, especially in the United States and Canada.

words.tr: n. 摊牌；最后一决胜负；决战
words.ex: The showdown between the two leaders is scheduled for next week.
words.ex_cn: 两位领导人的摊牌定于下周举行。
words.en: A showdown is a decisive confrontation or test of strength or will.

chapters.name: Level 10 名词 自然•植物

words.ex: Ammonia has a strong smell.
words.ex_cn: 氨有一种刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Ammonia is a colorless gas with a characteristic pungent smell. It is used in the manufacture of fertilizers and as a refrigerant.

words.ex: A cascade of complaints flooded the office.
words.ex_cn: 大量投诉涌进了办公室。
words.en: A cascade is a small waterfall or a series of small waterfalls. As a verb, it means to flow or fall in or like a cascade.

words.ex: The fish swim among the coral in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在海中的珊瑚间游动。
words.en: A hard stony substance secreted by certain marine coelenterates as an external skeleton, typically forming large reefs in warm seas.

words.ex: The embryo grows inside the mother's womb.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎在母亲的子宫内生长。
words.en: An embryo is an unborn animal or human being in the very early stages of development.

words.ex: The apple fell because of gravitation.
words.ex_cn: 苹果掉下来是因为重力。
words.en: Gravitation is the force of attraction that exists between any two masses, any two bodies, any two particles. It is the force that pulls objects towards each other.

words.ex: The iceberg is floating in the cold sea.
words.ex_cn: 冰山在寒冷的海面上漂浮。
words.en: An iceberg is a large piece of ice that has broken off from a glacier and is floating in the sea.

words.tr:
n. 紫丁香；淡紫色
adj. 淡紫色的
words.ex: The lilac blooms in spring.
words.ex_cn: 丁香花在春天盛开。
words.en: A lilac is a type of shrub or small tree which has bunches of sweet-smelling pink, white, or purple flowers.

words.ex: Farmers spread manure on the fields to help crops grow.
words.ex_cn: 农民把肥料撒在田里以帮助庄稼生长。
words.en: Manure is organic matter used as fertilizer in agriculture.

words.tr: n. 自然学家；博物学家；
words.ex: The naturalist studied birds in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这位自然学家在森林里研究鸟类。
words.en: A naturalist is a person who studies or is an expert in natural history, especially a zoologist or botanist.

words.ex: The storm caused an upheaval in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A very large change in something that often causes confusion or problems.

words.tr:
n. （葡萄酒）制造年份；
adj. 古老的；
words.ex: This wine is from a vintage of 2015.
words.ex_cn: 这款葡萄酒产自2015年的酿造年份。
words.en: Vintage is used to describe something that is not just old, but is also of high quality and typical of the best of its kind.

chapters.name: Level 10 名词 生活

words.ex: The team has a strong backup for the captain.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍有一位强大的后援来代替队长。
words.en: A backup is a copy of a file or other item of data made in case the original is lost or damaged. It can also refer to support or assistance provided to someone or something.

words.ex: The walls are beige.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁是米黄色的。
words.en: A pale sandy yellowish-brown color.

words.tr:
n. 宾果游戏
int. 太好了！
words.ex: He shouted bingo when he got five in a row.
words.ex_cn: 当他连成五子时，他大喊‘宾果’。
words.en: Bingo is a game in which each player has a card with numbers on it. The caller calls out numbers and if a player has that number on their card they mark it off. The first player to mark off all their numbers calls out 'Bingo!' and wins the game.

words.ex: Pandas and bamboo coexist in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫和竹子在野外共存。
words.en: The state or fact of existing at the same time or in the same place.

words.ex: The team's cohesion helped them win the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队的凝聚力帮助他们赢得了比赛。
words.en: Cohesion refers to the action or fact of forming a united whole, especially in the context of a group of people or the parts of a substance.

words.ex: The file size is reduced by compression.
words.ex_cn: 通过压缩，文件大小被减小了。
words.en: Compression is the act or process of making something smaller or pressing it into a smaller space, or the state of being pressed or squeezed in this way.

words.ex: The two countries reached a concord on trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上达成了一致。
words.en: Concord is a state of agreement or harmony between people or groups.

words.ex: The doctor must keep patient information confidentiality.
words.ex_cn: 医生必须保持病人的信息机密性。
words.en: The state of keeping or being kept secret or private.

words.tr: n. 连接器；连接物；联系者
words.ex: He used a connector to join the two wires.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个连接器把两根电线接在一起。
words.en: A connector is a device or a part of a device that is used to join two pieces of equipment, or a person or thing that connects two other people or things.

words.tr: n. 输送；运输；财产让与；运输工具
words.ex: The conveyance of goods took three days.
words.ex_cn: 货物的运输花了三天时间。
words.en: The act or process of transporting or carrying something from one place to another.

words.ex: He is a man of great eminence in science.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界享有很高的声望。
words.en: Eminence refers to a position of great distinction or superiority, especially in a particular field or profession.

words.ex: He is facing a difficult decision.
words.ex_cn: 他正面对一个艰难的决定。
words.en: Facing can refer to the material that covers the outside of a building or structure, or it can mean to confront or deal with a problem or situation.

words.ex: He joined a fraternity at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学加入了兄弟会。
words.en: Fraternity refers to a group of people sharing a common profession or interests, or a feeling of friendship and mutual support within a group.

words.tr:
n. 家具；设备；配备
v. 布置家具；配备；“furnish”的现在分词
words.ex: The furnishing of the apartment includes a sofa, table, and chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这个公寓的家具包括一张沙发、一张桌子和几把椅子。
words.en: Furnishing refers to the furniture, fixtures, and other movable objects in a building or room that make it suitable for living or working.

words.tr: n. 肥皂泡; 紧张; 激动; （马的）汗沫 vi. （指肥皂）形成泡沫 vt. 用皂沫覆盖; <口
words.ex: The horse was covered in lather after the race.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，马全身都是汗沫。
words.en: Lather is a frothy white mass of bubbles produced by soap or a similar substance when mixed with water.

words.ex: He is the liaison between the two departments.
words.ex_cn: 他是两个部门之间的联络人。
words.en: A liaison is a person who acts as a link to assist communication between different groups or organizations.

words.ex: The magnificence of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的壮丽让每个人都很惊讶。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: The burden became a millstone around his neck.
words.ex_cn: 这个负担成了他脖子上的磨石。
words.en: A millstone is one of two large, circular stones used, especially in the past, to crush grain to make flour. It can also refer to a problem or responsibility that is very difficult to get rid of or deal with.

words.tr:
n. 拙劣的模仿（作品）
v. 拙劣模仿
words.ex: The film is a parody of classic horror movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对经典恐怖电影的滑稽模仿。
words.en: A parody is a humorous or satirical imitation of a serious piece of literature or writing.

words.ex: He left his watch as a pawn at the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他把手表当成了典当品放在店里。
words.en: To pawn something means to leave it with a pawnbroker, who lends you money in exchange. The pawnbroker keeps the item until you pay back the money plus interest.

words.ex: The payoff for working hard is a better life.
words.ex_cn: 努力工作的报酬是更好的生活。
words.en: The benefit or profit gained from something, especially after effort or investment.

words.tr: n. 衬裙；裙子; adj. 女性的
words.ex: She wore a petticoat under her dress.
words.ex_cn: 她在裙子下穿了一条衬裙。
words.en: A petticoat is a piece of clothing like a thin skirt, which is worn under a skirt or dress.

words.ex: He always follows social propriety.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵守社交礼仪。
words.en: Propriety is the quality of being proper, suitable, or appropriate in behavior or conduct.

words.tr: n. 调整器；调节器；监管者
words.ex: The regulator controls the water pressure in the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 这个调整器控制管道中的水压。
words.en: A regulator is a person or organization appointed by a government to regulate an area of activity such as banking or industry.

words.tr: n. 轿子；小轿车；厢式轿车
words.ex: The man rode in a sedan carried by two servants.
words.ex_cn: 这个人坐在两个仆人抬的轿子里。
words.en: A sedan is a type of car that has a closed body and a separate trunk, typically seating four or more people.

words.tr: n. 挑选者；选拔者；选择器
words.ex: The selector can filter items based on specific criteria.
words.ex_cn: 选择器可以根据特定标准筛选项目。
words.en: A selector is someone who chooses or selects, especially someone whose job is to choose people or things for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 外观；样子；相似；表象
words.ex: She tried to maintain a semblance of normality.
words.ex_cn: 她试图维持一种正常的假象。
words.en: The outward appearance or apparent form of something, especially when the reality is different.

words.ex: The old shipwreck lies at the bottom of the sea.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船的残骸躺在海底。
words.en: A shipwreck is the destruction of a ship at sea by sinking or breaking up, for example in a storm or after hitting a rock.

words.ex: We had a stopover in Dubai on our way to Sydney.
words.ex_cn: 我们在飞往悉尼的途中在迪拜中途停留。
words.en: A stopover is a short stay in a place in between parts of a journey, especially a long journey.

words.ex: The strike caused a stoppage of the train service.
words.ex_cn: 罢工导致了列车服务的停止。
words.en: A stoppage is an instance of stopping or the state of being stopped, especially in a work context.

words.ex: The company made a subdivision of its market by age.
words.ex_cn: 公司按年龄对市场进行了细分。
words.en: A subdivision is a part or section of something which is itself divided into parts.

words.ex: Click the tab to open the new page.
words.ex_cn: 点击标签以打开新页面。
words.en: A tab is a small piece of material that sticks out from something, used for opening, closing, or identifying it. In computing, a tab is a key on a keyboard that moves the cursor a set number of spaces or to a specific position. In a restaurant or bar, a tab is a bill for food or drinks that is kept and paid for later.

words.tr:
v. （使）纠缠；使陷入；使混乱
n. 纠缠；混乱；纠纷
words.ex: The cat got into a tangle with the yarn.
words.ex_cn: 猫和毛线缠在一起了。
words.en: If something is tangled or tangles, it becomes twisted together in an untidy way.

words.ex: She tinted the glass blue.
words.ex_cn: 她把玻璃染成了蓝色。
words.en: A tint is a small amount of a particular color, especially when it is used to make the main color lighter or darker.

chapters.name: Level 10 名词 政治•经济•法律

words.ex: He supports advocacy for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他支持清洁用水的倡导。
words.en: The act of pleading or arguing in favor of something, such as a cause, idea, or policy; active support.

words.ex: The local company is an affiliate of the big global brand.
words.ex_cn: 这家本地公司是这个全球大品牌的分公司。
words.en: If an organization is affiliated with another larger organization, it is officially connected with the larger organization or is a member of it.

words.ex: The club has an affiliation with the university.
words.ex_cn: 这个俱乐部与大学有从属关系。
words.en: An affiliation is a close connection or association with a particular group, organization, or institution.

words.ex: His family's affluence allowed him to travel the world.
words.ex_cn: 他家的富裕让他能环游世界。
words.en: Affluence is the state of having a lot of money or owning many things.

words.tr: n. 拨用；拨款；挪用；占有
words.ex: The government made an appropriation for education.
words.ex_cn: 政府为教育拨款。
words.en: The act of setting something aside for a specific purpose, especially funds.

words.ex: He believes education is his birthright.
words.ex_cn: 他认为教育是他的天赋权利。
words.en: A birthright is a right, privilege, or possession that a person has from birth, especially as a descendant of a particular family or social class.

words.tr: n. 借用的言语（或思想等）； v. 借；借用；“borrow”的现在分词；
words.ex: His poem shows a lot of borrowing from old folk tales.
words.ex_cn: 他的诗大量借用民间故事的言语。
words.en: The act of taking and using something that belongs to someone else with the intention of returning it.

words.tr:
n. 中产阶级的人；资产阶级的人
adj. 中产阶级的；追求名利的；资产阶级的
words.ex: He lives a bourgeois life with a big house and a car.
words.ex_cn: 他过着资产阶级的生活，有一栋大房子和一辆车。
words.en: If you describe people, their way of life, or their attitudes as bourgeois, you are criticizing them for caring too much about money and possessions and for being too conventional.

words.ex: The company wants centralization for better control.
words.ex_cn: 公司希望集中管理以更好地控制。
words.en: The process or policy of concentrating control of an organization or activity under a single authority.

words.ex: The rain and the thunder happened in conjunction.
words.ex_cn: 雨和雷声同时发生。
words.en: A conjunction is a word that is used to connect clauses or sentences or to coordinate words in the same clause.

words.ex: The default setting is on.
words.ex_cn: 默认设置是开启的。
words.en: If a person, company, or country defaults on something that they have legally agreed to do, such as paying a debt or keeping to an agreement, they fail to do it.

words.ex: The heavy fine is a deterrent to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款是一种威慑作弊的力量。
words.en: Something that discourages or is intended to discourage someone from doing something.

words.tr: n. 支配；领土；统治（权）；管辖
words.ex: The king had dominion over the land.
words.ex_cn: 国王对这片土地拥有统治权。
words.en: Dominion refers to the power or right of governing and controlling; it can also denote a territory or sphere of influence.

words.tr:
n. 禁止贸易令；禁运
v. 禁止…的贸易；禁运
words.ex: The country placed an embargo on imported goods.
words.ex_cn: 该国对进口商品实施了禁运。
words.en: An embargo is an official order to stop trade with another country.

words.tr: n. 使节；特使；外交使节；
words.ex: The envoy met the president to discuss peace.
words.ex_cn: 使节会见了总统以讨论和平事宜。
words.en: An envoy is a representative sent by one government or leader to another, especially in order to carry out a particular task or to negotiate.

words.ex: There was a large influx of tourists during the summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天期间涌入了大量游客。
words.en: An influx of people or things is a large number of them arriving somewhere at the same time.

words.ex: The police did an interrogation at night.
words.ex_cn: 警察在晚上进行了审问。
words.en: The process of asking someone a lot of questions in order to get information, especially in a police or military context.

words.ex: The teacher was fired for misconduct.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师因行为不端被解雇了。
words.en: Misconduct refers to unacceptable or improper behavior, especially by a professional person.

words.ex: The government declared a moratorium on new construction.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布暂停新的建筑项目。
words.en: A moratorium is a temporary prohibition of an activity.

words.tr: n. 强烈的抗议（或反对）
words.ex: There was an outcry when the school closed the library.
words.ex_cn: 当学校关闭图书馆时，引起了强烈的抗议。
words.en: An outcry is a reaction of strong disapproval and anger shown by the public or by a group of people, often in the form of protests or complaints.

words.tr:
adj. 偏袒的；党派性的
n. 强烈支持者；党羽；游击队员
words.ex: He gave a partisan answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了偏袒的回答。
words.en: A partisan is a strong supporter of a party, cause, or person. It can also refer to a member of an armed group formed to fight secretly against an occupying force.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.tr: n. 代理人；代表；代理权；代理服务器
words.ex: He gave his friend a proxy to vote for him.
words.ex_cn: 他让朋友当他的代理人替他投票。
words.en: A proxy is a person or thing that is authorized to act on behalf of another, especially in voting or representing someone in a meeting.

words.ex: The old building had a rebirth as a museum.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧建筑作为博物馆获得了新生。
words.en: Rebirth is the process of being born again, or a period of new growth or revival in something.

words.ex: He sent a remittance to his family last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周给家人汇了一笔款。
words.en: A remittance is a sum of money that you send to someone.

words.ex: The retrieval of lost files took a long time.
words.ex_cn: 找回丢失文件花费了很长时间。
words.en: The act of getting something back from somewhere.

words.ex: Children learn socialization through playing with others.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们通过与其他孩子玩耍来学习社交。
words.en: The process by which individuals learn and adopt the behaviors and norms of their society or group.

words.ex: The workers showed solidarity during the strike.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在罢工期间表现出团结。
words.en: Solidarity is unity or agreement of feeling or action, especially among individuals with a common interest; mutual support within a group.

words.ex: The speculator bought gold hoping it would rise in price.
words.ex_cn: 这位投机者购买了黄金，希望它的价格会上涨。
words.en: A speculator is someone who buys goods, property, money, etc. in the hope of selling them at a profit.

words.tr: n. 统一派；工会主义者
words.ex: The unionist supports keeping the country united.
words.ex_cn: 统一派支持保持国家统一。
words.en: A unionist is a person who supports or belongs to a trade union, or someone who supports the union of different groups or countries.

words.ex: This food contains a harmless additive for flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物含有用于调味的无害添加物。
words.en: An additive is a substance which is added in small amounts to something else in order to improve it, preserve it, or make it more effective.

words.ex: He drank a glass of ale at the pub.
words.ex_cn: 他在酒吧喝了一杯麦芽酒。
words.en: Ale is a type of beer that is brewed using a warm fermentation method, resulting in a sweet, full-bodied and fruity taste.

words.ex: Bread and rice are rich in carbohydrate.
words.ex_cn: 面包和米饭富含碳水化合物。
words.en: A carbohydrate is a substance found in foods such as bread, potatoes, and rice which provides your body with heat and energy and which consists of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

words.tr:
n. 滴落；油滴
v. 滴落；“drip”的现在分词
adj. 湿淋淋的
words.ex: The dripping from the faucet woke me up.
words.ex_cn: 水龙头的滴落声把我吵醒了。
words.en: The act or sound of liquid falling in drops.

words.ex: He is fixing his bicycle.
words.ex_cn: 他正在修理他的自行车。
words.en: The act of making something firm, stable, or stationary; the process of repairing or installing something.

words.ex: He drinks gin with ice.
words.ex_cn: 他喝加冰的杜松子酒。
words.en: A clear strong alcoholic drink flavoured with juniper berries.

words.ex: He drank a glass of malt.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一杯麦芽饮料。
words.en: Malt is grain, usually barley, that has been soaked in water, allowed to germinate, and then dried. It is used in brewing and distilling.

words.ex: He eats oatmeal for breakfast every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃燕麦片当早餐。
words.en: Oatmeal is a type of coarse flour made of hulled oat grains that have either been milled or steel-cut. Ground oats are also called white oats. Steel-cut oats are known as coarse oatmeal, Irish oatmeal, or pinhead oats.

words.tr:
n. 定量；配给量
v. 配给；定量供应
words.ex: He gets a small ration of food each day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天得到少量的食物配给。
words.en: A ration is a fixed amount of something such as food or fuel that is officially allowed to each person, especially when there is not enough of it available.

words.tr: n. 食物；营养；维持生计
words.ex: Water and food are basic sustenance for life.
words.ex_cn: 水和食物是生命的基本生存物资。
words.en: Sustenance refers to the food and drink that people, animals, and plants need to live and stay healthy. It can also mean the means of maintaining life or supporting existence.

chapters.name: Level 10 名词 程度•单位

words.ex: Each family was given an allotment of land to farm.
words.ex_cn: 每个家庭都被分配了一块土地来耕种。
words.en: An allotment is a share or portion of something that has been divided or distributed.

words.tr:
n. 膨胀；凸出部分；暴涨
v. 膨胀；凸出；急增
words.ex: The balloon begins to bulge when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充气时开始鼓起来。
words.en: If something bulges, it sticks out or swells in a rounded shape.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.ex: The team's victory brought a wave of exaltation.
words.ex_cn: 团队的胜利带来了一阵欣喜。
words.en: Exaltation is a feeling or state of extreme happiness or elation, often as a result of a success or achievement.

words.ex: He has high expectancy for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他对未来有很高的预期。
words.en: The feeling of excitement about something that is going to happen.

words.tr: n. 美好；纯度；细微；优雅
words.ex: The fineness of her smile made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的美好让每个人都感到开心。
words.en: The quality of being fine, in particular the quality of a metal or gemstone that is free from impurities.

words.ex: The book has a gloss at the bottom of each page.
words.ex_cn: 这本书每页底部都有注释。
words.en: A gloss is a bright shine on the surface of something. It can also refer to a superficial appearance or interpretation that conceals the true nature of something.

words.ex: The stars seem to go on to infinity.
words.ex_cn: 星星似乎延伸到无限。
words.en: Infinity is a concept of something that is unlimited, endless, without bound.

words.ex: The teacher changed the parameter to make the test easier.
words.ex_cn: 老师更改了参数，使测试更容易。
words.en: A parameter is a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity.

words.ex: He chewed a quid of tobacco after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后咀嚼了一小块烟草。
words.en: A quid is a British slang term for one pound sterling. It can also refer to something that is chewed, such as tobacco.

words.ex: Einstein developed the theory of relativity.
words.ex_cn: 爱因斯坦提出了相对论。
words.en: The theory of relativity, developed by Albert Einstein, fundamentally altered our understanding of space, time, and gravity.

words.ex: This apple is a variant of the red delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这种苹果是红富士的一个变体。
words.en: A variant is something that is slightly different from other similar things.

chapters.name: Level 10 名词 场所•位置

words.ex: The concealment of the truth made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 对真相的隐藏让每个人都生气了。
words.en: The action of hiding something or the state of being hidden.

words.ex: The old building has a beautiful facade with stone pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老建筑有一个带有石柱的漂亮正面。
words.en: The front of a building, especially an imposing or decorative one. Also, a superficial appearance or illusion of something.

words.ex: The diamond has many smooth facets.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石有许多光滑的小平面。
words.en: A particular aspect or feature of something.

words.ex: The nail fits into the groove.
words.ex_cn: 钉子卡在槽里。
words.en: A groove is a long, narrow space or cut in a surface, often made to guide the movement of something or to hold something in place. It can also refer to a settled routine or way of doing things that is hard to change.

words.tr: n. 内地；中部地方; adj. 中部的；在内陆的
words.ex: He lives in a small town in the midland.
words.ex_cn: 他住在中部的一个小镇上。
words.en: The term 'midland' refers to the central part of a country or region, often characterized by its geographical location away from the coast.

words.tr: n. 商机；理想的工作或生活；
words.ex: He found a niche in selling eco-friendly phone cases.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售环保手机壳方面找到了商机。
words.en: A niche is a hollow area in a wall which has been made to hold a statue, or a comfortable or suitable position in life or employment.

words.tr:
n. V字形刻痕；等级；切口
v. 赢得；刻凹痕
words.ex: He made a notch on the stick to count days.
words.ex_cn: 他在木棍上刻了一个刻痕来计数天数。
words.en: A notch is a small cut or indentation in a surface. It can also refer to a level or degree in a scale or a narrow pass between mountains.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.ex: The workers load stones from the quarry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们从采石场装载石头。
words.en: A quarry is a place where stone, sand, etc., is dug out of the ground. It can also refer to an animal or person that is being hunted or chased.

words.tr: n. 仓库；贮藏室；存放处；智囊
words.ex: He saves his code in a GitHub repository.
words.ex_cn: 他把代码保存在 GitHub 仓库中。
words.en: A repository is a place where something is stored or can be found.

words.ex: There is a small rift in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: A rift is a major fault or break in the Earth's crust.

words.tr:
n. 寿衣；裹尸布；覆盖物
v. 覆盖；遮蔽
words.ex: The body was wrapped in a white shroud.
words.ex_cn: 遗体被裹在一件白色的寿衣里。
words.en: A shroud is a cloth which is used for wrapping a dead body. It can also refer to something that covers, hides, or protects.

words.ex: The train stops at the terminus.
words.ex_cn: 火车在终点站停下。
words.en: A terminus is the end of a transportation line or the station at the end of a railway or bus route.

words.ex: The underside of the table is dirty.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的下侧很脏。
words.en: The underside of something is the part of it which normally faces towards the ground or is not normally seen.

words.ex: The upside of working late is more money.
words.ex_cn: 加班的好处是能赚更多钱。
words.en: The upside is the more positive aspect of a situation that is generally bad.

words.ex: The hikers enjoyed a beautiful vista from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者们从山顶欣赏到了美丽的景色。
words.en: A vista is a pleasing view, especially one seen through a long, narrow opening.

words.tr:
n. 拥护者；信徒
adj. 黏附…的
words.ex: He is an adherent of the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 他是这项新政策的拥护者。
words.en: An adherent is someone who supports a particular party, person, or set of ideas.

words.tr: n. 主席；主持人；董事长；
words.ex: The chairman called the meeting to order.
words.ex_cn: 主席宣布会议开始。
words.en: A chairman is a man who is in charge of a meeting, committee, or organization.

words.tr: n. 对手；对立者；对抗者
words.ex: The antagonist in the story is a greedy king.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的反派是一个贪婪的国王。
words.en: An antagonist is someone who opposes another person.

words.ex: That bloke is waiting for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 那个家伙正在等公交车。
words.en: A bloke is a man, especially an ordinary man.

words.tr:
n. 球童
v. 当球童
words.ex: He hired a caddie to carry his golf clubs.
words.ex_cn: 他雇了一个球童来帮他拿高尔夫球杆。
words.en: A caddie is a person who carries a golfer's clubs and provides other assistance during a game of golf.

words.ex: The courier delivered the letter quickly.
words.ex_cn: 信使迅速送来了这封信。
words.en: A courier is a person or company that delivers messages, packages, and mail.

words.tr: n. 管理人；保管人；监护人
words.ex: The custodian takes care of the school building.
words.ex_cn: 管理人负责照顾学校大楼。
words.en: A custodian is someone who is responsible for looking after or protecting something valuable or important.

words.ex: The head-teacher speaks to the students every morning.
words.ex_cn: 校长每天早上对学生讲话。
words.en: The principal teacher in a school, responsible for its management and administration.

words.ex: My mentor helped me choose my career path.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮助我选择了职业道路。
words.en: A mentor is a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school.

words.ex: The midwife helped the baby come out safely.
words.ex_cn: 助产士帮助婴儿安全出生。
words.en: A midwife is a person, usually a woman, who is trained to help women during childbirth.

words.ex: I bought a newspaper from the newsagent.
words.ex_cn: 我从报刊亭买了一份报纸。
words.en: A newsagent is a person or shop that sells newspapers and magazines.

words.tr: n. 被排斥者；被抛弃者；
words.ex: He became an outcast after speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因为说出真相而被排斥。
words.en: An outcast is someone who is not accepted by a group of people or by society.

words.tr:
n. 侏儒；俾格米人
adj. 矮小的
words.ex: The pygmy lived in a small hut in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这个侏儒住在森林里的一间小屋里。
words.en: A pygmy is a member of a group of very small people who live in Africa.

words.tr:
n. 替罪羊；代人受过者
v. 使…成为替罪羊
words.ex: He was made the scapegoat for the company's financial failures.
words.ex_cn: 他被当作公司财务失败的替罪羊。
words.en: A scapegoat is a person who is blamed for something that someone else has done.

words.ex: He got the promotion because of his seniority.
words.ex_cn: 他因为资历深而获得了晋升。
words.en: Seniority is the state of being older or higher in rank than someone else.

words.tr: n. 求婚者；起诉者；有意收购另一公司的机构
words.ex: He is a suitor who brings flowers every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天送花的追求者。
words.en: A suitor is a man who wants to marry a particular woman.

words.tr: n. 不幸的人；潦倒的人；恶棍；坏蛋
words.ex: The poor wretch had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 那个可怜的人没有食物和住所。
words.en: A wretch is someone who is extremely unhappy or unfortunate, or someone who behaves in a way that is morally bad.

chapters.name: Level 10 名词 物品

words.tr: n. 加速器；油门；促进剂
words.ex: He pressed the accelerator to speed up the car.
words.ex_cn: 他踩下油门让车加速。
words.en: An accelerator is a device in a vehicle that you press with your foot to make the vehicle go faster.

words.ex: She wore a necklace made of amber.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一条琥珀制成的项链。
words.en: Amber is a hard, translucent, yellowish-brown substance that is used for making jewelry or other objects. It is formed from the resin of ancient trees.

words.tr:
n. 凿子
v. 雕；凿；欺骗
words.ex: He used a chisel to carve the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他用凿子雕刻石头。
words.en: A chisel is a tool with a long metal blade which has a sharp edge for cutting wood, stone, or metal.

words.tr:
v. 剧烈搅动；（使）猛烈翻腾
n. 搅乳器
words.ex: The machine churns the butter in the cream.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器剧烈搅动奶油来制作黄油。
words.en: To churn means to stir or shake milk or cream in order to make butter, or to move something around violently in water or air.

words.ex: She hung the shirt on the line with a clothespin.
words.ex_cn: 她用夹子把衬衫挂在绳子上。
words.en: A clothespin is a small device used to fasten clothes onto a clothesline.

words.tr:
n. 曲柄；怪人；脾气坏的人
v. 用曲柄转动
adj. 古怪的；易怒的
words.ex: He turns the crank to start the old engine.
words.ex_cn: 他转动曲柄来启动旧引擎。
words.en: A crank is a device for transmitting rotary motion, consisting of a handle or arm attached at right angles to a shaft. It can also refer to a person who holds unorthodox opinions or behaves in an eccentric manner.

words.tr:
n. 饲料槽；有栏小卧床
v. 抄袭
words.ex: The horse eats hay from the crib.
words.ex_cn: 马从饲料槽里吃干草。
words.en: A crib is a bed with high sides for a baby or very young child. It can also mean to copy someone else's work and present it as your own.

words.ex: The cheese is a derivative of milk.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪是牛奶的派生物。
words.en: A derivative is something which has been developed or obtained from something else.

words.tr: n. 探测器；检测器；发现者；
words.ex: The detector found a hidden metal object.
words.ex_cn: 探测器发现了一个隐藏的金属物体。
words.en: A detector is a device that is used to discover the presence of something, such as smoke, metal, or radiation.

words.ex: The truck runs on diesel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车使用柴油运行。
words.en: Diesel is a type of heavy oil used as fuel in diesel engines.

words.ex: He was dropping his keys on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他正在把钥匙掉在地板上。
words.en: The act of falling or being allowed to fall vertically; the act of delivering something by parachute.

words.ex: Ancient people used flint to make fire.
words.ex_cn: 古人用燧石生火。
words.en: Flint is a very hard greyish-black stone that was used in former times for making tools and weapons, and for starting fires.

words.ex: The new flooring in the kitchen is made of wood.
words.ex_cn: 厨房的新地板是木制的。
words.en: Flooring refers to the material used to cover the floor of a room, such as wood, carpet, or tiles.

words.tr: n. 衣饰上的绉边；褶皱
words.ex: The dress has a white frill at the bottom.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子的底部有一圈白色花边。
words.en: A frill is a strip of cloth with many folds in it, which is attached to something as a decoration.

words.tr: v. 由于保险丝烧断而电路不通；熔接；结合；
words.ex: The light went out because the fuse blew.
words.ex_cn: 灯灭了，因为保险丝烧断了。
words.en: A fuse is a safety device consisting of a strip of wire that melts and breaks an electric circuit if the current exceeds a safe level. As a verb, it means to join or blend to form a single entity.

words.ex: He took the helm of the company after the CEO retired.
words.ex_cn: CEO退休后，他成为了公司的领导人。
words.en: The helm is the wheel or control which is used to steer a ship or boat.

words.ex: The company uses a mainframe to store large amounts of data.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司使用大型机来存储大量数据。
words.en: A mainframe is a large, powerful computer that can handle the processing needs of large organizations and is capable of supporting many users simultaneously.

words.tr: n. 臼；研钵；灰浆；迫击炮
words.ex: The chef used a mortar to grind the spices.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用臼来研磨香料。
words.en: Mortar is a mixture of sand, water, and cement or lime that is used to hold bricks or stones together. It is also a type of gun that fires explosive shells at a high angle.

words.ex: The neutron has no electric charge.
words.ex_cn: 中子不带电荷。
words.en: A neutron is a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of every atom except that of simple hydrogen. It has no electric charge and a mass slightly greater than that of a proton.

words.tr: n. 玩物，供消遣的东西; <正>玩具
words.ex: She treated him like a plaything.
words.ex_cn: 她把他当作玩物。
words.en: A plaything is an object that a child plays with, such as a toy, or someone who is treated as if they have no feelings and is used for someone else's amusement.

words.ex: The children played on the rubble after the building fell.
words.ex_cn: 建筑物倒塌后，孩子们在碎石上玩耍。
words.en: Rubble is the broken pieces of stone, brick, etc., that are left when a building falls down or is destroyed.

words.ex: The child drew a semicircle on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在纸上画了一个半圆。
words.en: A semicircle is half of a circle, or something that has the shape of half a circle.

words.tr:
n. 假象；假冒者；冒牌货
adj. 虚假的
v. 假装
words.ex: The gift was a sham, not real.
words.ex_cn: 这份礼物是假的，不是真的。
words.en: A sham is something that is not what it appears to be and is intended to deceive people.

words.tr:
n. 碎片；细条；少量
v. 撕碎；切碎
words.ex: The dog found a shred of paper in the yard.
words.ex_cn: 狗在院子里找到一片纸屑。
words.en: A shred is a very small amount of something, especially a very small piece of paper or cloth. When you shred something, you cut it or tear it into very small pieces.

words.ex: The roof is made of slate.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶是由板岩制成的。
words.en: A slate is a fine-grained, foliated, homogeneous metamorphic rock derived from an original shale-type sedimentary rock composed of clay or volcanic ash through low-grade regional metamorphism. It is the finest grained foliated metamorphic rock. Foliation may not correspond to the original sedimentary layering, but instead is in planes perpendicular to the direction of metamorphic compression.

words.tr:
n. 喷口；水管；水柱
v. 喷出；滔滔不绝地说
words.ex: The kettle has a small spout for pouring water.
words.ex_cn: 这个水壶有一个小喷口用来倒水。
words.en: If something spouts liquid or fire, or if liquid or fire spout out of something, it comes out very quickly with a lot of force.

words.tr:
n. 烟蒂；铅笔头； 残根；票根
v. 碰到某物；捻灭（香烟）
words.ex: He picked up a stub from the ground.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起一个烟蒂。
words.en: A stub is a short piece of something that remains after the rest of it has been used or removed, such as a cigarette stub or a ticket stub.

words.ex: The volcano released sulfur into the air.
words.ex_cn: 火山向空气中释放了硫。
words.en: Sulfur is a pale yellow, odorless, brittle solid, which is insoluble in water but soluble in carbon disulfide.

words.tr: n. 晶体管；晶体管收音机
words.ex: The radio uses a small transistor.
words.ex_cn: 这个收音机使用了一个小晶体管。
words.en: A transistor is a semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electronic signals and electrical power.

words.tr:
n. 配料；装饰品；额外的事物；修剪下来的东西
v. 修剪；装饰；“trim”的现在分词
words.ex: The recipe needs more trimming for flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这个食谱需要更多的配料来提升味道。
words.en: The act of cutting away parts to make something neat or of the desired size; also refers to decorative additions or reductions.

words.tr:
n. 清漆；漆面；光泽面
v. 给…涂上清漆
words.ex: He put varnish on the wooden table.
words.ex_cn: 他在木桌上涂了清漆。
words.en: Varnish is a transparent, hard, protective finish or film primarily used in wood finishing but also for other materials. Varnish is traditionally a combination of a drying oil, a resin, and a thinner or solvent.

words.ex: The bank keeps money in a vault.
words.ex_cn: 银行把钱存放在金库里。
words.en: A vault is an arched structure that forms a ceiling or roof, or a room, especially in a church, that has an arched ceiling or roof. It can also refer to a jump over something using your hands or a pole to push yourself off the ground.

words.tr:
n. 楔子；三角木；楔形物
v. 把…楔住 ；将…挤入（或塞进、插入）
words.ex: He used a wedge to split the wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用楔子把木头劈开。
words.en: A wedge is a piece of wood, metal, or other material with one thick end and one thin edge, used to keep something in position or to split something apart.

words.tr:
n. 假发
v. 痛骂；严责；给…装假发
words.ex: She wore a wig to cover her bald head.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一顶假发来遮盖她光秃的头。
words.en: A wig is a covering of false hair which you wear on your head, for example because you are bald or because you want to cover up your own hair.

chapters.name: Level 10 形容词 位置关系•相对关系

words.tr: adj. 分割的；部门的；分区的
words.ex: The company has three divisional offices.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有三个分公司。
words.en: Relating to or constituting a division or divisions.

words.ex: He has a dual role as teacher and coach.
words.ex_cn: 他同时担任老师和教练的双重角色。
words.en: Having two parts or aspects.

words.tr: adj. 抬高的；地位高的； v. “elevate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The walkway is elevated above the road.
words.ex_cn: 这条人行道被抬高在道路之上。
words.en: An elevated place or thing is higher than the area around it.

words.tr:
adj. 最重要的；
adv. 首要地；
words.ex: He is the foremost expert in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的专家。
words.en: Most important or prominent; leading.

words.tr: adj. 不动的；固定的；不改变的
words.ex: The statue stood immovable, as if carved from stone.
words.ex_cn: 雕像屹立不动，仿佛是用石头雕刻而成。
words.en: If you describe something as immovable, you mean that it cannot be moved from its place or position.

words.tr: adj. 互相依赖的；相倚的；
words.ex: The two countries are interdependent in trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上互相依赖。
words.en: If two or more things are interdependent, they depend on each other.

words.ex: He acted as an intermediary between the two sides.
words.ex_cn: 他充当了双方之间的中间人。
words.en: An intermediary is a person who acts as a link between people or groups in order to try to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.tr: adj. 父亲的；父亲般的；父系的
words.ex: His paternal grandfather gave him a watch.
words.ex_cn: 他的父亲的父亲送给他一块表。
words.en: Paternal is used to describe feelings or actions which are typical of those of a kind father towards his child.

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.tr:
adj. 成比例的；相应的；相称的
v. 使成比例；使适应
words.ex: The punishment should be proportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚应当与罪行相称。
words.en: If one thing is proportionate to another, it increases or decreases according to the changes in the other thing, and there is a sensible relationship between them.

words.ex: This book is relational to math.
words.ex_cn: 这本书与数学有关。
words.en: Relational means concerning the way in which two or more people or things are connected.

words.tr: adj. 信任的；信赖的；依靠的
words.ex: He is reliant on his friend for help.
words.ex_cn: 他信任朋友来帮助他。
words.en: A person or thing that is reliant on someone or something else depends on them for support or help.

words.ex: The change is reversible under normal conditions.
words.ex_cn: 在正常条件下，这种变化是可逆的。
words.en: Capable of being reversed; able to return to an original state or condition.

words.ex: The rotary switch turns on the light.
words.ex_cn: 旋转开关打开灯。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by rotation.

words.ex: The butterfly is symmetrical.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶是对称的。
words.en: Something that is symmetrical has parts that are equal in size, shape, and position, and that are arranged in a balanced way.

chapters.name: Level 10 形容词 学术•文化•宗教

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.ex: He uses colloquial words when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时使用口语化的词语。
words.en: Colloquial language is informal language that is used in ordinary conversation rather than in writing or formal speech.

words.ex: The difference is discernible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个差异肉眼可见。
words.en: able to be discerned; perceptible

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.ex: His poem explores existential questions about life.
words.ex_cn: 他的诗歌探讨了有关存在的生命问题。
words.en: Relating to existence, especially human existence as viewed in the theories of existentialism.

words.tr: adj. 比喻的；象征的；写实的
words.ex: He used figurative language to describe his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他用了比喻性的语言来描述他的感受。
words.en: If you use a word or expression in a figurative sense, you use it with a more abstract or imaginative meaning than its ordinary literal one.

words.ex: He drew a geometric shape on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了一个几何图形。
words.en: Relating to geometry, or according to its methods and principles.

words.ex: The detective gave an investigative report.
words.ex_cn: 侦探提交了一份调查报告。
words.en: Involving or relating to the investigation of something, especially in a thorough and systematic way.

words.ex: He is methodical in organizing his work.
words.ex_cn: 他在安排工作时很有条理。
words.en: If you describe someone as methodical, you mean that they do things carefully, thoroughly, and in order.

words.ex: The bacteria are microscopic.
words.ex_cn: 这些细菌极小。
words.en: So small as to be visible only with a microscope; of or relating to a microscope.

words.tr: adj. 分子的；分子构成的；
words.ex: Water is a molecular compound.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种分子化合物。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of molecules.

words.ex: The project was a monumental task.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目是一项巨大的任务。
words.en: If you describe something as monumental, you are emphasizing that it is very large and impressive, or that it is of great importance or significance.

words.tr:
adj. 神秘的；神秘主义的
n. 神秘主义者
words.ex: He saw a mystic light in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里看到一道神秘的光。
words.en: A mystic is a person who seeks by contemplation and self-surrender to obtain unity with or absorption into the Deity or the absolute, or who believes in the spiritual apprehension of truths that are beyond the intellect.

words.ex: The dragon is a mythical creature.
words.ex_cn: 龙是一种神话中的生物。
words.en: Something that is mythical exists only in myths and is therefore imaginary.

words.tr:
adj. 超自然的；神秘的；隐藏的
v. 掩蔽
n. 神秘的事物；神秘学
words.ex: He is interested in the occult.
words.ex_cn: 他对神秘学感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to mystical, supernatural, or magical powers, practices, or phenomena.

words.tr: adj. 谚语的；众所周知的；已成话柄的
words.ex: It's a proverbial saying that early to bed makes you healthy.
words.ex_cn: 早睡早起是一个谚语，说这样会让你健康。
words.en: Something that is proverbial is well-known by a lot of people, often because it is a typical example of something.

words.tr: adj. 反应的；回应的；活性的；能起化学反应的
words.ex: The metal is reactive with water.
words.ex_cn: 这种金属与水会发生反应。
words.en: Reacting to events or situations rather than creating or controlling them.

words.tr: adj. 本质上的；实质性的；
words.ex: The change was substantive, not just cosmetic.
words.ex_cn: 这个改变是本质上的，而不仅仅是表面上的。
words.en: Something that is substantive is significant, meaningful, or important in a way that is not just superficial or formal.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

chapters.name: Level 10 形容词 身体•健康

words.tr:
adj. 健壮的；硬朗的
v. 强拉硬拖
words.ex: He is still hale at age 80.
words.ex_cn: 他80岁了依然身体健康。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially an old person, as hale, you mean that they are healthy.

words.ex: Smoking is injurious to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is injurious causes harm or damage.

words.tr: adj. 恶毒的；恶性的；恶意的
words.ex: His malignant words hurt everyone around him.
words.ex_cn: 他恶毒的话语伤害了周围的所有人。
words.en: If you say that someone is malignant, you mean they are very dangerous and cause harm to people.

words.tr:
adj. 神经（官能）症的；神经质的；神经过敏的
n. 神经官能症患者；神经质者；神经过敏者
words.ex: She had a neurotic fear of flying.
words.ex_cn: 她对飞行有一种神经质的恐惧。
words.en: If you say that someone is neurotic, you mean that they are always worried or anxious about things that you consider unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 精神病的；精神病学的；
words.ex: He works in a psychiatric hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家精神病医院工作。
words.en: Psychiatric means relating to psychiatry or to mental illness.

words.tr:
adj. 迟钝的；弱智的；智力发育迟缓的
v. 延迟；弄慢；使耽误；“retard”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was called retarded by some kids at school.
words.ex_cn: 他被学校的一些孩子叫做迟钝的。
words.en: Less advanced in mental, physical, or social development than is usual for one's age.

words.ex: The old man is toothless and eats soft food.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人没有牙齿，吃软食。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as toothless, you mean that they are ineffectual and unable to do anything to make their views or actions effective.

chapters.name: Level 10 形容词 感情•感觉

words.tr: adj. 骇人的； v. “appall”的现在分词；
words.ex: The accident caused an appalling sight.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了一幅骇人的景象。
words.en: If you describe something as appalling, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or unpleasant, and that you find it extremely unacceptable.

words.ex: The whisper was barely audible.
words.ex_cn: 那耳语几乎听不见。
words.en: If a sound is audible, it is loud enough for you to hear it.

words.tr:
n. 觉醒；醒悟；认识；感到
v. 唤醒；唤起；使意识到；“awaken”的现在分词
words.ex: The awakening of public interest in environmental issues is crucial.
words.ex_cn: 公众对环境问题的觉醒至关重要。
words.en: An awakening is a realization or awareness that comes to someone, often changing their perspective or behavior.

words.tr:
adj. 刺眼的；炫目的；使人眼花缭乱的
v. 使失明；“blind”的现在分词
words.ex: The sun was blinding as I walked outside.
words.ex_cn: 我走出去时，阳光刺眼。
words.en: If you describe something as blinding, you mean that it is very obvious or intense.

words.tr: adj. 令人毛骨悚然的；令人不寒而栗的
words.ex: The old house looks creepy at night.
words.ex_cn: 那栋老房子晚上看起来很阴森。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as creepy, you mean they make you feel very nervous or frightened.

words.ex: The eerie silence made us feel scared.
words.ex_cn: 那怪异的寂静让我们感到害怕。
words.en: If you describe something as eerie, you mean that it seems strange and frightening, and makes you feel nervous.

words.tr: adj. 期待的；未来的（母亲、父亲、父母）
words.ex: The expectant mother looked at the baby toys with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 这位期待的准妈妈看着婴儿玩具微笑着。
words.en: If someone is expectant, they are hopeful or excited because they think something interesting or pleasant is going to happen.

words.tr: adj. 充满（不愉快事物）的；
words.ex: The journey was fraught with delays.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅程充满了延误。
words.en: If a situation or activity is fraught with problems or risks, it is full of them.

words.ex: The swollen area is inflammatory and painful.
words.ex_cn: 这个肿胀的部位是发炎的，并且很痛。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behaviour as inflammatory, you mean that it is likely to cause people to react very angrily.

words.tr: adj. 引起兴趣的；引人入胜的； v. “intrigue”的现在分词；
words.ex: The mystery story was intriguing.
words.ex_cn: 这个侦探故事很引人入胜。
words.en: If you describe something as intriguing, you mean that it is interesting or strange.

words.tr: adj. 可悲的；令人惋惜的；质量低劣的
words.ex: The situation was lamentable, with many people losing their homes.
words.ex_cn: 情况非常可悲，许多人失去了家园。
words.en: If you describe something as lamentable, you mean that it is very unfortunate or disappointing.

words.tr: adj. 令人不快的；令人反感的；讨厌的
words.ex: The movie contains objectionable content.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影包含令人反感的内容。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as objectionable, you consider them to be extremely offensive and unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.tr: adj. 观察力敏锐的；谨慎遵守的；
words.ex: She is observant and notices small details.
words.ex_cn: 她观察力敏锐，能注意到细小的细节。
words.en: Someone who is observant pays close attention to things and notices more about them than most people do.

words.tr: v. 拥有；“possess”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He possessed a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有一栋靠近湖边的小房子。
words.en: If someone is described as possessed, they are thought to be under the control of an evil spirit.

words.tr: adj. 感官的；肉欲的；愉悦感官的；耽于肉欲的
words.ex: The sensual smell of fresh bread made her hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的感官香味让她感到饥饿。
words.en: Relating to or involving gratification of the senses and physical, especially sexual, pleasure.

words.tr:
adj. 未说出的；未表达的
v. 取消；撤回；’“unspeak”的过去分词
words.ex: There was an unspoken agreement between them.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间有一个未说出口的协议。
words.en: If something is unspoken, it has not been said, although it might have been thought or felt.

words.tr: adj. 扭曲的；弯曲的；复杂的
words.ex: The twistful road made driving difficult.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路让驾驶变得困难。
words.en: Characterized by twists or turns; winding.

chapters.name: Level 10 形容词 形状•性质•外观•状态

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.tr: adj. 崎岖不平的；颠簸的；
words.ex: The car drove over a bumpy road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车开过一条崎岖不平的路。
words.en: If you say that something is bumpy, you mean that it is uneven, with a lot of bumps.

words.ex: The cellular structure of plants is very small.
words.ex_cn: 植物的细胞结构非常微小。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of cells; having a porous structure.

words.tr: adj. 讲究礼仪的；隆重的
words.ex: He gave a ceremonious speech at the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他在婚礼上发表了一篇庄重的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as ceremonious, you mean that they are very formal or polite.

words.ex: He drives a red convertible on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他周末开一辆红色敞篷车。
words.en: A convertible is a car with a roof that can be folded down or removed.

words.tr: adj. 值得赞扬的；道德的
words.ex: His performance was creditable despite the difficult circumstances.
words.ex_cn: 尽管处境艰难，他的表现仍然值得称赞。
words.en: Deserving praise or approval; trustworthy.

words.tr: v. 越过； adj. 越过（cross 的过去式和过去分词）；
words.ex: He crossed the street quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速地越过了街道。
words.en: If you cross something, you go from one side of it to the other.

words.tr:
adj. 值得的；应得的
v. 值得；应得；“deserve”的现在分词
words.ex: He is deserving of a prize for his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他因努力工作而配得上一份奖品。
words.en: If you describe a person, organization, or cause as deserving, you mean that you think they should be helped. Deserving is also used to describe actions or qualities that are worthy of praise or reward.

words.tr: adj. 不整齐的；混乱的；骚乱的；无秩序的
words.ex: The room was in a disorderly state.
words.ex_cn: 房间处于一片混乱之中。
words.en: If you describe something as disorderly, you mean that it is untidy, irregular, or disorganized.

words.tr: adj. 休眠的；蛰伏的；暂停活动的
words.ex: The volcano is dormant now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Something that is dormant is not active or growing but has the ability to be active at a later time.

words.ex: The floppy ears of the dog waved when it ran.
words.ex_cn: 狗的松垂耳朵在它跑时晃动。
words.en: Something that is floppy is loose and soft, often hanging or bending in a way that suggests it lacks stiffness.

words.ex: The gallant soldier saved his comrades in battle.
words.ex_cn: 这位英勇的士兵在战斗中救了他的战友们。
words.en: If someone is gallant, they behave bravely and honorably in a dangerous or difficult situation. It can also describe someone who is very polite and kind towards women.

words.tr: adj. 鬼似的；幽灵般的；可怕的
words.ex: The ghostly figure walked silently through the night.
words.ex_cn: 那个幽灵般的身影在夜里安静地走着。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a ghost; eerie or spectral.

words.tr: adj. 像家般舒适的；朴素的；
words.ex: The small cabin had a homely feel with soft blankets and a warm fire.
words.ex_cn: 这座小木屋有柔软的毛毯和温暖的火炉，感觉像家一样舒适。
words.en: If you describe something as homely, you mean that it is simple and plain, often in a way that is comforting. If you describe a person as homely, you mean that they are not very attractive.

words.ex: The small brown bird was inconspicuous among the trees.
words.ex_cn: 这只棕色的小鸟在树丛中不引人注目。
words.en: Something that is inconspicuous is not easily seen or noticed.

words.ex: The words on the sign are indistinct.
words.ex_cn: 标志上的字模糊不清。
words.en: not clear or sharply defined

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.ex: His excuse was laughable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口可笑极了。
words.en: If you describe something as laughable, you mean that it is so silly or unreasonable that you can only laugh at it.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；懒散的；马虎的
words.ex: He is lax about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很松懈。
words.en: If you say that a person's behaviour or a system is lax, you mean they are not careful or strict about maintaining high standards.

words.tr: n. 匹配； adj. 匹配的； v. 相配；“match”的现在分词；
words.ex: The matching of colors makes the room look nice.
words.ex_cn: 颜色的匹配让房间看起来很漂亮。
words.en: If one thing is matching with another, they are similar in appearance, style, or color and therefore look attractive together.

words.tr:
n. （发声）单调
adj. 单调的
words.ex: He spoke in a monotone voice.
words.ex_cn: 他用单调的声音说话。
words.en: A monotone sound or voice does not change in pitch and is therefore considered boring or uninteresting.

words.ex: The ornate ceiling had gold patterns and flowers.
words.ex_cn: 华丽的天花板上有金色的图案和花朵。
words.en: Something that is ornate is highly decorated with complex patterns.

words.tr:
adj. 假的；冒充的；欺骗的
n. 骗子；伪君子；假货
words.ex: He gave a phony excuse for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他编了一个虚假的借口来解释迟到。
words.en: If you describe something as phony, you disapprove of it because it is false rather than genuine.

words.ex: The old book had a powdery cover.
words.ex_cn: 那本旧书的封面有粉末状的质感。
words.en: Resembling or consisting of powder; covered with powder.

words.tr: adj. 无（接）缝的；无漏洞的；
words.ex: The software has a seamless interface.
words.ex_cn: 这个软件有一个无缝的界面。
words.en: Something that is seamless has no obvious joins or gaps between its different parts.

words.tr: adj. 毛发粗浓杂乱的；毛发蓬松的
words.ex: The dog has a shaggy coat.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗有一身蓬乱的毛。
words.en: Having or covered with long, rough, and thick hair or fur.

words.ex: His answer was too simplistic.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答太简单化了。
words.en: If you describe something as simplistic, you disapprove of it because it is so simple that it ignores important details or difficulties.

words.tr:
adj. 光滑的；圆滑的；熟练的；华而不实的
n. 浮油层；光滑之处
v. 使平滑
words.ex: The ice on the road was slick.
words.ex_cn: 路上的冰很光滑。
words.en: If something is slick, it is done smoothly and efficiently, often in a way that is intended to be impressive.

words.ex: The instructions are unambiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很清楚。
words.en: If you describe something as unambiguous, you mean that it is clear and cannot be misunderstood.

chapters.name: Level 10 形容词 数字•时间•频率

words.ex: We arrived at the opportune moment, just as the meeting was starting.
words.ex_cn: 我们到达得很及时，正好会议刚开始。
words.en: If something happens at an opportune time or is opportune, it happens at the time that is most convenient for someone or most likely to lead to success.

words.ex: The model gives predictive results for next month's sales.
words.ex_cn: 这个模型提供了下个月销售额的预测结果。
words.en: If you use predictive to describe something, you mean that it is able to predict what will happen in the future.

words.ex: It is presumable that he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天可能会到。
words.en: If you say that something is presumable, you mean that you think it is true or likely, although you are not certain.

words.ex: The primal forest has never been touched by humans.
words.ex_cn: 这片原始森林从未被人类触碰过。
words.en: Primal means relating to an early stage in the development of something, or being the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: The job is repetitive and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作重复且无聊。
words.en: Something that is repetitive involves doing the same thing over and over again.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: adj. 未被打败过的；（路）未被走过的
words.ex: The team remained unbeaten all season.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在整个赛季中保持不败。
words.en: If a sports team or a person is unbeaten, they have not been defeated in any of their matches or games.

words.tr: adj. 意料之外的；未预见到的；
words.ex: The storm caused unforeseen damage to the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给小镇造成了意料之外的破坏。
words.en: If something is unforeseen, it was not expected to happen or known about beforehand.

words.ex: Her talent is unparalleled.
words.ex_cn: 她的才华是无比的。
words.en: Having no parallel or equal; unmatched.

chapters.name: Level 10 形容词 性格•倾向

words.tr:
adj. 乐于助人的；随和的
v. 为某人提供住宿；容纳；适应；“accommodate”的现在分词
words.ex: He is always accommodating to his friends' needs.
words.ex_cn: 他总是满足朋友的需求。
words.en: If you describe someone as accommodating, you like the fact that they are willing to do things in order to please you or help you.

words.tr: adj. 确定的； v. 向…保证；“assure”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was assured that the package would arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他确定包裹明天会到。
words.en: If you are assured of something, you are certain to get it or achieve it.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.ex: The soup was too bland for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太淡了，我不喜欢。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bland, you mean that they are rather dull and unexciting.

words.tr: adj. 孩子气的；像男孩的；幼稚的
words.ex: She had a boyish charm that many found endearing.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种孩子气的魅力，很多人都觉得非常可爱。
words.en: If you describe a man or his behaviour as boyish, you mean that he behaves like a young boy in a way that is attractive or endearing.

words.ex: He is calculating the total cost.
words.ex_cn: 他正在计算总费用。
words.en: If you describe someone as calculating, you disapprove of the fact that they deliberately plan to get what they want, often by hurting or harming other people.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.tr:
adj. 失职的；违法的；拖欠债务的
n. 违犯者；少年罪犯；违法者
words.ex: The delinquent worker ignored his duties.
words.ex_cn: 这位失职的员工忽视了他的职责。
words.en: A delinquent is someone, especially a young person, who commits a crime or breaks the law.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；衷心的；诚挚的；
words.ex: He is a devout Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名虔诚的基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: If you describe someone as devout, you mean that they have a deep religious faith.

words.tr: adj. 自我本位的；自负的；自高自大的
words.ex: He is egotistic and only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他很自我中心，只谈论自己。
words.en: If you describe someone as egotistic, you disapprove of them because they think they are better or more important than other people.

words.tr:
adj. 使人显得更漂亮的；奉承的
v. 奉承；讨好；“flatter”的现在分词
words.ex: She wore a flattering dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件很显身材的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If something is flattering, it makes you look or feel more attractive or better than you really are.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.ex: He gave a heartless reply to her plea.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的恳求给出了无情的答复。
words.en: If you describe someone as heartless, you mean that they are cruel and unkind, and have no sympathy for anyone or anything.

words.tr: adj. 无能力的；不称职的；不能胜任的；
words.ex: He is incompetent at managing simple tasks.
words.ex_cn: 他无法胜任简单的任务。
words.en: If you describe someone as incompetent, you are criticizing them because they are unable to do their job or a task properly.

words.tr: adj. 不可征服的；不能战胜的
words.ex: He felt invincible after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 赢得比赛后，他觉得自己不可战胜。
words.en: If someone or something is invincible, they are impossible to defeat or overcome.

words.ex: He was neglectful of his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很疏忽。
words.en: If you describe someone as neglectful, you mean they fail to do everything they should do to look after someone or something properly.

words.tr: adj. 有智虑的；精明的；有策略的
words.ex: It was politic to stay silent during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 在会议上保持沉默是明智的。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as politic, you mean that it is sensible and likely to achieve what you want.

words.tr: adj. 爱争吵的；好争论的
words.ex: He was a quarrelsome man who always started arguments.
words.ex_cn: 他是个爱争吵的人，总是挑起争论。
words.en: If you describe someone as quarrelsome, you mean that they are bad-tempered and often become involved in arguments.

words.tr: adj. 善于接受的；能接纳的；
words.ex: He is receptive to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他善于接受新想法。
words.en: Willing to consider or accept new suggestions and ideas.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.tr: adj. 遮遮掩掩的；守口如瓶的；
words.ex: He gave a secretive smile and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他露出一个遮遮掩掩的微笑，然后走开了。
words.en: If you are secretive, you like to have secrets and to keep your knowledge, feelings, or intentions hidden.

words.tr: adj.  羞怯的；腼腆的；局促不安的
words.ex: He gave a sheepish smile after forgetting his lines.
words.ex_cn: 他忘记台词后，尴尬地笑了笑。
words.en: If you look sheepish, you look slightly embarrassed because you feel foolish or you have done something silly.

words.tr: n. 英国货币；英镑；标准纯银；银制品；
words.ex: He paid for the book with sterling.
words.ex_cn: 他用英镑支付了这本书的费用。
words.en: Sterling is used to describe something of very high quality or value. It can also refer to British money or a standard of purity for silver.

words.ex: He is stingy with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很吝啬。
words.en: If you describe someone as stingy, you are criticizing them for being unwilling to spend money or to give or use a lot of something.

words.ex: Hiking up the mountain was a strenuous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰苦的任务。
words.en: Requiring or using great effort or exertion.

words.tr: adj. 不让步的；不妥协的；强硬的
words.ex: He is uncompromising about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他在诚实方面毫不妥协。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncompromising, you mean that they are determined not to change their opinions or aims in any way.

words.tr: adj. 未受控制、约束或统治的；
words.ex: The fire spread in an uncontrolled way.
words.ex_cn: 火以一种不受控制的方式蔓延。
words.en: If something is uncontrolled, no-one is controlling it or checking that it is done properly, so it may continue or spread without being stopped.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.tr: adj. 负有责任的；应作解释的
words.ex: He is accountable for his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他要为自己的错误负责。
words.en: If you are accountable to someone for something that you do, you are responsible for it and must be prepared to justify your actions to that person.

words.tr: adj. 道歉的；谢罪的；愧疚的
words.ex: He gave an apologetic smile after bumping into her.
words.ex_cn: 他撞到她后露出了歉意的微笑。
words.en: If you are apologetic, you show or say that you are sorry for having caused someone trouble or unhappiness.

words.tr: adj. 群体的；社区的；公有的；
words.ex: They share a communal kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他们共用一个群体厨房。
words.en: Communal means relating to or shared by all the members of a community.

words.ex: The school has a hierarchical system.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个等级制度。
words.en: A hierarchical system or organization is one in which people have different ranks or positions, depending on how important they are.

words.tr:
n. 帝国主义者
adj. 帝国主义的
words.ex: The imperialist country took over many colonies.
words.ex_cn: 这个帝国主义国家占领了许多殖民地。
words.en: An imperialist is a person who supports or practices imperialism, which is a policy of extending a country's power and influence through colonization, use of military force, or other means.

words.ex: The senate is doing lawmaking for the new tax rule.
words.ex_cn: 参议院正在为新的税收规则制定法律。
words.en: The process of making laws.

words.ex: He has a managerial role in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司中担任管理职务。
words.en: relating to the job of a manager

words.ex: The nomadic family moves with their sheep every season.
words.ex_cn: 这个游牧家庭每季都随着羊群迁移。
words.en: A nomadic way of life is one in which people move from place to place instead of living in one place all the time.

words.ex: He took a provisional job until he found a better one.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到更好的工作之前做了一份临时工作。
words.en: Something that is provisional is temporary and likely to be changed or replaced in the future.

words.ex: The regulatory agency checks food safety.
words.ex_cn: 监管机构检查食品安全。
words.en: Relating to the regulation of something, especially by the government.

words.tr:
adj. 不爱交际的；离群索居的；即将退休的
v. 退休；退役；“retire”的现在分词
words.ex: She was a retiring woman, preferring to spend her evenings at home.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个不爱与人交往的女人，更喜欢在家度过晚上。
words.en: If someone is retiring, they are about to leave their job permanently, usually because of age.

words.ex: He works in a secretarial role at the office.
words.ex_cn: 他在办公室担任秘书工作。
words.en: Relating to the work of a secretary or the duties of a secretary.

words.tr: adj. 少量使用的； v. “spare”的现在分词；
words.ex: He uses sparing amounts of sugar in his tea.
words.ex_cn: 他在茶里只用很少的糖。
words.en: If you describe someone as sparing, you mean that they are careful in the way they use something, especially money or food, because there is very little of it.

words.tr: adj. 战术上的；有谋略的；手段高明的
words.ex: He made a tactical move to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个战术性的举动来赢得比赛。
words.en: relating to or constituting actions carefully planned to gain a specific military end.

words.tr: adj. 未经许可的；未经授权的；
words.ex: He entered the building through an unauthorized door.
words.ex_cn: 他通过一扇未经许可的门进入了大楼。
words.en: If something is unauthorized, it has been done without the official permission of someone in authority.

words.tr: adj. 不盈利的；无利可图的；没有用的
words.ex: The small shop is unprofitable because few customers come.
words.ex_cn: 这家小店不赚钱，因为顾客很少。
