words.en: If an activity or business is unprofitable, it does not make a profit.

words.tr:
adj. 幻想的；有远见的
n. 空想家；有远见的人
words.ex: He had a visionary idea about flying cars.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个关于飞行汽车的幻想想法。
words.en: A visionary is someone who has strong ideas about how things might be different in the future, especially in a way that leads to changes in society or technology.

words.ex: The alcohol is volatile and evaporates quickly.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是易挥发的，会迅速蒸发。
words.en: A volatile situation or person is one that is likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, especially by getting worse.

words.tr: adj. 好战的；战备的；尚武的
words.ex: The nation was known for its warlike tendencies.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家以其好战倾向而闻名。
words.en: If you describe a person, nation, or behaviour as warlike, you mean that they are aggressive or eager to engage in war.

chapters.name: Level 10 形容词 天气•自然

words.tr: n. 开花时节；鼎盛时期；
words.ex: The flowering of cherry trees happens in spring.
words.ex_cn: 樱花的开花时节在春天。
words.en: The process or period of producing flowers; the state of being in bloom.

words.tr:
n. 淡水；
adj. 淡水的；
words.ex: Fish live in freshwater lakes.
words.ex_cn: 鱼生活在淡水湖中。
words.en: Freshwater refers to water that is not salty, especially water in rivers and lakes.

words.tr: adj. 长满…的； v. “overgrow”的过去分词；
words.ex: The garden is overgrown with weeds.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园长满了杂草。
words.en: If a place is overgrown, it is covered with plants that have grown in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: adj. 完全的；荒凉的；光秃秃的；僵硬的；严厉的
words.ex: There was a stark difference between the two results.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果之间有完全的差异。
words.en: Stark means complete, severe, or obvious in a way that is impossible to avoid noticing.

words.ex: The box remained untouched on the table.
words.ex_cn: 盒子原封不动地留在桌子上。
words.en: If something is untouched, it has not been changed or affected by something.

words.tr: adj. 长满树木的；树木覆盖的；
words.ex: The wooded hillside is home to many birds.
words.ex_cn: 长满树木的山坡是许多鸟类的家园。
words.en: A wooded area is covered with trees.

words.ex: The zoo has a zoological garden for rare animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个动物园有一个动物学花园，用于展示稀有动物。
words.en: Relating to the scientific study of animals.

chapters.name: Level 10 形容词 程度•单位

words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.ex: The cumulative score is the total of all previous points.
words.ex_cn: 累积得分是所有之前分数的总和。
words.en: If a series of events have a cumulative effect, each event makes the effect greater.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；肤浅的；易做到的
words.ex: He gave a facile answer to the hard question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个简单的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's arguments or suggestions as facile, you are criticizing them because their ideas are too simple and indicate a lack of careful, intelligent thinking.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；命中注定的；决定命运的；预言性的
words.ex: It was a fateful day when he met her.
words.ex_cn: 那是他遇见她的命运般的一天。
words.en: If you describe an event or action as fateful, you mean that it has very important and often bad effects on the future.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.tr: adj. 永无变化的；始终如一的
words.ex: The speed of light is invariable.
words.ex_cn: 光速是不变的。
words.en: An invariable thing or quality never changes or is always the same.

words.tr: adj. 可管理的；可应付的；可处理的；
words.ex: The project is manageable if we work together.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们一起合作，这个项目是可以管理的。
words.en: If you describe something as manageable, you mean that it is easy to control or deal with.

words.tr: adj. 最低限度的；极少的；最小的；
words.ex: He made minimal changes to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对计划做了最低限度的修改。
words.en: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

words.ex: The momentous decision changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 这个重要的决定改变了他的一生。
words.en: If you refer to a decision, event, or change as momentous, you mean that it is very important, often because of the effects that it will have in the future.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.ex: The keyboard is a peripheral device.
words.ex_cn: 键盘是一个外围设备。
words.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.ex: This plan is practicable.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的。
words.en: If a task, plan, or idea is practicable, it can be successfully done or achieved.

words.tr: adj. 值得称赞的；可嘉的
words.ex: His praiseworthy effort helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他值得称赞的努力帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Deserving praise; commendable.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

words.ex: He uses an unorthodox method to teach math.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种非传统的方法教数学。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour, beliefs, or customs as unorthodox, you mean that they are different from what is generally accepted.

words.tr: adj. 难以想象的；不可思议的；难以置信的；
words.ex: It is unthinkable to leave a child alone in the car.
words.ex_cn: 把孩子单独留在车里是难以想象的。
words.en: If something is unthinkable, it cannot be imagined or considered because it is so bad, impossible, or unlikely to happen.

words.ex: This tool is usable for beginners.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具初学者可以用。
words.en: If something is usable, it is in a good enough state or condition to be used.

words.tr: adj. 很小的；极小的；微量的；很少的
words.ex: She had only a wee bit of sugar left.
words.ex_cn: 她只剩下一点点糖了。
words.en: Very small; very early.

words.tr: adj. 沉重的；重要的；重大的；
words.ex: The box is weighty and hard to carry.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子很重，很难搬。
words.en: Something that is weighty is important and serious, or seems to be so.

chapters.name: Level 10 副词 位置•场所

words.tr:
adv. 顺时针方向地
adj. 顺时针方向的
words.ex: Turn the knob clockwise to open the jar.
words.ex_cn: 顺时针转动旋钮来打开罐子。
words.en: Moving in the same direction as the hands of a clock.

words.tr:
adj. 逆时针方向的
adv. 逆时针方向地
words.ex: The fan spins counterclockwise.
words.ex_cn: 风扇逆时针旋转。
words.en: In the opposite direction to the way in which the hands of a clock move.

chapters.name: Level 10 副词 频率

words.ex: He started afresh after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后从头开始。
words.en: If you do something afresh, you do it again in a different way, often in a way that is better than before.

chapters.name: Level 10 副词 程度

words.ex: He expressly told me not to be late.
words.ex_cn: 他特意告诉我不要迟到。
words.en: If something is said or done expressly, it is said or done in a clear, deliberate way.

words.tr:
adv. 小心地；谨慎地
adj. 小心的；谨慎的
words.ex: He walked gingerly on the icy path.
words.ex_cn: 他小心翼翼地走在结冰的小路上。
words.en: If you do something gingerly, you do it in a careful manner, usually because you expect it to be dangerous, unpleasant, or painful.

words.tr: adv. 详细地；极微地；极小心精确地
words.ex: He explained the plan minutely.
words.ex_cn: 他详细地解释了这个计划。
words.en: In a detailed or precise manner; every minute.

words.tr: adv. 痛苦地；强烈地；非常地
words.ex: He was sorely hurt in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中痛苦地受伤了。
words.en: If you are sorely in need of something, you need it very much.

chapters.name: Level 10 副词 其他

words.tr:
n. 赞成票；投赞成票者
adv. 是；赞成；常常；永远
words.ex: The motion was carried by an aye vote.
words.ex_cn: 该动议以赞成票通过。
words.en: An expression of assent or agreement; always or forever.

words.ex: Theoretically, the plan should work.
words.ex_cn: 理论上，这个计划应该可行。
words.en: In a way that relates to the theory of a subject or area of study rather than its practical application.

chapters.name: Level 10 感叹词

words.tr: int. （表示惊奇、感动或气恼）哇，哎呀；
words.ex: Gee, I didn't expect you to win!
words.ex_cn: 哇，我没料到你会赢！
words.en: Used to express surprise, enthusiasm, or simple emphasis.

chapters.name: Level 10 代词

words.ex: I will protect thee from all harm.
words.ex_cn: 我会保护你免受一切伤害。
words.en: Thee is an archaic or dialect form of 'you', used as the object of a verb or preposition.

chapters.name: Level 11 状态•存在类动词

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.ex: He was a successful financier who made his fortune in the stock market.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成功的金融家，在股市中赚取了他的财富。
words.en: A financier is a person who is skilled in managing large amounts of money, especially someone who controls or lends large sums of money to businesses or governments.

words.ex: Children play in the plaza after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在广场上玩耍。
words.en: A plaza is an open public space that is found in the heart of a city or town. It is often surrounded by buildings and may include shops, restaurants, and other amenities.

words.ex: He wants to invest in a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他想投资一家小企业。
words.en: To put money, effort, time, etc. into something to make a profit or achieve a result.

words.ex: He was arrested as an accomplice to the robbery.
words.ex_cn: 他因作为抢劫的帮凶而被逮捕。
words.en: An accomplice is someone who helps another person to commit a crime.

words.ex: The court acquitted him of all charges.
words.ex_cn: 法院宣告他无罪。
words.en: If someone is acquitted of a crime in a court of law, they are formally declared not to have committed the crime.

words.ex: She sang a beautiful aria at the opera.
words.ex_cn: 她在歌剧上唱了一段优美的咏叹调。
words.en: An aria is a song for one voice in an opera, often expressing a character's emotions.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.ex: His wrath scared everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒吓到了房间里的每个人。
words.en: Extreme anger.

words.tr: v. 废除；取消；宣告无效
words.ex: The court will annul the marriage.
words.ex_cn: 法院将宣布婚姻无效。
words.en: To annul something means to declare it invalid or to officially say that it no longer exists.

words.ex: The lion showed ferocity when it hunted.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在捕猎时表现出凶猛。
words.en: Ferocity refers to the state or quality of being ferocious, which means savagely fierce, cruel, or violent.

words.tr:
adj. 制药的；配药的；
n. 药物；
words.ex: He works at a pharmaceutical company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家制药公司工作。
words.en: relating to the production and sale of medicinal drugs

words.tr: v. 迅速生长；急速增长
words.ex: The flowers burgeon in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，花朵绽放。
words.en: To grow or develop quickly; to flourish.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉剂；麻醉药
adj. 麻醉的
words.ex: The doctor gave him an anesthetic before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生在手术前给他用了麻醉剂。
words.en: An anesthetic is a substance that causes loss of sensation or consciousness, used especially to prevent pain during medical procedures.

words.ex: He runs every day to keep his cardiovascular system healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天跑步以保持心血管系统健康。
words.en: Relating to the heart and the blood vessels.

words.tr:
n. 凝块；泥团；密集的一群
v. 凝结成块
words.ex: The blood began to clot after the cut.
words.ex_cn: 伤口流血后开始凝固。
words.en: A clot is a sticky lump that forms when blood dries up or becomes thick. If blood clots, it becomes thick and forms a lump.

words.ex: The children were boisterous at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在聚会上喧闹不已。
words.en: Someone who is boisterous is noisy, lively, and full of energy.

words.tr:
n. 酒；酒宴；暴饮
v. 暴饮；痛饮
words.ex: He drinks too much booze at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上喝太多酒。
words.en: To booze means to drink alcohol, especially in large quantities.

words.tr:
n. 杂乱；混乱
v. 弄乱
words.ex: The table is full of clutter.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上堆满了杂物。
words.en: If things or people clutter a place, they fill it in an untidy way.

words.ex: The two cultures are disparate in their traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化在传统上完全不同。
words.en: Things that are disparate are clearly different from each other in quality or type.

words.tr: v. 聚合；合并；长到一起
words.ex: The small ponds coalesce into a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 小池塘合并成一个大湖。
words.en: If two or more things coalesce, they come together and form a single group or system.

words.tr:
adj. 砾岩的；成球状的；结成团块的
n. 砾岩；企业集团；联合大公司；合成物
v. （使）结聚成一团
words.ex: The rock layer is conglomerate, made of small stones stuck together.
words.ex_cn: 这层岩石是砾岩，由小石头粘合而成。
words.en: A conglomerate is a large business firm consisting of several different companies.

words.ex: A sliver of wood stuck in his finger.
words.ex_cn: 一小片木头扎进了他的手指。
words.en: A sliver is a small, thin piece of something that has been cut, broken, or torn off from a larger piece.

words.tr:
adj. 引火的；燃烧的；纵火的；煽动的
n. 燃烧弹
words.ex: The incendiary device set the building on fire.
words.ex_cn: 这个引火装置把大楼点燃了。
words.en: An incendiary device is designed to cause fires. Incendiary remarks or actions are likely to cause anger or violence.

words.tr:
v. 发劈啪声；发尖而轻的爆裂声
n. 劈啪响；裂纹
words.ex: The fire crackles in the hearth.
words.ex_cn: 壁炉里的火噼啪作响。
words.en: If something crackles, it makes a rapid series of short, sharp noises.

words.ex: He has hepatitis and needs to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他患有肝炎，需要休息。
words.en: Hepatitis is an inflammation of the liver, often caused by a viral infection.

words.ex: The illness debilitates him every winter.
words.ex_cn: 每年冬天，这场疾病都会使他虚弱。
words.en: To make someone weak and infirm.

words.ex: He is obese because he eats too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多垃圾食品而肥胖。
words.en: If someone is obese, they are extremely fat.

words.ex: The patriarch leads his large family with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 这位族长以智慧领导他的大家庭。
words.en: A patriarch is a man who is the head of a family or tribe, or a highly respected man in a particular field.

words.tr: v. 放气；紧缩；缩小；挫某人锐气
words.ex: The balloon will deflate if you let the air out.
words.ex_cn: 如果你放出空气，气球就会瘪掉。
words.en: If you deflate someone or something, you take away their confidence or make them seem less important.

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.ex: The managers met in the boardroom to discuss the plan.
words.ex_cn: 经理们在会议室里讨论计划。
words.en: A boardroom is a room where the board of directors of a company meets.

words.tr:
adj. 退步的；堕落的；腐化的
v. 退化；堕落
n. 堕落的人
words.ex: The old machine became degenerate and stopped working.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器退步了，停止工作了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something degenerates, you mean that they become worse in some way, for example, poorer, weaker, or less respectable.

words.ex: The announcement caused an uproar in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个公告在小镇上引起了轩然大波。
words.en: A loud and impassioned noise or disturbance.

words.tr:
n. 大量贮备；囤积
v. 大量储备；囤积
words.ex: The government built a stockpile of food for emergencies.
words.ex_cn: 政府为紧急情况储备了大量食物。
words.en: A stockpile is a large supply of something that is kept to be used in the future.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.tr: v. 驱逐出境；使举止得体
words.ex: They will deport him for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 他们将因他违法而驱逐他。
words.en: If a government deports someone, usually someone who is not a citizen of that country, it sends them out of the country because they have committed a crime or because it believes they do not have the right to be there.

words.ex: The police seized illicit drugs from the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察从嫌疑人那里没收了非法毒品。
words.en: Illicit activities or substances are not allowed by law or by social or religious custom.

words.tr: n. 聚居区；犹太人区；贫民区
words.ex: He grew up in a poor ghetto.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个贫穷的贫民区长大。
words.en: A ghetto is a part of a city in which members of a minority group live, especially because of social, legal, or economic pressure.

words.tr: v. 罢免；废黜；宣誓证明
words.ex: The people deposed the corrupt leader.
words.ex_cn: 人民推翻了腐败的领导人。
words.en: To depose someone means to remove them from a position of power or authority, especially a monarch or political leader.

words.ex: He was punished for treason against the king.
words.ex_cn: 他因对国王叛国而受到惩罚。
words.en: Treason is the crime of betraying your country, for example by helping its enemies or by trying to remove its government using violence.

words.ex: The man faced deportation for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因违法而面临驱逐。
words.en: The act of expelling a person from a country, typically because they do not have the legal right to be there or because they have committed a crime.

words.ex: The czar ruled Russia with strong power.
words.ex_cn: 沙皇以强大的权力统治俄罗斯。
words.en: A czar is a male monarch or emperor, especially one of the former emperors of Russia.

words.ex: The enactment of the new law took effect last month.
words.ex_cn: 新法律的颁布上个月生效了。
words.en: The process of passing legislation or the state of being enacted.

words.ex: The power will devolve to the local government.
words.ex_cn: 权力将下放给地方政府。
words.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

words.ex: The cartel controls the price of oil.
words.ex_cn: 这个卡特尔控制着石油的价格。
words.en: A cartel is an association of manufacturers or suppliers with the purpose of maintaining prices at a high level and restricting competition.

words.ex: The band will disband next month.
words.ex_cn: 这个乐队下个月将解散。
words.en: If someone disbands a group of people, or if the group disbands, it stops operating as a single unit.

words.ex: The government announced a devaluation of the currency.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布货币贬值。
words.en: A reduction in the value of a currency with respect to other monetary units.

words.tr: n. 骑兵；骑警；伞兵；部队运输船; n. （Trooper）人名；（英）特鲁珀
words.ex: The trooper rode a horse on the battlefield.
words.ex_cn: 这名骑兵在战场上骑马。
words.en: A trooper is a soldier of low rank in the cavalry or in an armoured unit in the army, or a member of the state police in some countries.

words.tr:
v. 使湿透；浸透
n. 弄湿；浸液
words.ex: The rain drenched his clothes.
words.ex_cn: 雨把他的衣服淋湿了。
words.en: To drench something or someone means to make them completely wet.

words.tr: adj. 寒冷的；冷淡的；性冷淡的（女子）
words.ex: The water is frigid in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的水很冰冷。
words.en: Frigid means extremely cold in temperature or lacking warmth or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.
words.ex_cn: 他是耶稣的十二使徒之一。
words.en: An apostle is one of the twelve disciples chosen by Jesus Christ to preach his gospel.

words.ex: Her kindness emanates from her smile.
words.ex_cn: 她的善良表现在她的微笑中。
words.en: To emanate means to come out from a source.

words.ex: The old house has a mysterious aura.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子有一种神秘的氛围。
words.en: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality that seems to surround and be generated by a person, thing, or place.

words.tr: v. 使卷入；使陷入；牵连
words.ex: He didn't want to embroil his friend in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让朋友卷入这场争吵。
words.en: To involve someone in a difficult or complicated situation.

words.tr:
n. （文字）诽谤
v. 发表文字诽谤（某人）
words.ex: He wrote a false story about her, and it was libel.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于她的虚假文章，这是诽谤。
words.en: A libel is a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation; a written defamation.

words.tr: v. 使根深蒂固；使处于牢固地位；用壕沟围住
words.ex: The habit entrenches itself over time.
words.ex_cn: 这个习惯随着时间的推移变得根深蒂固。
words.en: To establish something very firmly so that it is very difficult to change.

words.ex: The ancient text contained arcane symbols that no one could understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本古籍中包含着无人能理解的晦涩难解的符号。
words.en: Arcane refers to something that is mysterious or difficult to understand, often because it is known or understood by only a few people.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.tr: n. 暗指；影射；间接提及
words.ex: He made an allusion to Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中提到了莎士比亚。
words.en: An allusion is an indirect reference to someone or something.

words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.ex: He felt animosity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对邻居感到敌意。
words.en: Animosity is a strong feeling of dislike and anger towards someone.

words.ex: The roller coaster exhilarates the children.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让孩子们感到兴奋。
words.en: To make someone feel very happy and excited.

words.ex: The artist painted a colorful mural on the school wall.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家在学校墙上画了一幅色彩斑斓的壁画。
words.en: A mural is a large painting, typically executed directly on a wall.

words.tr: n. 收容所；避难所；精神病院；（政治）庇护
words.ex: The old building now serves as an asylum for the homeless.
words.ex_cn: 这栋旧建筑现在是无家可归者的收容所。
words.en: An asylum is a place where people who are in danger or who have no homes can go for safety and protection.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr: phrase. 生命的丧失；死亡（尤指多人死亡）
words.ex: The storm caused a loss of life in the coastal town.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴在沿海小镇造成了人员死亡。
words.en: The death of a person or people, especially in large numbers as a result of an accident, disaster, or war.

words.ex: He will forgo dessert to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 为了保持健康，他将放弃甜点。
words.en: If you forgo something, you decide to do without it, even though you would like it.

words.tr:
n. 尿布
v. 用尿布衬上
words.ex: The baby needs a clean diaper.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝需要一块干净的尿布。
words.en: A diaper is a piece of soft cloth or paper which is fastened around a baby's bottom in order to absorb its waste.

words.ex: The factory galvanize iron sheets to prevent rust.
words.ex_cn: 工厂对铁片进行镀锌以防止生锈。
words.en: To galvanize someone means to cause them to take action, for example by making them feel very excited, afraid, or angry.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.ex: The children are vibrant and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们充满活力。
words.en: If you describe something as vibrant, you mean that it is bright, lively, and full of energy.

words.ex: He tried to gild the old box with gold paint.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用金漆把旧盒子镀金。
words.en: To cover something with a thin layer of gold or to make something seem more attractive or valuable than it really is.

words.tr: n. 入门；大门；入口网站
words.ex: This book is a portal to learning English.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是学习英语的入门。
words.en: A portal is a large and imposing entrance, doorway, or gate, or a website that provides access or links to other sites.

words.ex: The onslaught of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 大量倾泻的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: An onslaught is a very powerful, often violent, attack against someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 弹弓；石弩；弹射器
v. 用弩炮（等）发射；（使）突然处于…情况
words.ex: The boys used a catapult to launch stones.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们用投石机发射石头。
words.en: A catapult is a device used to throw or hurl a projectile a great distance without the aid of explosive devices—particularly various types of ancient and medieval siege engines. In a more modern context, it can also refer to a device that launches aircraft from a ship, or metaphorically, to propel someone to fame or success suddenly.

words.tr:
n. 弧口凿；半圆凿；凿成的槽（或孔、洞）
v. 凿；挖出；敲竹杠；诈骗
words.ex: He used a gouge to carve the wooden bowl.
words.ex_cn: 他用弧口凿雕刻木碗。
words.en: To gouge means to make a hole or groove in something using a sharp tool or object, or to charge someone too much money for something.

words.tr: n. 防御土墙；城墙；壁垒
words.ex: The old castle had a high rampart around it.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡周围有一道高高的城墙。
words.en: A rampart is a wide, high wall of earth, stone, or other material built around a place to protect it from attack.

words.tr: n. 宣告无罪；无罪的判决
words.ex: The court gave him an acquittal after the trial.
words.ex_cn: 审判后，法院宣布他无罪。
words.en: An acquittal is a formal declaration in a court of law that someone who has been accused of a crime is not guilty.

words.ex: Her smile heartened the tired students.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑鼓舞了疲惫的学生。
words.en: If someone is heartened by something, it encourages them and makes them cheerful.

words.ex: The company made a cutback on office supplies.
words.ex_cn: 公司减少了办公用品的开支。
words.en: A reduction in something, especially in the amount of money spent on a particular thing.

words.ex: He used a match to ignite the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: If you ignite something or if it ignites, it starts burning or explodes.

words.ex: The new law caused a big backlash from the public.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律引起了公众的强烈反应。
words.en: A backlash is a strong, adverse reaction by a large number of people, especially to a social or political development.

words.tr: v. 使负罪；指控…有罪；牵连
words.ex: He did not want to incriminate his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让他的朋友涉罪。
words.en: If something incriminates someone, it suggests that they are guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.

words.ex: He was charged with perjury after lying in court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后被控伪证罪。
words.en: The crime of telling a lie in a court of law after having sworn to tell the truth.

words.ex: I suspect it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我猜想明天会下雨。
words.en: If you suspect someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you believe that they have done it, although you have no proof.

words.tr:
adj. 可怕的；恐怖的；惨白的；令人不快的
adv. 可怖地；惨白地
words.ex: The ghost looked ghastly in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 那个幽灵在黑暗中看起来吓人极了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as ghastly, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant or shocking.

words.ex: The conflagration destroyed the whole forest.
words.ex_cn: 这场大火烧毁了整个森林。
words.en: A conflagration is a large and destructive fire that causes considerable damage.

words.tr: v. 淹没；泛滥；使不胜负荷；使应接不暇
words.ex: The rain inundated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 大雨淹没了这个小镇。
words.en: To inundate means to flood or overwhelm something with a large amount of water or things.

words.tr: phrase. 死者与伤者（指事故、灾难或冲突中的伤亡人员）
words.ex: The ambulance took the dead and injured to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 救护车把死者和伤者送到了医院。
words.en: The dead and injured refers to people who have been killed or hurt in an accident, war, or disaster.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.ex: There is a dearth of clean water in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄缺乏干净的水。
words.en: A dearth of something is a lack or scarcity of it.

words.tr: n. 朝圣之旅；参拜之行；瞻仰之旅；
words.ex: Many people go on a pilgrimage to the holy city.
words.ex_cn: 许多人前往圣城进行朝圣之旅。
words.en: A pilgrimage is a journey to a holy place for religious reasons.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢而弯曲地流动；漫步；闲聊
n. 河流的曲折；漫步；迂回曲折的进程
words.ex: The river meanders through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河蜿蜒穿过森林。
words.en: To meander means to follow a winding and turning course, often used to describe the way a river flows or the way a person walks without a clear direction.

words.ex: Many pilgrims visit the holy land every year.
words.ex_cn: 每年有许多朝圣者前往圣地。
words.en: The term 'the holy land' refers to a region revered as sacred by various religions, particularly the area in the Middle East associated with biblical events.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.ex: He traced his lineage back to ancient kings.
words.ex_cn: 他追溯了自己的家系到古代的国王。
words.en: Your lineage is the series of families from which you are directly descended.

words.tr: n. 参与人（数）；装束；产量；清理
words.ex: The turnout for the election was very high.
words.ex_cn: 这次选举的投票率很高。
words.en: The number of people attending or participating in an event, especially a political meeting or election.

words.ex: The new car outstrips the old one in speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆新车在速度上超过了旧车。
words.en: To outstrip means to go faster or to do better than someone or something else.

words.tr: n. 特技表演；噱头；发育不良的动植物；
words.ex: The actor performed a dangerous stunt in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在电影中表演了一个危险的特技。
words.en: A stunt is a dangerous feat that is done to entertain people, especially in a film.

words.ex: His talent overshadowed his brother's achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华使他兄弟的成就黯然失色。
words.en: If an unpleasant event or feeling overshadows something, it makes it less happy or enjoyable.

words.ex: The troupe performed a dance show in the town square.
words.ex_cn: 这个表演团在广场上演了一出舞蹈表演。
words.en: A troupe is a group of actors, singers, or dancers who work together.

words.ex: The city passed an ordinance to stop littering.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过了一项禁止乱扔垃圾的法令。
words.en: An ordinance is an authoritative rule, law, decree, or command.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.ex: The movie shows an apocalypse after a big nuclear war.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了核战争后的末世景象。
words.en: An apocalypse is a very serious event resulting in great destruction and change.

words.ex: Rabbits proliferate quickly in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在野外繁殖得很快。
words.en: If something proliferates, it increases in number or spreads quickly.

words.tr: phrase. 在当时；在那些日子里；从前
words.ex: In those days, people traveled by horse and carriage.
words.ex_cn: 在过去，人们乘坐马车旅行。
words.en: In the past, during that period.

words.ex: The government raised the excise on tobacco.
words.ex_cn: 政府提高了烟草的货物税。
words.en: Excise is a tax that is charged on goods produced within a country, or on goods that are brought into a country from abroad, especially on goods such as alcohol and tobacco. It can also refer to the act of cutting out or removing something, especially in a surgical operation.

words.ex: The company's profits quadrupled last year.
words.ex_cn: 公司去年的利润增长了四倍。
words.en: To quadruple something means to make it four times as great in size, amount, or number.

words.ex: The court will quash the false order.
words.ex_cn: 法院将撤销这个虚假的命令。
words.en: If a court or someone in authority quashes a decision or judgment, they officially reject it and say that it is not valid.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；丑恶可耻的；公然的
words.ex: He made a flagrant mistake during the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中犯了一个明显的错误。
words.en: If you describe an action as flagrant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way and is intended to shock or offend people.

words.ex: The email was bogus and tried to steal my password.
words.ex_cn: 这封邮件是假的，试图窃取我的密码。
words.en: If you describe something as bogus, you mean that it is not genuine, true, or real.

words.tr: n. 会合地点；约会；集会
words.ex: They will rendezvous at the park at 6 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 他们将在晚上6点在公园会合。
words.en: A rendezvous is a meeting that has been arranged between people, often secretly.

words.ex: The sound reverberated in the empty hall.
words.ex_cn: 声音在空荡的大厅里回响。
words.en: If a sound reverberates, it continues to be heard as an echo, or it seems to be repeated many times.

words.ex: Beijing is a transport hub in China.
words.ex_cn: 北京是中国的交通中心。
words.en: A hub is the central part of a wheel, rotating on or with the axle, and from which the spokes radiate. It can also refer to a central point of activity or interest.

words.ex: The city plan will revitalize the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市计划将使老城区复兴。
words.en: To revitalize something means to give it new life or energy.

words.ex: The magic show riveted the children's attention.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们的注意力。
words.en: A rivet is a short metal pin or bolt for holding together two plates of metal, its headless end being beaten out or pressed down when in place. As a verb, to rivet means to attract and hold the attention of someone completely.

words.ex: The old edifice stands near the river.
words.ex_cn: 那座古老的建筑坐落在河边。
words.en: An edifice is a large, impressive building.

words.ex: The loan requires collateral documents.
words.ex_cn: 这笔贷款需要附属文件。
words.en: Collateral is something pledged as security for repayment of a loan, to be forfeited in the event of a default.

words.tr:
v. 下垂；下跌；消沉
n. 下垂；下跌；下陷
words.ex: The old bridge sags in the middle.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥中间下垂。
words.en: If something sags, it hangs down loosely or sinks downwards in the middle, often because it is not supported properly or because it is too heavy.

words.tr:
n. 睡眠；
v. 睡觉；
words.ex: He needs more sleep to feel better.
words.ex_cn: 他需要更多的睡眠来感觉好些。
words.en: Sleep is the natural state of rest in which your eyes are closed, your body is inactive, and your mind is unconscious.

words.tr:
n. 导管；管道；管子
v. 通过管道输送
words.ex: The air flows through the duct.
words.ex_cn: 空气通过管道流动。
words.en: A duct is a pipe or tube through which liquid or gas flows.

words.ex: The company had a meltdown after the scandal.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在丑闻后彻底垮台了。
words.en: A situation in which something fails or collapses suddenly and completely, often used to describe a financial crisis or the overheating and melting of a nuclear reactor's core.

words.tr:
n. 手铐；脚镣；镣铐；束缚物
v. 给...戴上镣铐；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner wore iron shackle on his ankle.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯脚上戴着铁镣。
words.en: A shackle is a pair of metal rings connected by a chain which are fastened around someone's wrists or ankles in order to prevent them from moving or escaping.

words.tr: adj. 濒临死亡的；垂死的；
words.ex: The moribund patient stopped breathing.
words.ex_cn: 这位濒临死亡的病人停止了呼吸。
words.en: If you describe something as moribund, you mean that it is in a very bad condition and is not active or successful.

words.ex: He feared retribution for his actions.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕因自己的行为而受到报复。
words.en: Retribution is punishment for a crime, especially punishment that is carried out by someone other than the official authorities.

words.tr: v. 重击；猛击；突然深有感触
words.ex: The knight will smite the dragon with his sword.
words.ex_cn: 骑士将用他的剑击打龙。
words.en: To strike or hit someone or something very hard.

words.tr:
n. 鬼；幽灵；间谍
v. 鬼怪般出没；吓唬
words.ex: The children were scared of the spook in the haunted house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们害怕鬼屋里的鬼。
words.en: A spook is a ghost or a spy. It can also mean to frighten or scare someone.

words.tr: n. 鬼怪；幽灵；缠绕心头的恐惧
words.ex: The specter of famine haunted the war-torn region.
words.ex_cn: 饥荒的幽灵在饱受战争蹂躏的地区徘徊。
words.en: A specter is a ghost or a phantom, or something that haunts or perturbs the mind.

words.ex: The garrison stayed in the fort during the war.
words.ex_cn: 驻军在战争期间留在堡垒里。
words.en: A garrison is a group of soldiers whose job is to guard the town or building where they live.

words.ex: This is his first foray into painting.
words.ex_cn: 这是他首次涉足绘画。
words.en: A foray is a sudden and brief incursion or attack into enemy territory, especially to obtain something; a raid. It can also refer to an initial attempt to become involved in a different activity or profession.

words.ex: They tried to subvert the government.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图颠覆政府。
words.en: To subvert means to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.

words.tr: v. 发音；宣告；“pronounce”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 显著的；
words.ex: He pronounced the word correctly.
words.ex_cn: 他正确地发音了这个单词。
words.en: Something that is pronounced is very noticeable or obvious.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.ex: The school's ethos is respect for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的社會精神特质是尊重每一个人。
words.en: The fundamental character or spirit of a culture; the underlying sentiment that informs the beliefs, customs, or practices of a group or society.

words.ex: Confucian values emphasize respect for elders.
words.ex_cn: 儒家价值观强调尊重长辈。
words.en: Relating to Confucius or his teachings.

words.ex: The rupture in the pipe caused a flood.
words.ex_cn: 管道的破裂导致了洪水。
words.en: A rupture is a severe injury in which an internal part of your body tears or bursts open, or the act of breaking or bursting something.

words.tr:
v. （使）失去光泽；使晦暗；玷污
n. 晦暗；污渍
words.ex: The silver spoon will tarnish if not cleaned.
words.ex_cn: 如果银勺不清洗，就会变暗。
words.en: If you say that something tarnishes someone's reputation or image, you mean that it causes people to have a worse opinion of them than they would otherwise have had.

words.ex: The chef made a deft cut with the knife.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用刀熟练地切了一下。
words.en: A deft action is skilful and often quick.

words.ex: Our team won the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 我们的团队赢得了足球比赛。
words.en: A team is a group of people who play a particular sport or game together against other similar groups of people.

words.tr:
adj. 犬的；狗的；似犬的；犬科的
n. 犬；犬齿
words.ex: The dog has sharp canine teeth.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗有锋利的犬齿。
words.en: Canine refers to anything related to dogs or the family Canidae, which includes dogs, wolves, foxes, and other similar animals.

words.ex: He has business acumen and makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他有商业洞察力，能做出明智的决定。
words.en: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain.

words.tr: adj. 庄重的；庄严的；堂皇的；
words.ex: The stately mansion stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 那座庄重的豪宅矗立在山上。
words.en: Something that is stately is impressive because of its size, beauty, or grandeur.

words.tr:
v. 衰落；减弱；缺；亏
n. 衰退；减弱；缺；亏
words.ex: The moon begins to wane after the full moon.
words.ex_cn: 满月之后，月亮开始变暗。
words.en: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

chapters.name: Level 11 沟通类动词

words.ex: The comptroller checks all the money records.
words.ex_cn: 审计长检查所有的财务记录。
words.en: A comptroller is a person who is in charge of the financial accounts of a company or organization.

words.tr: n. 好友；密友；任人唯亲
words.ex: He went to lunch with his crony after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后和好友一起去吃午饭。
words.en: A crony is a close friend or companion.

words.ex: He abetted his friend to steal the car.
words.ex_cn: 他教唆朋友偷车。
words.en: To abet someone to do something wrong means to help or encourage them to do it.

words.ex: The curator arranged the paintings in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 馆长在博物馆里布置了这些画作。
words.en: A curator is someone who is in charge of the objects or works of art in a museum or art gallery.

words.ex: The teacher admonished the student to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师劝告学生完成作业。
words.en: To admonish someone means to tell them in a serious way that they have done something wrong.

words.tr: n. （基督教的）教牧人员；（任一宗教的）牧师; adj. 牧师的，教士的
words.ex: The cleric delivered a powerful sermon.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧师发表了一篇有力的布道。
words.en: A cleric is a member of the clergy, especially in the Christian Church.

words.tr: v. 晒太阳（取暖）；沉浸于
words.ex: He basks in the warm sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 他沐浴在温暖的阳光下。
words.en: If you bask in the sunshine, you lie somewhere sunny and enjoy the heat.

words.tr: adj. 黄铜制的；黄铜色的；厚颜无耻的
words.ex: The brazen statue sparkled in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 这尊黄铜雕像在阳光下闪闪发光。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as brazen, you mean that they are doing something shocking or immoral in a very open way, without trying to hide it.

words.tr: v. 诱骗；消遣；迷住；消磨
words.ex: He beguiles her with sweet words.
words.ex_cn: 他用甜言蜜语哄骗她。
words.en: If someone beguiles you, they charm you in a way that makes you trust them or like them, often so that they can deceive you.

words.tr:
v. 虚张声势；唬人
n. 虚张声势；吓唬；峭壁
adj. 直率的
words.ex: He used a bluff to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚张声势赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you bluff, you try to make someone believe that you will do something when you do not really intend to do it, or that you know something when you do not really know it.

words.tr: n. 福音传道者；福音传教士
words.ex: He is an evangelist who shares his faith every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每周日都分享信仰的传教士。
words.en: An evangelist is a person who seeks to convert others to the Christian faith, especially by public preaching.

words.tr: n. 领班；工头；陪审团主席
words.ex: The foreman told the workers to start the job.
words.ex_cn: 工头告诉工人们开始工作。
words.en: A foreman is a skilled and experienced worker who is in charge of a group of workers, especially in a factory or on a building site.

words.ex: He blurted out the secret by accident.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心说出了秘密。
words.en: If someone blurts something, they say it suddenly, after trying hard to keep quiet or to keep it secret.

words.tr: adj. 阴险的；潜伏的；暗中作祟的
words.ex: The insidious virus spread quietly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种隐蔽的病毒悄然在小镇蔓延。
words.en: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way, but with harmful effects.

words.ex: His defection shocked the whole team.
words.ex_cn: 他的叛逃让整个团队震惊。
words.en: The act of abandoning a cause, party, or nation, especially in favor of an opposing one.

words.ex: The coach chastened the team for their poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 教练因球队表现不佳而惩罚了他们。
words.en: If you are chastened by something, it makes you regret that you have behaved badly or stupidly.

words.ex: My mother chides me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈因为我回家晚而责备我。
words.en: If you chide someone, you speak to them angrily because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: His upbringing taught him to be honest and kind.
words.ex_cn: 他的抚育让他学会了诚实和善良。
words.en: The way that a child is cared for and taught how to behave while it is growing up.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.tr:
v. 移居国外；把…逐出国外
n. 侨民；移居国外者
adj. 移居国外的；被逐出国外的
words.ex: He decided to expatriate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他决定移居加拿大以追求更好的生活。
words.en: An expatriate is someone who lives in a country that is not their own, often for work or political reasons.

words.ex: The spy practiced espionage to get secret information.
words.ex_cn: 间谍从事间谍活动以获取秘密信息。
words.en: The practice of spying or of using spies, typically by governments to obtain political and military information.

words.tr: n. 小型爵士乐队；结合物
words.ex: The combo played jazz at the small club last night.
words.ex_cn: 这个小型爵士乐队昨晚在小俱乐部演奏了爵士乐。
words.en: A combo is a small group of musicians who play jazz, dance, or popular music together.

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.ex: They deride him for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他们嘲笑他穿旧衣服。
words.en: If you deride someone or something, you say that they are stupid or have no value.

words.tr: n. 前奏曲；主动表示；提议；提案
words.ex: The orchestra played a soft overture before the show.
words.ex_cn: 演出开始前，管弦乐队演奏了一段轻柔的序曲。
words.en: An overture is a piece of music played by an orchestra at the beginning of an opera or ballet, or a suggestion or approach made to someone with the aim of opening negotiations or establishing a relationship.

words.tr: n. 友好关系的恢复；和解
words.ex: The two countries began rapprochement after the war.
words.ex_cn: 两国在战争后开始和解。
words.en: An establishment or resumption of harmonious relations between two countries or groups.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.ex: He is a connoisseur of fine wine.
words.ex_cn: 他是优质葡萄酒的行家。
words.en: A connoisseur is a person who is especially competent to pass critical judgments in an art, particularly one of the fine arts, or in matters of taste.

words.ex: He never disparages his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他从不贬低他的同学。
words.en: If you disparage someone or something, you speak about them in a way which shows that you do not have a good opinion of them.

words.ex: The cooper made wooden barrels by hand.
words.ex_cn: 这位箍桶匠手工制作木桶。
words.en: A cooper is a person who makes or repairs barrels and casks.

words.ex: The farmer used a drone to check his crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民用无人驾驶飞机检查他的庄稼。
words.en: A drone is a male bee that does not work and exists solely to mate with the queen bee. It can also refer to an unmanned aircraft or ship guided by remote control or onboard computers. Additionally, 'drone' can describe a continuous low humming sound or to speak in a monotonous tone.

words.tr:
n. 胆汁；胆量；怨恨；磨伤
v. 使愤怒（尤指因不公平引起）
words.ex: The bitter gall made him feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 苦涩的胆汁让他感到恶心。
words.en: Gall can refer to a bitter liquid produced by the liver, or it can describe someone's boldness or impudence. It can also mean to irritate or annoy someone.

words.ex: He extols the beauty of nature every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天赞美大自然的美。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.ex: The park is within the precinct of the city center.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园位于市中心的范围内。
words.en: A precinct is a part of a city or town that has its own police force, or a division of a city for police or voting purposes.

words.tr: n. 慈善；博爱；慈善事业
words.ex: He gives money to charity because of his philanthropy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为慈善精神而捐钱给慈善机构。
words.en: Philanthropy is the act of donating money, goods, time, or effort to support a charitable cause, usually over an extended period of time and in regard to a defined objective.

words.ex: He is a maverick who always does things his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是按自己方式做事的独行其是者。
words.en: If you describe someone as a maverick, you mean that they are unconventional and independent, and do not think or behave in the same way as other people.

words.tr:
n. 幼鹿；浅黄褐色
v. 奉承；讨好
words.ex: The forest was filled with the sounds of baby fawns.
words.ex_cn: 森林里充满了幼鹿的叫声。
words.en: If someone fawns over you, they flatter you and show you too much attention.

words.ex: In some countries, caste determines a person's job and social status.
words.ex_cn: 在一些国家，社会等级决定一个人的职业和社会地位。
words.en: A caste is one of the traditional social classes into which people are divided in a Hindu society.

words.ex: The choreographer taught the dancers new moves.
words.ex_cn: 舞蹈指导教舞者新的动作。
words.en: A choreographer is a person who designs and directs the dance movements in a ballet, show, or film.

words.tr:
n. 松鸡；松鸡肉；怨言；牢骚
v. 抱怨；发牢骚
words.ex: The hunter saw a grouse in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎人在森林里看到一只松鸡。
words.en: A grouse is a bird with a plump body and feathered legs, belonging to the family Tetraonidae. As a verb, to grouse means to complain or grumble.

words.tr: adj. 难以控制的；任性的；捉摸不定的
words.ex: The wayward child refused to listen to his parents.
words.ex_cn: 这个任性的孩子不肯听父母的话。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as wayward, you mean that they behave in a selfish, bad, or unpredictable way, and are difficult to control.

words.tr:
adj. 苛刻的；尖刻的
v. 损伤；伤害；“scathe”的现在分词
words.ex: The critic wrote a scathing review of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 评论家写了一篇尖刻的电影评论。
words.en: If you say that someone is being scathing about something, you mean that they are being very critical of it.

words.tr:
n. 额外费用；附加费
v. 额外索价；附加罚款
words.ex: He paid a surcharge for extra baggage.
words.ex_cn: 他为额外行李支付了附加费。
words.en: An additional charge or payment.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；（猪等）打呼噜
n. 咕哝；呼噜声
words.ex: He grunted when he lifted the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他搬起沉重的箱子时咕哝了一声。
words.en: To make a low, short guttural sound, typically to express dissatisfaction or effort.

words.ex: He insinuated that she was lying.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她在撒谎。
words.en: If you say that someone insinuates that something bad is the case, you mean that they say it in an indirect way.

words.tr: adj. 自鸣得意的；沾沾自喜的
words.ex: He smiled in a smug way after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后得意地笑了。
words.en: If you say that someone is smug, you are criticizing the fact they seem very pleased with how good, clever, or lucky they are.

words.tr: v. 逐步渗透；逐渐灌输
words.ex: Parents try to instill good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To instill something in someone means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in their mind.

words.tr: n. 紧缩；艰苦朴素；节俭
words.ex: The government implemented austerity measures to reduce the budget deficit.
words.ex_cn: 政府实施了紧缩措施以减少预算赤字。
words.en: Austerity is a situation in which people's living standards are reduced because of economic difficulties.

words.ex: He showed civility even when he was angry.
words.ex_cn: 即使他生气了，他依然表现出礼貌。
words.en: Civility is polite, reasonable, and respectful behaviour.

words.ex: The teacher lauded the student for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 老师称赞了这名学生努力学习。
words.en: If people laud someone, they praise and admire them.

words.ex: He is a Nobel laureate for his poetry.
words.ex_cn: 他因诗歌而获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: A laureate is someone who has been given a prize or honor for achievement in a particular field, especially in the arts or sciences.

words.tr:
adj. 有害的；恶意的
v. 中伤；污蔑
words.ex: The virus is malign and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒是有害的，并且传播迅速。
words.en: If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them. If something is malign, it is harmful or evil.

words.tr: adj. 无害的；无冒犯之意的
words.ex: The comment was innocuous and didn't upset anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个评论无害，没有惹恼任何人。
words.en: Something that is innocuous is not harmful or offensive.

words.ex: The government issued a communique about the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 政府发布了一份关于新政策的公告。
words.en: An official announcement or statement, especially one made to the media.

words.tr:
v. 唠叨；喋喋不休；不断困扰
n. 老马；驽马；矮小马
words.ex: She nagged him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 她不停地催他打扫房间。
words.en: If someone nags you, they keep asking you to do something you have not done yet or do not want to do.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.tr:
v. 献出；拿出；提供
n. 献出；拿出；提供
words.ex: He proffered a cup of tea to his guest.
words.ex_cn: 他递给客人一杯茶。
words.en: If you proffer something to someone, you offer it to them for acceptance.

words.tr: n. 基本原理；基础理论；
words.ex: The rationale for the new rule is to save time.
words.ex_cn: 这个新规则的基本原理是节省时间。
words.en: The fundamental reasons or logical basis for a course of action or belief.

words.tr:
n. 避孕药；避孕用具
adj. 避孕的
words.ex: She uses a contraceptive to avoid pregnancy.
words.ex_cn: 她使用避孕药来避免怀孕。
words.en: A contraceptive is a device or drug used to prevent pregnancy.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；激昂地说
n. 喧闹的话；夸口话；叫喊
words.ex: He went on a rant about bad service.
words.ex_cn: 他大肆抱怨服务很差。
words.en: To speak or write in an angry or violent manner, often for a long time.

words.ex: He sued him for defamation after the false story was published.
words.ex_cn: 虚假报道发布后，他因诽谤起诉了他。
words.en: Defamation is the act of damaging someone's good reputation by saying or writing bad things about them that are not true.

words.tr:
n. 申斥；谴责
v. 斥责；训斥
words.ex: The teacher gave him a reprimand for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而训斥了他。
words.en: A reprimand is a formal or official expression of disapproval, typically by a person in authority.

words.tr: adj. 不直接的；不正直的；迂回的；
words.ex: He gave a devious answer to avoid telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不直接的回答，以避免说出真相。
words.en: If you describe someone as devious, you mean that they are dishonest and unfair in the way that they behave, often by using indirect methods to achieve their aims.

words.ex: He was reviled by his opponents for his controversial views.
words.ex_cn: 由于他的有争议的观点，他受到了对手的辱骂。
words.en: To revile someone means to criticize them in an abusive or angrily insulting manner.

words.ex: He had the audacity to lie to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他竟敢对老板撒谎。
words.en: Audacity is the willingness to take bold risks, often in a way that shocks or surprises people.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.tr:
n. 服药过量；嗑药过量；过量
v. （使）服药过量；过量…
words.ex: He took an overdose of pills and went to hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他服用了过量的药片，被送到了医院。
words.en: An overdose is the taking of too much of a drug, which can cause serious harm or death.

words.ex: He was punished for plagiarism in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他因论文剽窃而受到惩罚。
words.en: Plagiarism is the practice of using or copying someone else's idea or work and pretending that you thought of it or created it.

words.tr:
n. 喷溅声；劈啪声；急语；咕哝
v. 唾沫飞溅；发噼啪声；语无伦次地说
words.ex: The engine sputtered and then died.
words.ex_cn: 发动机发出劈啪声然后熄火了。
words.en: If something sputters, it makes a series of short, sharp noises, or if a person sputters, they speak in a series of short, unclear sounds because they are angry, surprised, or confused.

words.tr:
n. 争吵
v. 争吵
words.ex: The two boys squabble over toys every day.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天为玩具争吵。
words.en: A squabble is a noisy disagreement about something unimportant.

words.ex: He was diagnosed with dementia last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被诊断出患有痴呆。
words.en: Dementia is a condition characterized by progressive or persistent loss of intellectual functioning, especially memory impairment, often associated with aging.

words.tr:
n. 甜食；好东西；佳品
int. （儿语）好哇
words.ex: The children love eating goody after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢在晚饭后吃甜食。
words.en: A goody is something that is pleasant or attractive, especially something nice to eat.

words.tr:
n. 长声尖叫；长而尖的声音
v. 尖声长叫
words.ex: The child let out a loud squeal when she saw the spider.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子看到蜘蛛时，发出了一声长长的尖叫。
words.en: If someone or something squeals, they make a long, high-pitched sound.

words.ex: The elf lives in a small tree house.
words.ex_cn: 精灵住在一间小树屋里。
words.en: In folklore, an elf is a type of supernatural being in Germanic mythology and folklore. Elves are often depicted as youthful-seeming men and women of great beauty living in forests and other natural places, underground, or in wells and springs.

words.tr: n. 愤世嫉俗者；悲观者；怀疑者
words.ex: He is a cynic who never believes in good intentions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不相信任何善意的愤世嫉俗者。
words.en: A cynic is someone who believes that people are motivated purely by self-interest rather than acting for honorable or unselfish reasons.

words.ex: He taunted his brother for losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他奚落弟弟比赛输了。
words.en: If someone taunts you, they say unkind or insulting things to you, especially about your weaknesses or failures.

words.tr:
n. 粪便；废话；质量差的东西
v. 排便
words.ex: The dog left crap on the grass.
words.ex_cn: 狗在草地上拉了粪便。
words.en: If you describe something as crap, you think that it is of very poor quality.

words.tr: v. 兜售；招徕；吹捧；倒卖（高价票）
words.ex: He touts the new phone as the best on the market.
words.ex_cn: 他吹捧这款新手机是市场上最好的。
words.en: If someone touts something, they try to sell it or convince people that it is good, especially in an aggressive or exaggerated way.

words.tr:
adj. 镇静的；镇定的；止痛的
n. 镇静剂；止痛药
words.ex: The doctor gave her a sedative pill to calm her down.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了她一颗镇静药片来让她平静下来。
words.en: A sedative is a drug that calms you down or makes you sleep.

words.tr: adj. 呼吸的；与呼吸有关的；
words.ex: The respiratory system helps us breathe.
words.ex_cn: 呼吸系统帮助我们呼吸。
words.en: Relating to or affecting respiration or the organs of respiration.

words.ex: At first, he did not like math.
words.ex_cn: 起初，他不喜欢数学。
words.en: At the beginning; initially.

words.tr:
adj. 秘密的；隐蔽的
n. （动物可藏身的）小树丛
words.ex: He made a covert plan to leave without telling anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他秘密制定了一个不告诉任何人就离开的计划。
words.en: Covert activities or situations are secret or hidden.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.ex: They unearthed an old coin in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们在花园里挖出了一枚旧硬币。
words.en: To unearth something means to find it by digging in the ground or to discover something that was hidden or unknown.

chapters.name: Level 11 动作类动词

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.ex: The soldiers were bombarded with cannon fire.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们遭到炮火轰击。
words.en: To bombard someone or something means to attack them continuously with bombs, shells, or other missiles. It can also mean to subject someone to a lot of something, such as questions or information.

words.ex: The squadron flew over the city at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 中队在黎明时飞过城市。
words.en: A squadron is a principal subdivision of an armored or cavalry regiment, consisting of two or more troops, companies, or batteries.

words.tr:
adj. 吵闹的；粗暴的
n. 凶暴的人；无赖
words.ex: The rowdy kids made noise in the library.
words.ex_cn: 那些吵闹的孩子在图书馆里制造噪音。
words.en: If you describe someone as rowdy, you mean that they are noisy, rough, and likely to cause trouble.

words.tr:
v. 挥；舞动；炫耀地显示
n. 挥舞
words.ex: He brandished a knife to scare the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他挥舞着一把刀吓唬小偷。
words.en: If you brandish something, especially a weapon, you wave it about in a threatening way.

words.ex: The farmer used a sickle to cut the wheat.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用镰刀割小麦。
words.en: A tool with a curved blade used for cutting crops such as wheat or grass.

words.tr:
adj. 偏僻的；离群的；孤独的；内向的
v. 撤回；撤退；“withdraw”的过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is in a withdrawn area, far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋位于一个偏僻的地方，远离城镇。
words.en: If someone is withdrawn, they are very quiet, and do not want to talk to other people. If something is withdrawn, it is taken back or removed.

words.ex: The goldsmith made a beautiful ring.
words.ex_cn: 金匠做了一个漂亮的戒指。
words.en: A goldsmith is a person who makes, repairs, or sells articles made of gold.

words.tr:
v. 擦亮；磨光
n. 光泽
words.ex: He burnishes the old metal every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末都抛光那块旧金属。
words.en: To burnish something means to polish it and make it shine by rubbing it.

words.ex: The rodent ran quickly across the floor.
words.ex_cn: 这只啮齿动物迅速跑过地板。
words.en: A rodent is a small mammal which has sharp front teeth that it uses for gnawing. Rodents include rats, mice, and squirrels.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.tr: n. 木兰；玉兰类的植物
words.ex: The magnolia tree blooms in spring.
words.ex_cn: 玉兰树在春天开花。
words.en: A magnolia is a type of tree or shrub that has large, usually white or pink flowers. It is widely grown for its beauty and fragrance.

words.ex: The wizard conjure a fireball with ancient words.
words.ex_cn: 巫师用古老的咒语召唤出一个火球。
words.en: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

words.ex: The jay flew over the tree.
words.ex_cn: 松鸦飞过了树。
words.en: A jay is a noisy bird with brightly colored feathers, known for its loud calls and chatter.

words.ex: He raised his stein in a toast to the bride.
words.ex_cn: 他举起啤酒杯向新娘祝酒。
words.en: A stein is a large mug, typically made of earthenware, used for drinking beer.

words.ex: He crumpled the paper in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他把纸揉皱了。
words.en: If you crumple something such as paper or cloth, or if it crumples, it is squashed and becomes full of untidy creases and folds.

words.ex: She chose a delicate lace lingerie set for her wedding night.
words.ex_cn: 她为新婚之夜挑选了一套精致的蕾丝内衣。
words.en: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes, especially items made of lightweight, decorative fabric.

words.tr:
n. 布帘；垂下的褶皱状
v. 盖上褶缀的布；将（织物）悬挂；懒散地垂着
words.ex: The blue drape covered the window completely.
words.ex_cn: 蓝色的布帘完全遮住了窗户。
words.en: To drape something means to arrange it in a loose, flowing way, especially fabric or clothing.

words.ex: The commando unit executed a daring night raid.
words.ex_cn: 突击队实施了一次大胆的夜间突袭。
words.en: A commando is a soldier who is specially trained to carry out quick and dangerous military operations.

words.tr: n. 国家或组织的法定歌曲
words.ex: The team sang the national anthem before the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛前，球队唱了国歌。
words.en: An anthem is a song that is used to represent a particular nation, society, or group and that is sung on special occasions.

words.ex: Everyone stood still when they played the national anthem.
words.ex_cn: 当播放国歌时，所有人都静静地站着。
words.en: A song that is officially adopted by a country as an expression of national identity and pride, typically performed at public and ceremonial occasions.

words.tr:
v. 疏浚；挖掘
n. 挖泥船；疏浚机
words.ex: They dredge the river to remove mud.
words.ex_cn: 他们疏浚河流以清除淤泥。
words.en: To dredge means to remove mud, sand, or other material from the bottom of a river, lake, etc., in order to make it deeper or to search for something.

words.ex: The scavengers fed on the carcass of the dead deer.
words.ex_cn: 食腐动物以那只死鹿的尸体为食。
words.en: The dead body of an animal, especially one that is ready to be cut up as meat or eaten by animals.

words.ex: He got pneumonia after a bad cold.
words.ex_cn: 他得了重感冒后患了肺炎。
words.en: Pneumonia is a serious disease which affects your lungs and makes it difficult for you to breathe.

words.ex: He exhale slowly after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后慢慢呼出气。
words.en: To exhale means to breathe out air from your lungs.

words.ex: He suffers from a bad cold.
words.ex_cn: 他患了重感冒。
words.en: If you suffer from an illness or from a medical condition, you are badly affected by it.

words.ex: The tenor of his speech was positive.
words.ex_cn: 他演讲的大意是积极的。
words.en: The tenor of something such as a speech or piece of writing is its general meaning or the general attitude expressed in it.

words.tr:
n. 小提琴；骗局
v. 摆弄；虚度时光；拉小提琴；篡改
words.ex: He bought a fiddle at the music shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在音乐店买了一把小提琴。
words.en: A fiddle is a musical instrument with strings that you play with a bow. It is the same as a violin.

words.ex: He fondled the old photo gently.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻抚摸着那张旧照片。
words.en: To handle or touch (someone or something) in a tender and loving way.

words.ex: The irate customer shouted at the clerk.
words.ex_cn: 这位愤怒的顾客对店员大喊大叫。
words.en: If someone is irate, they are very angry about something.

words.tr:
v. 断然拒绝
n. 粗暴回绝；生硬的拒绝
words.ex: He rebuffed her offer with a shake of his head.
words.ex_cn: 他摇了摇头，拒绝了她的提议。
words.en: If you rebuff someone or rebuff a suggestion that they make, you refuse to do what they suggest.

words.tr: phrase. 遭遇；经历；与…会面；与…会晤
words.ex: I will meet with my teacher tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天要和我的老师见面。
words.en: To have a meeting or discussion with someone, often for a specific purpose.

words.tr: n. 飞地；被包围的领土
words.ex: The village is an enclave surrounded by forest.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄是一个被森林包围的飞地。
words.en: An enclave is a part of a country or a group of people that is surrounded by another country or group of people.

words.ex: The village held a gala to celebrate the harvest.
words.ex_cn: 村庄举办了一个节日来庆祝丰收。
words.en: A gala is a special public celebration, entertainment, performance, or festival.

words.tr:
v. 嬉戏
n. 嬉戏；欢乐的活动
words.ex: The children were frolicking in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里嬉戏。
words.en: If people or animals frolic, they play or move in a lively, happy way.

words.tr:
n. 决斗
v. 决斗；使（另一人）参加决斗
words.ex: The two knights prepared for a duel.
words.ex_cn: 两位骑士准备决斗。
words.en: A duel is a formal fight between two people in which they use weapons, especially in order to settle a quarrel.

words.tr: v. 幸灾乐祸；沾沾自喜；满足地看
words.ex: He gloats when his rival loses the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的对手输掉比赛时，他幸灾乐祸。
words.en: To gloat means to observe or think about something with triumphant and often malicious satisfaction, gratification, or delight.

words.ex: The child played with a wooden cube.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩了一个木制立方体。
words.en: A cube is a solid object with six square faces which are all the same size.

words.ex: The mouse is gnawing on the wood.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠正在啃木头。
words.en: To gnaw means to bite or chew something persistently, especially something hard, or to cause persistent worry or discomfort.

words.tr: n. 雌鹿（或雌兔、雌羚羊等）
words.ex: The doe drank water by the forest.
words.ex_cn: 母鹿在森林边喝水。
words.en: A doe is an adult female deer, rabbit, or hare.

words.tr: adj. 不守规矩的；难控制的；难管束的
words.ex: The unruly child refused to sit quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这个不守规矩的孩子不肯安静地坐着。
words.en: If you describe people, especially children, as unruly, you mean that they behave badly and are difficult to control.

words.ex: He is grappled with the math problem for hours.
words.ex_cn: 他花了好几个小时努力解决这道数学题。
words.en: To grapple with something means to try hard to understand or deal with a difficult problem or subject.

words.ex: He gropped in the dark for the light switch.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中摸索着找电灯开关。
words.en: If you grope for something that you cannot see, you try to find it by moving your hands around in order to feel it.

words.ex: The king kept gold in his coffer.
words.ex_cn: 国王把黄金存放在他的金库中。
words.en: A coffer is a large strong chest used for storing valuable objects such as money or gold.

words.tr:
n. 手铐；思想上的桎梏
v. 用手铐铐住（某人）；把（某人）铐在（某物、某人）上；限制
words.ex: The police put handcuff on the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察给小偷戴上了手铐。
words.en: A handcuff is a pair of lockable linked metal rings for securing a prisoner's wrists.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.ex: The thug stole the wallet from the man.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍从那人身上偷了钱包。
words.en: A thug is a violent person, especially a criminal.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把（某人）带走；引开；使分心
words.ex: The teacher will lead away the students for the field trip.
words.ex_cn: 老师将带学生们离开去参加实地考察。
words.en: To take someone or something away from a place or situation, often by guiding or directing them.

words.ex: The asteroid flew past Earth safely.
words.ex_cn: 这颗小行星安全地从地球旁飞过。
words.en: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun. Large numbers of these, ranging enormously in size, are found between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, though some have more eccentric orbits.

words.tr: v. 猛冲；猛投；猛烈碰撞
words.ex: The car hurtled down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 汽车飞速冲下山坡。
words.en: If someone or something hurtles somewhere, they move there very quickly, often in a uncontrolled way.

words.ex: The platoon was deployed to the front line.
words.ex_cn: 该排被部署到前线。
words.en: A platoon is a military unit typically consisting of two or more squads, sections, or patrols. It is usually commanded by a lieutenant and is part of a company.

words.tr: n. 弹幕射击；掩护炮火；拦河坝
words.ex: The soldiers faced a barrage of bullets.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们面对着一阵弹雨。
words.en: A barrage is a heavy and continuous bombardment of gunfire or a dam built across a river to control the flow of water.

words.ex: The hustle of the market filled the morning air.
words.ex_cn: 市场的熙攘充满了清晨的空气。
words.en: If you hustle, you work hard to do something quickly, especially in order to earn money.

words.ex: The castle was a stronghold against invaders.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是抵御入侵者的要塞。
words.en: A stronghold is a place that is well protected and difficult to attack, often used by a military force or a group with a particular interest or belief.

words.tr:
adj. 要求严格的；要求小心仔细的；苛求的
v. 强求；急需；要求；“exact”的现在分词
words.ex: He is an exacting teacher who wants perfect work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个要求严格的老师，要求完美无缺的作业。
words.en: requiring a lot of effort, care, or attention

words.ex: The dentist placed a dental implant to replace the missing tooth.
words.ex_cn: 牙医植入了一个牙科植入物来替代缺失的牙齿。
words.en: To implant something means to put it firmly into something else, especially into a person's body.

words.tr:
n. 方法；接近；靠近；路径；
v. 接近；靠近；临近；处理；
words.ex: He used a new approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一种新方法来解决问题。
words.en: To come near or nearer to something or someone in distance or time.

words.tr: v. 大批出没于；成群滋扰；遍布于；寄生
words.ex: The bugs infest the old house.
words.ex_cn: 这些虫子侵袭了这栋老房子。
words.en: If creatures such as insects or rats infest a place, they are present in large numbers and usually cause damage or disease.

words.tr: n. 大型废弃物；巨大笨重的人（物）
words.ex: The old boat was left as a hulk on the shore.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船被遗弃在岸边，成为了一堆大型废弃物。
words.en: A hulk is a large, clumsy, or old ship that is no longer in use and is often left to decay in a harbor.

words.ex: The township has a small school and a post office.
words.ex_cn: 这个乡镇有一所小学和一个邮局。
words.en: A township is a division of a county with some corporate powers.

words.ex: He inhale the fresh air in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他早上吸入新鲜空气。
words.en: To inhale means to breathe in air, smoke, or gas.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr:
v. 刺；戳；捅；用拳猛击
n. 刺；戳；捅；猛击
words.ex: He gave a quick jab to his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他给了对手一记快速的刺拳。
words.en: To poke or thrust sharply; to make a quick, sharp punch.

words.ex: He has arthritis in his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手有关节炎。
words.en: Arthritis is a medical condition in which the joints in someone's body are swollen and painful.

words.ex: He adds sodium to his food for taste.
words.ex_cn: 他为了味道在食物里加钠。
words.en: Sodium is a soft, silvery-white, highly reactive metal. Sodium is an alkali metal, being in group 1 of the periodic table, because it has a single electron in its outer shell that it readily donates, creating a positively charged ion—the Na⁺ cation.

words.tr:
v. 过滤；滤去；渗入
n. 过滤；滤去
words.ex: The soil is leached of nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 土壤中的养分被过滤掉了。
words.en: To leach means to remove or be removed from a substance by a percolating liquid, especially to remove soluble constituents from soil, ash, or similar material by the action of percolating water.

words.ex: The city cleaned the sewage from the streets.
words.ex_cn: 城市清理了街道上的污水。
words.en: Sewage is waste matter such as faeces or dirty water from homes and factories, which flows away through sewers.

words.ex: The deterioration of the road made driving dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 道路的恶化使驾驶变得危险。
words.en: The process of becoming progressively worse.

words.ex: There is a blob of ink on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 纸上有一团墨水。
words.en: A small drop of a thick liquid or viscous substance.

words.tr:
n. 尖木桩；警戒哨；纠察队（队员）
v. 进行罢工纠察
words.ex: The fence has wooden pickets to keep animals out.
words.ex_cn: 这个围栏有木制尖木桩，用来防止动物进入。
words.en: A picket is a person or group of people who stand outside a place of work or other venue to protest or to try to persuade others not to enter during a strike. It can also refer to a pointed stake or post driven into the ground, typically to form a fence or to tether a horse.

words.tr: phrase. 一种释放催泪气体的爆炸装置，用于驱散人群
words.ex: The police threw a tear gas grenade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察扔了一枚催泪弹来阻止人群。
words.en: A grenade designed to release tear gas, used especially by the police or military to control crowds or disperse riots.

words.ex: Noah built an ark to save animals from the flood.
words.ex_cn: 诺亚建造了一艘方舟来拯救动物免受洪水之灾。
words.en: An ark is a large boat mentioned in the Bible, built by Noah to save his family and two of every kind of animal from the Flood.

words.tr:
n. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
v. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
words.ex: The boat made a sudden lurch to the left.
words.ex_cn: 船突然向左倾斜。
words.en: If you lurch, you move suddenly and uncontrollably in one direction.

words.tr:
n. 大洪水；暴雨；泛滥
v. 泛滥；大量涌入
words.ex: The rain caused a deluge in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨在镇上引发了洪水。
words.en: A deluge is a severe flood or a very heavy fall of rain that causes a lot of damage.

words.tr: n. 诺亚（男子名，也指《圣经》中的诺亚方舟故事中的主人公）
words.ex: Noah built a big boat to save animals.
words.ex_cn: 诺亚造了一条大船来拯救动物。
words.en: A male given name, from the Hebrew 'Noach', meaning 'rest' or 'comfort'.

words.tr: adj. 繁重而累人的；艰苦的；使人精疲力尽的
words.ex: He ran a grueling marathon last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他上周日跑了一场艰苦的马拉松。
words.en: A grueling activity is extremely difficult and tiring, often continuing for a long time.

words.tr: v. 安顿；安居；安卧；坐落于
words.ex: The baby nestles close to her mother.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿依偎在妈妈身边。
words.en: To settle or lie comfortably within or against something.

words.tr:
v. 轻咬；啃；一点点地吃
n. 一小口；轻咬；少量
words.ex: The dog nibble the biscuit slowly.
words.ex_cn: 狗慢慢地轻咬着饼干。
words.en: To nibble means to take small bites of something, especially food.

words.tr: adj. 坚果味的；含果仁的；多坚果的；狂热的；发疯的
words.ex: He ate a nutty granola bar for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一块坚果味的格兰诺拉麦片棒。
words.en: 1. Containing nuts or tasting of nuts. 2. Crazy or eccentric.

words.ex: He ate a bun for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一个面包卷。
words.en: A bun is a small, usually round piece of bread. It can also refer to a hairstyle in which the hair is gathered into a tight coil or knot at the back of the head.

words.tr:
v. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
n. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
words.ex: He gave me a nudge to start the project.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻推了我一下，让我开始这个项目。
words.en: If you nudge someone, you push them gently, usually with your elbow, in order to draw their attention to something.

words.tr:
n. 教堂的长凳式座位；座位
v. 排座位
words.ex: He sat on a wooden pew in the church.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在教堂里的木长椅上。
words.en: A long bench with a back, placed in rows in the main part of some churches to seat the congregation.

words.ex: He got a blister on his foot from new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 他新鞋磨出了一个水泡。
words.en: A blister is a small pocket of fluid within the upper layers of the skin, typically caused by forceful rubbing, burning, freezing, chemical exposure or infection. As a verb, it means to form such a pocket of fluid.

words.ex: The glass is translucent, so you can see light through it.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃是半透明的，所以你能看到光透过它。
words.en: If a material or substance is translucent, it is almost transparent, allowing some light to pass through it but not detailed shapes.

words.tr:
v. 渗出；流出；分泌出
n. 软泥；淤泥；泥浆
words.ex: Mud is oozing from the hole.
words.ex_cn: 泥巴正从洞里渗出来。
words.en: If a liquid oozes from something or if something oozes a liquid, the liquid flows from it slowly and in small quantities.

words.tr:
n. （高尔夫球）轻击
v. 以推杆推球；轻轻一击
words.ex: He managed to putt the ball into the hole on the last stroke.
words.ex_cn: 他在最后一击成功地将球轻击入洞。
words.en: In golf, a putt is a gentle stroke that you make when the ball is on the short grass near the hole, in order to get the ball into the hole.

words.ex: The building has a strong footing on solid ground.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑坐落在坚固的地基上。
words.en: The term 'footing' refers to the basis or foundation on which something is established or the relationship between people or groups.

words.tr:
n. 雄性种兽；（古语）陛下
v. 繁殖；成为父亲
words.ex: The king's sire was a wise ruler.
words.ex_cn: 国王的父亲是一位英明的统治者。
words.en: A sire is a term used to refer to a male parent of a child or animal, especially a horse. It can also be used as a title of respect for a king or other male ruler.

words.ex: The colt runs fast across the field.
words.ex_cn: 小马在田野上快速奔跑。
words.en: A colt is a young male horse, especially one that is less than four years old.

words.tr:
v. 玩闹；轻易地取得胜利
n. 嬉闹；贪玩的人
words.ex: The children romped in the playground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在操场上嬉戏玩耍。
words.en: To play roughly and energetically; to win easily.

words.ex: The battalion marched slowly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 那个营缓缓穿过小镇。
words.en: A battalion is a large group of soldiers that consists of three or more companies.

words.ex: He used to rove through the forests when he was young.
words.ex_cn: 他年轻时常常在森林里漫游。
words.en: To rove means to travel constantly without a fixed destination; wander.

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.tr:
n. 叛徒；变节者；叛教者
adj. 背叛的；变节的
v. 背叛
words.ex: He is a renegade who left the team suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个突然离开团队的叛徒。
words.en: A renegade is a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles.

words.tr:
n. 嘲笑；嘲弄
v. 嘲笑；狼吞虎咽
words.ex: His joke received a scoff from the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话引来了人群的嘲笑。
words.en: If you scoff at something, you speak about it in a way that shows you think it is ridiculous or inadequate.

words.ex: The ancient people worshipped a sun deity.
words.ex_cn: 古人崇拜太阳神。
words.en: A deity is a god or goddess, or anything revered as divine.

words.tr:
n. 尖叫声；尖锐的声音
v. 发出尖锐刺耳的声音
words.ex: The cat let out a loud screech.
words.ex_cn: 猫发出了一声尖叫声。
words.en: If a vehicle screeches, its wheels make a high-pitched noise as it moves along or stops.

words.ex: The movie showed a gruesome accident.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一起令人毛骨悚然的事故。
words.en: Something that is gruesome is extremely unpleasant and shocking, especially because it involves death or injury.

words.ex: The farmer shears sheep every spring.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每年春天给羊剪毛。
words.en: To shear means to cut the wool off a sheep or to cut or trim something with scissors or shears.

words.ex: He works as a teacher but his sideline is selling handmade crafts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名教师，但他的副业是卖手工制品。
words.en: A sideline is an activity that you do in addition to your main job in order to earn extra money.

words.ex: The epitaph on his grave says, 'Beloved father and friend.'
words.ex_cn: 他墓碑上的墓志铭写着：‘受人爱戴的父亲和朋友。’
words.en: An epitaph is a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone.

words.tr:
v. 没精打采地站（或坐、走）；低头垂肩地站（或坐、走）
n. 没精打采的样子
words.ex: He slouches in his chair while watching TV.
words.ex_cn: 他看电视时驼背坐着。
words.en: If someone slouches, they sit or stand with their shoulders and head bent so that they look lazy and tired.

words.tr: phrase. +n. 绝望地；陷入绝望；在绝望中
words.ex: He gave up in despair after many failed attempts.
words.ex_cn: 多次尝试失败后，他绝望地放弃了。
words.en: In a state of despair means to have lost all hope, feeling very sad and helpless.

words.ex: The police arrested the pimp who controlled several sex workers.
words.ex_cn: 警察逮捕了控制多名性工作者的男妓。
words.en: A pimp is a man who controls prostitutes and arranges clients for them, taking part of their earnings in return.

words.tr:
n. 傻笑；假笑
v. 傻笑；自鸣得意地笑
words.ex: He gave a smirk when he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛时露出了冷笑。
words.en: A smirk is a smile expressing smugness or scorn instead of pleasure.

words.ex: The brawl started over a simple misunderstanding.
words.ex_cn: 这场争吵源于一个简单的误解。
words.en: A brawl is a rough or noisy fight or quarrel.

words.ex: The panther walks quietly through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 美洲豹静静地穿过森林。
