words.en: An assortment is a group of similar things that are of different types or sizes.

words.tr: n. 祸根；致命伤；烦扰之源；
words.ex: Smoking is the bane of his health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是他健康的祸根。
words.en: Something that causes misery or death.

words.ex: He put up new decor for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对布置了新的装饰。
words.en: The style of decoration and furnishing of a room or building.

words.tr: n. 摧毁；拆毁；拆除；大败；
words.ex: The demolition of the old building started last week.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧楼的拆除上周开始了。
words.en: The act of demolishing something, especially a building.

words.tr: v. 强迫；“force”的现在分词； n. 催熟；
words.ex: They were forcing him to work late.
words.ex_cn: 他们强迫他加班。
words.en: Forcing refers to the act of making someone do something against their will, often using threats or physical power.

words.ex: The fragmentation of the market makes it hard to control.
words.ex_cn: 市场的碎片化使得它难以控制。
words.en: The process or state of breaking or being broken into small or separate parts.

words.ex: The walls had colorful graffiti on them.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有着五颜六色的涂画。
words.en: Graffiti is words or pictures that are written or drawn in public places, for example on walls or posters.

words.ex: The city improved its power grid to handle more electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改进了其电力输送网，以承载更多的电力。
words.en: A grid is a pattern of straight lines that cross each other to form squares. It is used to help you draw or to help you find places on a map.

words.tr:
n. 麻烦；困难；争吵
v. 烦扰；纠缠
words.ex: It's not worth the hassle to change your plans.
words.ex_cn: 改变计划不值得这么麻烦。
words.en: If you describe something as a hassle, you mean that it is inconvenient and annoying. As a verb, to hassle someone means to annoy or trouble them persistently.

words.ex: With hindsight, I should have saved more money.
words.ex_cn: 事后看来，我本该多存些钱。
words.en: The understanding of a situation or event only after it has happened or developed.

words.ex: His incompetence caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的无能力导致项目失败。
words.en: If you refer to someone's incompetence, you are criticizing them because they are unable to do their job or a task properly.

words.ex: He has a knack for fixing bikes.
words.ex_cn: 他有修自行车的技巧。
words.en: A knack is a special skill or ability that someone has, especially one that is hard to explain or teach.

words.ex: His mannerism of tapping his fingers shows he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 他敲手指的行为特征表明他很紧张。
words.en: A mannerism is a particular habit or way of speaking or behaving that someone has, especially one that they have had for a long time and that has become characteristic of them.

words.ex: The party turned into an orgy of drinking and dancing.
words.ex_cn: 派对变成了饮酒跳舞的狂欢。
words.en: An orgy is a wild party or gathering where people behave in an unrestrained way, often involving excessive drinking, eating, or sexual activity.

words.tr:
n. 刺穿；刺孔
v. 刺穿；削弱
words.ex: The bike tire has a puncture.
words.ex_cn: 自行车轮胎有一个漏气孔。
words.en: A puncture is a small hole made by a sharp object, especially in a tire. To puncture something means to make a hole in it with a sharp object.

words.tr: n. 奇事；巧合；怪癖；奇行
words.ex: His habit of talking to his plants is a strange quirk.
words.ex_cn: 他跟植物说话的习惯是一个奇怪的奇事。
words.en: A quirk is a peculiar habit or aspect of a person's character, or an unexpected twist in a situation or story.

words.ex: They have good rapport with their students.
words.ex_cn: 他们与学生关系友好。
words.en: A friendly relationship in which people understand each other very well.

words.ex: He was eager to regain his lost respectability.
words.ex_cn: 他急切地想要恢复失去的名望。
words.en: The quality of being socially acceptable or respectable.

words.tr:
n. 灾难；祸患；鞭子
v. 鞭打；折磨；使受苦难
words.ex: Pollution is a scourge on the environment.
words.ex_cn: 污染是对环境的祸害。
words.en: A scourge is something that causes a lot of trouble or suffering, or a whip used as an instrument of punishment.

words.tr: n. 秘密行动；偷偷摸摸
words.ex: The cat moved in stealth to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫悄悄地移动去抓老鼠。
words.en: Stealth is the action of moving or behaving in a secretive way in order to avoid being noticed.

words.ex: He felt the stigma of being unemployed.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了失业的耻辱。
words.en: A stigma is a strong feeling of disapproval that most people in a society have about something, especially when this is unfair.

chapters.name: Level 11 名词 政治•经济•法律

words.ex: The man was arrested for arson.
words.ex_cn: 这名男子因纵火被逮捕。
words.en: The crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

words.ex: The actors stood in front of the backdrop with a mountain scene.
words.ex_cn: 演员们站在有山景的背景幕布前。
words.en: A backdrop is a large piece of cloth, often with scenery or buildings painted on it, that is hung at the back of a stage in a theatre.

words.ex: His bounty helped the poor family survive winter.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助这个贫困家庭度过了冬天。
words.en: If you say that someone is bountiful or does something in a bountiful way, you mean that they are very generous or that they give a lot of something.

words.ex: He was accused of complicity in the theft.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控参与了这起盗窃案。
words.en: Complicity is involvement with other people in an illegal activity or wrongdoing.

words.ex: The two countries formed a confederate alliance to defend their borders.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成了同盟联盟以保卫它们的边界。
words.en: A confederate is someone who works with others to achieve a common goal, often in a political or military context. It can also refer to a member of a confederation, which is a union of states or groups united for a common purpose.

words.tr: n. 偶然事故；意外事件
words.ex: He saved money for a contingency.
words.ex_cn: 他存钱以备不时之需。
words.en: A contingency is an event or situation that might happen in the future, especially one that could cause problems.

words.ex: The team's loss was a total debacle.
words.ex_cn: 球队的失败是一场彻底的惨败。
words.en: A debacle is a sudden and complete failure or collapse, often in a way that is very embarrassing or causes a lot of damage.

words.ex: There is a disparity in pay between men and women.
words.ex_cn: 男女之间的工资存在差异。
words.en: A disparity between two or more things is a noticeable difference between them.

words.ex: He tried evasion to avoid paying taxes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图逃避缴税。
words.en: The act of avoiding something that you are supposed to do or deal with.

words.ex: The country agreed to extradition of the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 该国同意引渡这名嫌疑人。
words.en: The act of officially sending someone back to their own country to be tried for a crime that they have been accused of in another country.

words.ex: The two families have a long feud.
words.ex_cn: 这两个家族有长期的世仇。
words.en: A feud is a prolonged and bitter quarrel or dispute, especially between two families or groups, often involving violence.

words.ex: The king issued a fiat to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王下达了一道命令来停止战争。
words.en: An authoritative or arbitrary order.

words.tr:
n. 供过于求；过量
v. 使充满；过量供应
words.ex: The market has a glut of cheap phones.
words.ex_cn: 市场上廉价手机泛滥。
words.en: An excessive supply of something, more than is needed, wanted, or can be used; to supply or fill to excess.

words.tr: n. （新法律或体系的）实施；不合理要求；麻烦
words.ex: The tax imposition made life harder for poor families.
words.ex_cn: 征税让贫困家庭的生活更加艰难。
words.en: The act of imposing something, such as a tax, duty, or law, especially in a way that is considered to be unfair or burdensome.

words.tr: n. 免于惩罚；不受惩处
words.ex: He stole the money and got away with it in impunity.
words.ex_cn: 他偷了钱，却逍遥法外。
words.en: If someone does something with impunity, they do it without fear of being punished for it.

words.ex: The infusion of new ideas has revitalized the company.
words.ex_cn: 新思想的注入使公司焕发了生机。
words.en: The process of steeping or soaking a substance in water or other liquid to extract its active principles.

words.ex: The law has a loophole that lets companies avoid taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律有一个漏洞，让公司可以避税。
words.en: A loophole is a small mistake in a law or set of rules which allows people to do something that would otherwise be illegal or not allowed.

words.tr: n. 身体不适；不快；萎靡不振；痼疾
words.ex: She felt a general malaise after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长途飞行后，她感到全身不适。
words.en: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease whose exact cause is difficult to identify.

words.ex: The middleman helped the buyer and seller agree on a price.
words.ex_cn: 中间人帮助买家和卖家达成了价格协议。
words.en: A middleman is a person who arranges business or political deals between other people.

words.ex: The company updated the payroll last Friday.
words.ex_cn: 公司上星期五更新了职工工资册。
words.en: A payroll is a list of employees and the amount of money they are to be paid, or the total amount of money paid to the employees of a company.

words.ex: He is on probation for one year.
words.ex_cn: 他被判缓刑一年。
words.en: Probation is a period of time during which someone who has committed a crime has to behave well and not commit any more crimes in order to avoid being sent to prison.

words.tr: n. （为军队或其他组织的）采购
words.ex: The army's procurement of food and fuel takes months.
words.ex_cn: 军队的食品和燃料采购需要数月时间。
words.en: Procurement is the act of obtaining or buying goods and services, often for a business or government.

words.ex: The kidnappers asked for a ransom of $1 million.
words.ex_cn: 绑匪要求一百万美元的赎金。
words.en: A ransom is the money that is demanded for the release of a person who has been kidnapped.

words.ex: He went to the registry to register his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他去登记处登记了他的新车。
words.en: A registry is an official list or record of people or things.

words.ex: The coach checks the roster before every game.
words.ex_cn: 教练在每场比赛前检查名单。
words.en: A roster is a list which gives details of the members of a team, organization, or group, and the times or order in which they are to perform a particular duty.

words.tr:
n. 记数；
v. 合计；
words.ex: He kept a tally of how many goals he scored.
words.ex_cn: 他记录了自己进了多少球。
words.en: A tally is a record of amounts or numbers which you keep changing and adding to as the activity which affects it progresses.

words.ex: He gave an ultimatum: leave now or stay forever.
words.ex_cn: 他发出最后通牒：现在走，或者永远留下。
words.en: An ultimatum is a final demand or statement of terms, the rejection of which will result in retaliation or a breakdown in relations.

words.ex: He felt vindication when the truth came out.
words.ex_cn: 当真相大白时，他感到被证实了。
words.en: Vindication is the act of proving that someone is not guilty of a crime or that something is true.

words.ex: He signed a waiver before the ride.
words.ex_cn: 他在坐过山车前签了免责协议。
words.en: A waiver is an official document or statement that gives up a right or claim, especially in legal contexts.

chapters.name: Level 11 名词 食物

words.ex: The farmer piled up fodder for the cows.
words.ex_cn: 农夫为奶牛堆了一堆饲料。
words.en: Fodder is food that is given to cows, horses, and other animals.

words.ex: He follows a strict regimen to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循严格的作息计划来保持健康。
words.en: A regimen is a systematic plan or course of action intended to improve or maintain health, or a prescribed routine of diet, exercise, or manner of living.

chapters.name: Level 11 名词 程度•单位

words.tr: n. 脱离常规；误差；偏差；失常
words.ex: The sudden rain was an aberration in the dry season.
words.ex_cn: 这场突如其来的雨是旱季中的异常现象。
words.en: An aberration is an instance of straying from the normal or usual way, or something that is unusual or unexpected.

words.tr: n. 异常事物；反常现象；
words.ex: The strange weather this month is an anomaly.
words.ex_cn: 这个月奇怪的天气是一个异常现象。
words.en: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.ex: The rifle has a 5.56 mm caliber.
words.ex_cn: 这把步枪的口径是5.56毫米。
words.en: The caliber of something or someone is their quality, especially when this is high.

words.tr: n. 关键部分；餐桌中央装饰品
words.ex: The fountain is the centerpiece of the park.
words.ex_cn: 喷泉是公园的关键部分。
words.en: The most important or attractive part or feature of something.

words.ex: He won the game with great finesse.
words.ex_cn: 他以高超的技巧赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you finesse something, you handle it in a skillful and often slightly deceptive way.

words.tr:
n. 微弱的闪光；微弱的迹象；一丝
v. 发出微弱的闪光
words.ex: I saw a glimmer of light in the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 我在黑暗的房间里看到一丝光亮。
words.en: A glimmer is a faint, wavering light or a slight indication or trace of something.

words.ex: The hallmark of a good teacher is patience.
words.ex_cn: 好老师的标志是耐心。
words.en: A hallmark is a distinctive characteristic or attribute that is typical of a particular person or thing.

words.ex: A horde of children ran to the ice cream truck.
words.ex_cn: 一群孩子跑向冰淇淋车。
words.en: A horde is a large group of people or animals, especially one that is moving or acting together.

words.ex: The parity of the numbers is important in this game.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的奇偶性在这个游戏中很重要。
words.en: If there is parity between two things, they are equal to each other.

words.ex: His rectitude in business dealings was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业交易中的正直是众所周知的。
words.en: Moral integrity; honesty and correctness of judgement or behaviour.

words.ex: The math proof requires rigor.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学证明需要严谨。
words.en: Rigor is a situation in which people are made to follow rules in a very strict way.

words.tr: n. 泛滥；猛涨；大批；一连串
words.ex: A spate of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 一场暴雨淹没了街道。
words.en: A spate of things, especially unpleasant ones, is a large number of them that happen or appear within a short period of time.

words.ex: He went on a shopping spree last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他上周末进行了一次疯狂购物。
words.en: A spree is a short period of time during which you do a lot of something, often something that you do not normally do and that you enjoy.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.tr:
v. 染上点颜色
n. 一丝痕迹；色调
words.ex: The sky has a tinge of pink at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空有一丝粉红色。
words.en: A tinge of a colour, feeling, or quality is a small amount of it.

chapters.name: Level 11 名词 场所•位置

words.ex: The hiker stared into the dark abyss.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者凝视着黑暗的深渊。
words.en: An abyss is a very deep hole in the ground, or a very difficult or unpleasant situation that seems to have no end.

words.ex: We sat under the arbor to escape the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在树阴下躲避炎热的阳光。
words.en: An arbor is a garden structure on which plants and vines are grown.

words.tr: n. 优势；支配地位；支配力量
words.ex: The king's ascendancy lasted for twenty years.
words.ex_cn: 国王的统治持续了二十年。
words.en: If one group has ascendancy over another group, it has more power or influence than the other group.

words.ex: The castle is a bastion of safety.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是安全的堡垒。
words.en: A bastion is a projecting part of a fortification built at an angle to the line of a wall, so as to allow defensive fire in several directions.

words.ex: The building is built on solid bedrock.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑建在坚实的基岩上。
words.en: The solid rock underlying loose deposits such as soil or alluvium.

words.ex: She sat under a bower of roses.
words.ex_cn: 她坐在一丛玫瑰花形成的凉亭下。
words.en: A bower is a pleasant place in the shade under a tree or a structure in a garden where people can sit and relax.

words.tr:
n. 藏物处；隐藏物；
v. 匿藏；
words.ex: The hunters found a cache of food under the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人们在石头下发现了一个食物藏匿处。
words.en: A cache is a hidden store of things such as weapons or a supply of food.

words.tr: n. 裂口；深坑；显著差别
words.ex: The earthquake created a deep chasm in the ground.
words.ex_cn: 地震在地面上造成了一道深深的裂口。
words.en: A chasm is a very deep, narrow opening in rock, ice, or the ground.

words.ex: The concert was the culmination of his music career.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会是他音乐生涯的顶点。
words.en: The culmination of something is the highest or final point of it, often after a long period of development.

words.tr:
n. 犁沟；车辙；皱纹
v. 犁耕；使皱眉头
words.ex: The farmer plowed a deep furrow in the field.
words.ex_cn: 农夫在田里犁出了一条深深的犁沟。
words.en: A furrow is a long narrow trench made in the ground by a plow, especially for planting seeds or for irrigation. It can also refer to a deep wrinkle on a person's face.

words.tr:
n. （驼）峰；驼背；小土丘
v. 背负（重物）；弓起
words.ex: The camel has a big hump on its back.
words.ex_cn: 骆驼的背上有一个大驼峰。
words.en: A hump is a rounded protuberance or bulge, especially on the back of a camel or other animal, or on a person's back. As a verb, it means to form into a hump or to carry something with difficulty.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.ex: He feels comfortable in his artistic milieu.
words.ex_cn: 他在他的艺术环境中感到自在。
words.en: The milieu is the environment or setting in which something happens or develops.

words.tr: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难；
words.ex: Don't ignore the pitfall of skipping homework.
words.ex_cn: 不要忽视不做作业这个陷阱。
words.en: A pitfall is a likely mistake or problem in a situation.

words.ex: The hikers got stuck in a quagmire near the river.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在河边陷入了一片沼泽地。
words.en: A quagmire is a difficult, complicated, or unpleasant situation that is hard to escape from.

words.tr:
n. 僵局；和棋；僵持状态
v. 使陷入僵局
words.ex: The two players are in a stalemate.
words.ex_cn: 两位选手陷入了僵局。
words.en: A situation in which further action or progress by opposing parties seems impossible.

words.ex: The parking lot has three tiers.
words.ex_cn: 这个停车场有三层。
words.en: A tier is a row or layer of something that has several rows or layers placed one above the other.

words.ex: The statue has a strong torso.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像有一个强壮的躯干。
words.en: The main part of the human body, not including the head, arms, or legs.

words.ex: The ball followed a smooth trajectory.
words.ex_cn: 球沿着一条平滑的轨迹飞行。
words.en: The path followed by a projectile flying or an object moving under the action of given forces.

words.tr: n. 前锋；前卫；先头部队；先驱
words.ex: He is at the vanguard of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他在新技术的前沿。
words.en: The vanguard is the leading part of an advancing military formation. It has a broader meaning, signifying the forefront of any movement or field.

words.tr: n. 兔子窝；狭窄拥挤的街区
words.ex: The rabbits live in a warren under the hill.
words.ex_cn: 兔子住在山下的兔子窝里。
words.en: A warren is a network of interconnecting rabbit burrows or a place where rabbits are kept in captivity. It can also refer to a densely populated or labyrinthine area.

words.tr: n. 分水岭；集水区；转折点
words.ex: The river forms a watershed between two valleys.
words.ex_cn: 这条河构成了两个山谷之间的分水岭。
words.en: A watershed is an event or period that is important because it represents a big change in how people do or think about something.

chapters.name: Level 11 名词 人

words.tr:
n. 别名；化名
adv. 又被称为；另外地
words.ex: He uses an alias to hide his real name.
words.ex_cn: 他使用一个化名来隐藏他的真实姓名。
words.en: An alias is a false or assumed identity, especially one used by a criminal.

words.ex: He is an alumnus of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的男毕业生。
words.en: An alumnus is a former student of a particular school, college, or university.

words.ex: The bard sang a song about love and war.
words.ex_cn: 这位吟游诗人唱了一首关于爱情与战争的歌。
words.en: A bard is a poet, traditionally one who recites epic poems and is associated with a particular oral tradition.

words.tr: n. 生育高峰中出生的人
words.ex: My dad is a boomer who loves classic rock.
words.ex_cn: 我爸爸是个婴儿潮一代，喜欢经典摇滚。
words.en: A boomer is a person born during the baby boom, especially in the US between 1946 and 1965, or something that makes a loud, deep sound.

words.tr: n. 弟兄们；同胞；教友；会友
words.ex: The brethren gathered for prayer each morning.
words.ex_cn: 兄弟们每天早上聚集祷告。
words.en: Brethren is an old-fashioned plural form of 'brother', used especially in religious contexts to refer to male members of a group or community.

words.ex: He is a strong comer in the talent show.
words.ex_cn: 他在才艺比赛中是个有成功希望的人。
words.en: A comer is someone who arrives somewhere or someone who is likely to be successful in the future.

words.ex: The celebrity walked with her entourage.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人带着她的随行人员走路。
words.en: An entourage is a group of people who travel with and assist an important person.

words.ex: He spoke in the guise of a friend.
words.ex_cn: 他以朋友的伪装说话。
words.en: An external form, appearance, or manner of presentation, typically concealing the true nature of something.

words.tr: adj. 异性的；异性恋的; n. 异性恋的人
words.ex: They are a heterosexual couple.
words.ex_cn: 他们是一对异性伴侣。
words.en: A heterosexual person is sexually attracted to people of the opposite sex.

words.ex: The mason built a stone wall with care.
words.ex_cn: 石匠仔细地砌了一堵石墙。
words.en: A mason is a person who builds or works with stone or brick.

words.ex: The dog has a long pedigree from champion lines.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗有着来自冠军血统的悠久血统。
words.en: A pedigree is the recorded ancestry or lineage of a person or animal, often used to indicate purity of breed or high social status.

words.ex: He writes books under a pseudonym.
words.ex_cn: 他用笔名写书。
words.en: A pseudonym is a name that someone, especially a writer, uses instead of their real name.

words.tr: n. 剥皮工人；皮革商；骗子; n. （Skinner）人名；（英）斯金纳；（瑞典）希纳
words.ex: Skinner taught psychology at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 斯金纳在哈佛大学教授心理学。
words.en: A person who removes the skin from animals, especially as a job.

words.tr:
adj. 代理的；代用的
n. 代理人；代用品
words.ex: He acted as a surrogate father to the child.
words.ex_cn: 他作为孩子的代理父亲。
words.en: A surrogate is a person or thing that takes the place of or acts for another, especially in a role or function that is typically filled by someone else.

words.tr: n. 自命不凡的新上任者；狂妄自大的新手
words.ex: The upstart claimed he could run the company better than the founder.
words.ex_cn: 这个自命不凡的新上任者声称他比创始人更能管理公司。
words.en: An upstart is someone who has suddenly risen to a higher social or economic class and behaves in a way that is considered arrogant or presumptuous.

words.tr: n. 妓女；娼妓；v. 卖淫；嫖妓
words.ex: The movie shows a poor woman who became a whore to survive.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一位为了生存而沦为妓女的贫穷女性。
words.en: A woman who engages in sexual activity for payment.

chapters.name: Level 11 名词 物品

words.ex: The beacon shines at night to guide ships.
words.ex_cn: 灯塔在夜晚发光以引导船只。
words.en: A beacon is a light or a fire, usually on a hill or tower, which acts as a signal or a warning.

words.ex: The computer uses a buffer to store data temporarily.
words.ex_cn: 计算机使用缓冲区临时存储数据。
words.en: A buffer is something that prevents something else from being harmed or that reduces the impact of something.

words.tr:
n. 扶墙；拱壁
v. 支持
words.ex: The old wall needs a buttress to stay standing.
words.ex_cn: 这面旧墙需要一个支撑物来保持不倒。
words.en: A buttress is a structure built against or projecting from a wall which serves to support or reinforce the wall. As a verb, to buttress means to support or strengthen something.

words.ex: He used a clamp to hold the wood together.
words.ex_cn: 他用夹具把木头固定在一起。
words.en: A clamp is a device that holds two things firmly together. As a verb, to clamp means to hold or fasten something tightly.

words.tr:
n. 鹅卵石
v. 修补（鞋）；粗制滥造
words.ex: He cobbled together a shoe from old leather.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧皮革拼凑了一双鞋。
words.en: To cobble means to make or assemble something in a rough or improvised way, or to pave with cobblestones.

words.ex: Education is the cornerstone of a strong society.
words.ex_cn: 教育是强大社会的基石。
words.en: A cornerstone is an important quality or feature on which a particular thing depends or is based.

words.tr: n. 板条箱；箱子；篓；破旧的飞机或汽车；
words.ex: The apples were packed in a wooden crate.
words.ex_cn: 苹果被装在一个木板条箱里。
words.en: A crate is a large box used for transporting or storing goods.

words.tr:
n. 袖口；裤子翻边；巴掌；手铐
v. 给...上袖口（或翻边）；用手掌轻拍；用巴掌打
words.ex: He rolled up his cuff to wash his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他卷起袖口来洗手。
words.en: The part at the end of a sleeve, where the material of the sleeve is turned back or a separate band is sewn on. Also, to fasten someone's hands together with a pair of handcuffs.

words.tr:
n. 洋娃娃；手推车；摄影车
v. 移动摄影
words.ex: The baby slept in a dolly beside the bed.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿睡在床边的小推车里。
words.en: A dolly is a small model of a human, often used as a child's toy, or a wheeled platform used for moving heavy objects or for supporting a camera in film-making.

words.ex: This phone is the flagship model of the company.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机是该公司的旗舰型号。
words.en: The most important product, service, or project of a company or organization.

words.tr:
n. 漏斗；
v. 输送；
words.ex: He poured the oil through a funnel.
words.ex_cn: 他把油通过漏斗倒了进去。
words.en: A funnel is an object with a wide, circular top and a narrow tube at the bottom, used for pouring liquids or powders into containers with small openings.

words.ex: He wore a pair of black gauntlets to protect his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一副黑色长手套来保护双手。
words.en: A gauntlet is a type of glove that covers the hand and wrist and sometimes extends up the arm. It can also refer to a challenge or a situation where someone is subjected to a series of difficult tests or attacks.

words.ex: The children played in the grit near the road.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在路边的沙砾中玩耍。
words.en: Grit is very small pieces of stone. It is often used to make surfaces less slippery. Grit is also a quality of character that enables someone to continue with determination in the face of difficulties.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: The wet stone has a soft sheen.
words.ex_cn: 湿石头有柔和的光泽。
words.en: A sheen is a soft, smooth, shiny quality on the surface of something.

words.tr: n. 木瓦；墙面板；鹅卵石；海滨砂石；招牌
words.ex: The roof is covered with brown shingles.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶铺着棕色的木瓦。
words.en: Shingles are thin, flat pieces of wood or other material that are laid in overlapping rows to cover the roof of a building.

words.ex: The factory dumped sludge into the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂把淤泥倾倒进河里。
words.en: Sludge is a thick, soft, wet mud or a similar viscous mixture of liquid and solid components, especially the product of an industrial or refining process.

words.tr:
n. 鱼雷
v. 用鱼雷袭击；完全摧毁
words.ex: The submarine fired a torpedo at the ship.
words.ex_cn: 潜艇向那艘船发射了一枚鱼雷。
words.en: A torpedo is a long, narrow weapon that is fired underwater and explodes when it hits something, such as a ship.

words.ex: The bottle contains zinc to help your body stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 这个瓶子里含有锌，有助于你的身体健康。
words.en: Zinc is a bluish-white metal that is used in making other metals or for covering other metals to protect them.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 位置关系•相对关系

words.tr: adj. 贴邻的；毗连的； v. “adjoin”的现在分词；
words.ex: The two houses are adjoining.
words.ex_cn: 这两所房子是贴邻的。
words.en: Adjoining is used to describe something that is next to or joined with something else.

words.ex: The trip is contingent on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行取决于天气情况。
words.en: A contingent event or situation depends on something else in order to happen or exist.

words.ex: The punishment was disproportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚与罪行不成比例。
words.en: Something that is disproportionate is surprisingly large or small in comparison to something else.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.ex: The village has a sparse population.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄人口稀少。
words.en: Something that is sparse is small in number or amount and spread out over an area.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.tr: adj. 高耸的；杰出的；激烈的； v. “tower”的现在分词；
words.ex: The towering building stood above all others in the city.
words.ex_cn: 那座高耸的建筑矗立在城市中所有其他建筑之上。
words.en: Very tall or high; outstanding or extreme.

words.ex: Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在现代生活中无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as ubiquitous, you mean that they seem to be everywhere.

words.ex: The country made a unilateral decision to close the border.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家单方面决定关闭边境。
words.en: Involving only one group or country.

words.tr:
adj. 本国的；地方的
n. 方言；土语
words.ex: He wrote the poem in the vernacular language.
words.ex_cn: 他用本国语言写了这首诗。
words.en: The vernacular is the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 学术•文化•宗教

words.tr:
n. 巴洛克式；
adj. 巴洛克式的；
words.ex: The church has a baroque style with gold decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这座教堂具有巴洛克风格，装饰有金色元素。
words.en: Baroque is a style of architecture, music, and art that was common in Europe in the 17th and early 18th centuries, characterized by ornate detail.

words.ex: He sat in a contemplative silence after the news.
words.ex_cn: 听到这个消息后，他静静地沉思着。
words.en: If you are contemplative, you spend a lot of time thinking seriously and quietly about something.

words.ex: They wore nuptial robes at the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他们在婚礼上穿了婚礼礼服。
words.en: Relating to marriage or weddings.

words.tr: adj. 教区的；地方范围的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The priest served in a small parochial church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在一座小型教区教堂服务。
words.en: If you describe someone as parochial, you are criticizing them because you think they are too concerned with their own affairs and should be thinking about more important things.

words.tr:
adj. 亵渎的；不敬神的；世俗的
v. 亵渎神灵；亵圣
words.ex: He used profane words during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵中说了脏话。
words.en: If someone uses profane language, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, especially because it refers to sex or other bodily functions in a way that is considered inappropriate.

words.ex: He is a prolific writer who publishes books every year.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位多产的作家，每年都会出版书籍。
words.en: A prolific artist, writer, or composer produces a large number of works of art, books, or pieces of music.

words.tr: adj. 推定的；假定的；一般认为的
words.ex: The putative father was asked to take a DNA test.
words.ex_cn: 被推定的父亲被要求做DNA测试。
words.en: Generally believed to be or to exist, but not proved to be so.

words.tr: adj. 典型的；精髓的；精华的
words.ex: He is the quintessential teacher, patient and kind.
words.ex_cn: 他是典型的教师，耐心而和善。
words.en: Representing the most perfect or typical example of a quality or class.

words.tr:
n. 证明书；推荐书
adj. 证明书的；表扬的
words.ex: She received a glowing testimonial from her former employer.
words.ex_cn: 她收到了前雇主的表扬推荐信。
words.en: A testimonial is a written statement about someone's character or abilities, or a thing given in recognition of service or achievement.

words.tr: adj. 神学的；神学性质的
words.ex: He is studying theological texts at the seminary.
words.ex_cn: 他在神学院学习神学文本。
words.en: Relating to the study of the nature of God and religious belief.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 身体•健康

words.tr: adj. 处境困难的； v. “ail”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ailing business needs help to survive.
words.ex_cn: 这家处境困难的公司需要帮助才能生存。
words.en: If someone is ailing, they are ill and are not getting better.

words.ex: The burly man carried two heavy boxes easily.
words.ex_cn: 那个健壮的男人轻松地搬了两个重箱子。
words.en: A burly person is big and strong.

words.tr: adj. 昏迷不醒的；不省人事的；困乏的
words.ex: The man became comatose after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，这个人陷入了昏迷。
words.en: If someone is comatose, they are in a coma and are not conscious.

words.ex: He had a coronary artery blockage.
words.ex_cn: 他有一条冠状动脉堵塞。
words.en: Relating to the arteries that supply the heart with blood.

words.ex: He felt a corporal pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他感到身体上的疼痛。
words.en: A corporal is a non-commissioned officer in the army, above a private and below a sergeant. As an adjective, it refers to the body or physical condition.

words.ex: He carried a hefty bag full of books.
words.ex_cn: 他提着一个异常大的装满书的包。
words.en: Something that is hefty is large in size, weight, or amount.

words.ex: The doctor checked his intestinal health.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肠道健康。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the intestines.

words.ex: The doctor gave him intravenous fluids.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他打了静脉输液。
words.en: Intravenous means within or by means of a vein or veins.

words.ex: He has a nasal voice when he has a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他感冒时声音有鼻音。
words.en: Nasal is used to describe something relating to the nose or the production of sound through the nose.

words.ex: The baby's neural connections are developing fast.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿的神经连接正在迅速发展。
words.en: Neural relates to a nerve or the nervous system.

words.tr: adj. 眼的；视觉的；光学的
words.ex: He wears optic glasses to see clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他戴光学眼镜以便看得清楚。
words.en: Relating to the eye or vision.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.ex: He hurt his spinal cord in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中伤到了脊髓。
words.en: Relating to the spine or the spinal cord.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 感情•感觉

words.ex: The abrasive surface wore down the metal.
words.ex_cn: 磨损的表面磨耗了金属。
words.en: An abrasive substance is rough and can be used to clean surfaces or to make them smooth by rubbing. An abrasive person is someone who is harsh and rude.

words.tr:
adj. 愤愤不平的；委屈的；受害的
v. 令委屈；令苦恼；侵害；“aggrieve”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She felt aggrieved by the unfair treatment she received.
words.ex_cn: 她因受到不公平的对待而感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you feel aggrieved, you feel upset and angry because you think that you have been treated unfairly.

words.tr:
adj. 诱人的；迷人的；有吸引力的
v. 诱惑；吸引；“allure”的现在分词
words.ex: The city's nightlife is alluring to many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的夜生活对许多游客来说都极具诱惑力。
words.en: Something that is alluring is powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: He felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对接受这份工作邀约感到矛盾。
words.en: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, you mean that they have mixed feelings about it or are unsure whether they want it or not.

words.ex: He is apprehensive about the test.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试感到担忧。
words.en: Anxious or fearful that something bad or unpleasant will happen.

words.ex: He is an avid reader of mystery novels.
words.ex_cn: 他热衷于阅读侦探小说。
words.en: If you say that someone is avid for something, you mean that they are very eager to get it.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is breathtaking.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: If you say that something is breathtaking, you mean that it is extremely beautiful or amazing.

words.tr: adj. 有浮力的；心情愉快的；
words.ex: The buoyant life jacket keeps you on the water.
words.ex_cn: 有浮力的救生衣让你浮在水面上。
words.en: A buoyant object floats on a liquid or in the air. A buoyant economy, market, or industry is successful because a lot of money is being spent or invested in it.

words.tr: adj. 心烦意乱的；忧心如焚的
words.ex: She was distraught when she lost her dog.
words.ex_cn: 当她丢失了她的狗时，她非常悲痛。
words.en: If someone is distraught, they are so upset and worried that they cannot think clearly.

words.ex: The music is evocative of childhood memories.
words.ex_cn: 这音乐唤起了童年的回忆。
words.en: If you describe something as evocative, you mean that it is good or interesting because it produces pleasant memories, ideas, emotions, and responses in people.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；热情洋溢的；
words.ex: The exuberant children ran around the park.
words.ex_cn: 那些精力充沛的孩子们在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: If you are exuberant, you are full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness.

words.tr: adj. 热烈的；强烈的；热情的
words.ex: He is a fervent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: having or showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

words.tr: adj. 使人晕眩的；头晕的；轻浮的
words.ex: She felt giddy after spinning around.
words.ex_cn: 她转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel giddy, you feel unsteady and think that you are about to fall over, usually because you are not well or because you are excited or frightened.

words.tr: adj. 阴郁的；闷闷不乐的
words.ex: He looked glum after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他看起来闷闷不乐。
words.en: If someone is glum, they are sad and quiet because they are disappointed or unhappy about something.

words.tr:
adj. 勉强的；不愿的；吝啬的
v. 勉强做；不情愿地给；吝惜；“grudge”的现在分词
words.ex: He gave a grudging nod of approval.
words.ex_cn: 他勉强地点头表示同意。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as grudging, you mean that they do something unwillingly, often because they feel they have to.

words.tr:
adj. 悲痛的；令人伤心的
v. 耙地；折磨；使愁苦；“harrow”的现在分词
words.ex: The harrowing story of the survivors left a deep impression on everyone.
words.ex_cn: 幸存者的悲惨故事给每个人留下了深刻的印象。
words.en: Causing feelings of deep distress or anguish.

words.ex: The heady smell of fresh flowers made her smile.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜花朵的兴奋香气让她露出了微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as heady, you mean that it has a strong or exhilarating effect, especially in making you feel excited, enthusiastic, or slightly drunk.

words.ex: The movie was hilarious and made us laugh a lot.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影非常搞笑，让我们笑得很开心。
words.en: If you describe something as hilarious, you mean that it is extremely funny and it makes you laugh a lot.

words.tr: adj. 羞辱性的；丢脸的； v. “humiliate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The humiliating comment made him feel small.
words.ex_cn: 那句羞辱性的话让他感到自己很渺小。
words.en: If something is humiliating, it makes you feel ashamed and stupid, often because it involves a loss of respect or dignity in front of other people.

words.tr: adj. 欢腾的；欢欣鼓舞的
words.ex: The children were jubilant after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们赢了比赛后非常高兴。
words.en: If you are jubilant, you feel extremely happy because of a success.

words.tr: adj. 病态的；心理不健康的
words.ex: He has a morbid fear of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗有一种病态的恐惧。
words.en: If you describe a person or their interest in something as morbid, you mean that they are very interested in unpleasant things, especially death, and you think this is strange.

words.ex: The loud music was obnoxious and made everyone leave.
words.ex_cn: 那刺耳的音乐非常讨厌，让所有人都离开了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as obnoxious, you think that they are very unpleasant because of being aggressive, loud, or offensive.

words.tr: adj. 痛切的；酸楚的；强烈的；尖刻的
words.ex: The letter was poignant and made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 这封信很感人，让她哭了。
words.en: A poignant piece of writing or music makes you feel sad or full of pity.

words.tr: adj. 处于准备状态的； v. “poise”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The athlete is poised to jump.
words.ex_cn: 这位运动员准备好了要跳。
words.en: If someone is poised, they are calm, dignified, and self-controlled, especially in a difficult situation.

words.tr: adj. 沙哑的；粗声的；喧闹的
words.ex: His raucous voice made it hard to understand him.
words.ex_cn: 他沙哑的声音让他很难被听清楚。
words.en: A raucous sound is loud and harsh.

words.tr: adj. 悔恨的；遗憾的；悲哀的
words.ex: He gave a rueful smile after forgetting his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他忘记带钥匙后，露出了一丝苦笑。
words.en: If someone is rueful, they feel or express regret or sorrow in a quiet and gentle way.

words.ex: He gave a sardonic smile when she told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当她说出真相时，他露出了讽刺的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as sardonic, you mean they are mocking or scornful in a humorous way.

words.tr: adj. 诱人的；有魅力的；性感的
words.ex: The seductive smile made him feel nervous.
words.ex_cn: 那诱人的微笑让他感到紧张。
words.en: Something that is seductive is very attractive or tempting.

words.tr: adj.  忧郁的；阴沉的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room had a somber mood.
words.ex_cn: 房间里有一种阴郁的气氛。
words.en: If someone is somber, they are serious or sad.

words.ex: Her strident voice broke the silence.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐的声音打破了寂静。
words.en: If you use strident to describe someone or the way they express themselves, you mean that they make their feelings or opinions known in a very strong way that perhaps makes people uncomfortable.

words.tr: adj. 心照不宣的；不作声的
words.ex: They have a tacit understanding about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们对规则有一种心照不宣的理解。
words.en: If you refer to someone's tacit agreement or approval, you mean they are agreeing to something or approving it without actually saying so, often because they are unwilling to admit to doing so.

words.tr:
adj. 撩拨人的；让人非常着急的
v. （以可望而不可即之物）逗引；使干着急；“tantalize”的现在分词
words.ex: The smell of fresh bread was tantalizing.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的香味令人垂涎。
words.en: If you describe something as tantalizing, you mean that it is very attractive, interesting, or desirable.

words.tr: adj. 拉紧的；绷紧的；紧张的
words.ex: The sail was taut in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 帆在强风中绷得紧紧的。
words.en: If something such as a rope or wire is taut, it is stretched very tight. If muscles or parts of the body are taut, they are stretched tight, often because of physical effort or anxiety.

words.ex: The guard is vigilant at night.
words.ex_cn: 这名守卫在夜里非常警惕。
words.en: Someone who is vigilant gives careful attention to a particular problem or situation and concentrates on noticing any danger or trouble that there might be.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 形状•性质•外观•状态

words.tr:
adv. 漂流地；漫无目的地
adj. 漂泊的；漫无目的的；脱落的
words.ex: The boat was adrift in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 小船在海上漂流。
words.en: If something is adrift, it is floating on the water and not fastened to anything or controlled by anyone.

words.tr: adj. 简朴的；严厉的；苦行的；紧缩的
words.ex: The room has austere walls with no decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的墙壁朴素，没有任何装饰。
words.en: If you describe something as austere, you approve of its plain and simple appearance.

words.tr: adj. 袋状的；宽松的；松弛垂落的
words.ex: He wears baggy jeans to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿宽松的牛仔裤去参加派对。
words.en: If a piece of clothing is baggy, it hangs loosely on your body.

words.tr: adj. 有刺的；有倒钩的；讽刺的
words.ex: The fence has barbed wire on top.
words.ex_cn: 围栏顶部有带刺的铁丝。
words.en: Having a sharp point or points, especially one that is designed to catch or hold something.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；公然的；喧闹的
words.ex: He made a blatant lie to avoid punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他为了逃避惩罚，公然撒了谎。
words.en: If you describe an action as blatant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way, often with a lack of shame or embarrassment.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.tr: v. 烧焦；“char”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The bread was charred from the fire.
words.ex_cn: 面包被火烤焦了。
words.en: If something is charred, it has been burned until it is black.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；暗中行事的
words.ex: He made a clandestine meeting with his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他与朋友进行了一次秘密会面。
words.en: Kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit.

words.ex: He has a culinary degree from a famous school.
words.ex_cn: 他从一所著名学校获得了烹饪学位。
words.en: Relating to cooking or the kitchen.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.tr: adj. 自由决定的；酌情行事的；便宜行事的
words.ex: He spent his discretionary money on a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的可自由支配的钱花在了一部新手机上。
words.en: If something is discretionary, it is available for use as someone chooses, rather than according to a set plan or rule.

words.ex: The walls were painted a drab color.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁被刷成了土褐色。
words.en: If you describe something as drab, you think that it is dull and boring to look at or experience.

words.tr: adj. 轻飘的；缥缈的；虚空的；精致的；
words.ex: The ethereal scarf floated gently in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 那条轻飘的围巾在风中轻轻飘动。
words.en: Something that is ethereal is extremely delicate and light in a way that seems not to be of this world.

words.tr: adj. 艳丽的；炫耀的；神气活现的
words.ex: He wears flamboyant clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿著華麗的衣服來引人注目。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting.

words.tr:
adj. 轻而薄的；易坏的；不足信的
n. 复写纸；薄纸副本
words.ex: The flimsy chair broke when he sat on it.
words.ex_cn: 那把脆弱的椅子当他坐上去时就断了。
words.en: Something that is flimsy is not very strong or solid, and therefore easily damaged or destroyed.

words.ex: The fluorescent lamp lights up the room quickly.
words.ex_cn: 荧光灯很快照亮了房间。
words.en: Fluorescent substances produce bright light of a particular color when they are exposed to light of a different wavelength.

words.ex: The palace has a grandiose design with tall columns and golden domes.
words.ex_cn: 这座宫殿有着宏伟的设计，配有高大的柱子和金色的圆顶。
words.en: If you describe something as grandiose, you mean it is larger or more elaborate than necessary, or it is intended to seem very impressive or magnificent.

words.ex: His idiosyncratic style makes his art easy to recognize.
words.ex_cn: 他独特的风格使他的艺术容易被认出。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions or characteristics as idiosyncratic, you mean that they are rather unusual.

words.ex: The small village is idyllic with green fields and quiet streams.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄有着绿色的田野和宁静的溪流，十分宁静美好。
words.en: An idyllic place or experience is extremely pleasant, beautiful, and peaceful, often in a way that seems too good to be true.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.tr: adj. 穷困的；赤穷的；贫瘠的； v. “impoverish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The impoverished family lived in a small house with no heating.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫困的家庭住在一个没有暖气的小房子里。
words.en: An impoverished person or area is very poor.

words.ex: The memory of her smile is indelible.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的记忆是无法磨灭的。
words.en: If you say that something leaves an indelible impression, you mean that it is very unlikely to be forgotten.

words.tr: adj. 锯齿状的； v. “jag”的过去式；
words.ex: The jagged edge of the rock cut his hand.
words.ex_cn: 岩石的锯齿状边缘割伤了他的手。
words.en: Something that is jagged has a rough, uneven shape or edge with lots of sharp points.

words.ex: The river water looked murky after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，河水看起来污浊。
words.en: If you describe something as murky, you mean that the details of it are not clear or that it is difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.ex: The soup was palatable after adding salt.
words.ex_cn: 加了盐后，汤变得可口美味了。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as palatable, you mean that it tastes pleasant.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.ex: The hotel has a plush lobby with velvet chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店有一个豪华的大堂，配有丝绒椅子。
words.en: Plush refers to something that is luxurious and expensive, or a type of fabric that is very soft and thick.

words.tr: adj. 豪华的；漂亮的； 优雅的；时髦的
words.ex: He wears posh clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿得很时髦去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as posh, you mean that it is smart, fashionable, and expensive.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.ex: He gave a pseudo answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个假的答案。
words.en: Not genuine; sham.

words.tr: adj. 洪亮的；共振的；引起共鸣的；
words.ex: The bell has a resonant sound.
words.ex_cn: 这口钟的声音洪亮。
words.en: A sound that is resonant is deep, strong, and clear, often because it is produced in a space that echoes or amplifies it.

words.tr: adj. 多籽的；褴褛的；邋遢的；脏乱的
words.ex: The watermelon has a seedy center.
words.ex_cn: 西瓜的中心有很多籽。
words.en: If you describe a place or person as seedy, you disapprove of them because they look dirty and untidy, or they have a bad reputation.

words.tr: adj. 劣质的；次品的；卑劣的
words.ex: He bought a shoddy chair that broke after one day.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一把劣质的椅子，一天就坏了。
words.en: If you describe something as shoddy, you mean that it has been done or made carelessly or badly.

words.tr: adj. 质地薄的；肮脏的；低劣的
words.ex: The sleazy curtain let in too much light.
words.ex_cn: 那层薄薄的窗帘透进了太多光。
words.en: If you describe something as sleazy, you mean that it is of low quality or morally questionable, especially because it is associated with sex or crime.

words.ex: The car has a sleek design.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有着流畅的外形。
words.en: Sleek describes something that is smooth, glossy, and streamlined, often implying a sense of elegance and efficiency.

words.ex: The water in the pond was stagnant.
words.ex_cn: 池塘里的水不流动。
words.en: If something such as a business or economy is stagnant, there is little activity or change.

words.ex: The village was stricken by a sudden flood.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄遭受了一场突如其来的洪水。
words.en: If a person or place is stricken by something such as an unpleasant feeling, an illness, or a natural disaster, they are severely affected by it.

words.tr: adj. 柔软的；灵活的；思维敏捷的
words.ex: The yoga teacher has supple legs.
words.ex_cn: 瑜伽老师腿很柔软。
words.en: A supple object or material bends or changes shape easily without breaking or cracking.

words.tr: adj. 缠结的； v. “tangle”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The hair was tangled after the wind.
words.ex_cn: 头发被风吹得打结了。
words.en: If something is tangled, it is twisted together untidily and is difficult to unravel or separate.

words.tr: adj. 俗丽而不值钱的；花里胡哨的
words.ex: She wore a tawdry dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着一件俗丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as tawdry, you mean that it is showy and bright but of very poor quality.

words.ex: Her terse reply left no room for further discussion.
words.ex_cn: 她简洁的回答没有留下进一步讨论的余地。
words.en: A terse statement or comment is brief and to the point, often seeming rude or unfriendly because of its brevity.

words.tr: adj. 骚乱的；喧闹的；热烈的
words.ex: The crowd was tumultuous during the concert.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会上人群喧闹不安。
words.en: A tumultuous event or period of time involves many exciting and confusing events or feelings.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 数量•时间•频率

words.ex: He has an abiding love for music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐有着持久的热爱。
words.en: If you have an abiding feeling for someone or something, you have a feeling that lasts for a long time.

words.tr:
adj. 已故的；不复存在的
n. 死者
words.ex: The defunct company no longer exists.
words.ex_cn: 这家已故的公司不再存在。
words.en: No longer existing or functioning; dead or inactive.

words.tr: adj. 人口统计的；人口的；
words.ex: The survey collected demographic data like age and income.
words.ex_cn: 这项调查收集了年龄和收入等人口统计数据。
words.en: Relating to the structure of populations.

words.tr:
n. 刚长齐羽毛学飞的幼鸟
adj. 新形成的；无经验的
v. 羽毛长成；用羽毛盖上；装上羽毛；“fledge”的现在分词
words.ex: The fledgling bird tried to fly for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这只幼鸟第一次尝试飞翔。
words.en: A fledgling is a young bird that has just grown its feathers and is learning to fly. It can also refer to a person or organization that is new and inexperienced.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的； v. “fleet”的现在分词；
words.ex: The smile was fleeting.
words.ex_cn: 那个微笑是短暂的。
words.en: If you describe something as fleeting, you mean that it lasts only for a very short time.

words.tr:
adj. 无准备的；即兴的；即席的
adv. 无准备地；即兴地；即席地
words.ex: He gave an impromptu speech at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上做了一次即兴演讲。
words.en: An impromptu action is one that you do without planning or organizing it in advance.

words.tr:
adj. 悠闲的；从容的；
adv. 悠闲地；从容地；
words.ex: He took a leisurely walk in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园里悠闲地散步。
words.en: If you do something in a leisurely way, you do it in a relaxed and unhurried manner.

words.tr: adj. 权宜的；临时凑合的；
words.ex: He used a makeshift table made of boxes and a board.
words.ex_cn: 他用箱子和木板做了一个权宜的桌子。
words.en: A makeshift object or arrangement is one that is made or done quickly and without much skill, using whatever is available at the time.

words.tr: adj. 上升的；增长的； n. 底托；登上；乘骑； v. “mount”的现在分词；
words.ex: The mounting pressure made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 上升的压力让他感到紧张。
words.en: The act of fixing or attaching something in position.

words.ex: The dark clouds looked ominous before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨来临前，乌云显得不祥。
words.en: If you describe something as ominous, you mean that it worries you because it makes you think that something unpleasant is going to happen.

words.ex: The resilient child bounced back quickly after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这个适应力强的孩子在事故后很快恢复了。
words.en: Something that is resilient is strong and not easily damaged by being hit, stretched, or squeezed.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 性格•倾向

words.ex: He was adamant about not changing his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他坚定不移地不改变主意。
words.en: If someone is adamant about something, they are determined not to change their mind about it.

words.ex: He is an astute businessman who always makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是个精明的商人，总是做出明智的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as astute, you think they are clever and can see through things quickly and make good judgments.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.tr: n. 废弃物（树枝、碎石等）；
words.ex: The workers cleared the brash from the construction site.
words.ex_cn: 工人们清除了建筑工地上的废弃物。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as brash, you disapprove of them because you think that they are too confident and aggressive.

words.tr: adj. 似公牛的；看涨的；上扬的；乐观的
words.ex: The bull looks bullish as it charges forward.
words.ex_cn: 公牛向前冲时显得似公牛的。
words.en: If someone is bullish about something, they are confident that it will be successful or improve.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；老谋深算的
words.ex: He is a canny trader who always makes smart choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精明的交易员，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: A canny person is clever and able to think quickly, especially in business or politics.

words.tr: adj. 腼腆的；怕羞的；忸怩的
words.ex: She gave a coy smile when asked about her new boyfriend.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及她的新男友时，她露出了腼腆的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as coy, you mean they are pretending to be shy about something in order to attract attention or to deceive people.

words.tr: adj. 简短而失礼的；唐突的
words.ex: He gave a curt reply and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答了一句，然后走开了。
words.en: If someone is curt, they speak in a brief and rather rude way.

words.tr: adj. 不满的；不高兴的； v. “disgruntle”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The disgruntled customer complained about the service.
words.ex_cn: 这位不满的顾客抱怨了这项服务。
words.en: If you are disgruntled, you are cross and dissatisfied because things have not happened the way you wanted them to.

words.tr: v. 缠住；“dog”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The reporter dogged the politician everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 记者紧紧跟随这位政治家到处。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as dogged, you mean that they are determined to continue with something even if it becomes difficult or dangerous.

words.ex: He had a dour expression on his face.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上带着严厉的表情。
words.en: If you describe someone as dour, you mean they are very serious and unfriendly.

words.tr: adj. 易变的；无常的；感情不专的
words.ex: He is fickle and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他善变，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as fickle, you disapprove of them because they keep changing their mind about what they like or want.

words.tr: adj. 直截了当的；直率的；坦白的
words.ex: He is forthright about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地承认自己的错误。
words.en: If you describe someone as forthright, you admire them because they show clearly and strongly what they think and feel.

words.ex: The twin boys are fraternal twins.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩是异卵双胞胎。
words.en: Fraternal is used to describe feelings or actions that are like those of a brother towards his brothers or sisters.

words.tr: adj. 油腔滑调的；口齿伶俐的；圆滑的
words.ex: He gave a glib answer to the difficult question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个轻率的回答。
words.en: If you describe what someone says as glib, you disapprove of it because it implies that something is simple or easy, or that there are no problems involved, when this is not the case.

words.ex: Dolphins are gregarious animals that swim in groups.
words.ex_cn: 海豚是群居动物，成群游泳。
words.en: Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.

words.ex: The hapless boy lost his wallet and got caught in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 这个倒霉的男孩丢了钱包，还被雨淋了。
words.en: If you describe someone as hapless, you mean that they are unlucky or unfortunate.

words.tr: adj. 不能和解的；不能平息的
words.ex: He is an implacable enemy who never forgives.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个永不原谅的不可调和的敌人。
words.en: If you say that someone is implacable, you mean that they have very strong feelings of hostility or disapproval which nobody can change.

words.tr: adj. 不适当的；无能的；笨拙的
words.ex: His inept reply made the situation worse.
words.ex_cn: 他不适当的回答让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you say that someone is inept, you are criticizing them because they do something with a complete lack of skill.

words.ex: He has an insatiable hunger for knowledge.
words.ex_cn: 他对知识有着无法满足的渴望。
words.en: If someone is insatiable, they always want more of something and are never satisfied.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.ex: He is introspective and often thinks about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他善于内省，经常思考自己的感受。
words.en: If you describe someone as introspective, you mean that they spend a lot of time examining their own thoughts, ideas, and feelings.

words.tr: adj. 灵活的；敏捷的；机敏的
words.ex: The cat is nimble and jumps over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳过了篱笆。
words.en: Someone who is nimble is able to move their fingers, hands, or legs quickly and easily.

words.ex: He has an obsessive need to clean everything.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种强迫性的需求，要把一切都打扫干净。
words.en: If someone's behaviour is obsessive, they cannot stop doing a particular thing or behaving in a particular way.

words.tr: adj. 活泼的；神气的；意气洋洋的；有生气的
words.ex: She is perky after drinking coffee.
words.ex_cn: 她喝完咖啡后精神抖擞。
words.en: Someone who is perky is cheerful and lively.

words.tr: adj. 乐天的；自信的；红润的
words.ex: Despite the setbacks, he remained sanguine about the future.
words.ex_cn: 尽管遭遇挫折，他对未来仍然充满希望。
words.en: If you are sanguine about something, you are cheerful and confident that things will happen in the way that you want them to.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.tr: adj. 卑鄙的；污秽的；肮脏的
words.ex: He made a sordid deal to cheat his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一笔卑鄙的交易来欺骗他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as sordid, you mean that it is very immoral or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难以处理的；敏感的
words.ex: He is touchy about his weight.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己体重很敏感。
words.en: If you describe someone as touchy, you mean that they are easily upset, offended, or irritated.

words.ex: He is upbeat about his new job.
words.ex_cn: 他对新工作感到乐观。
words.en: If people or their opinions are upbeat, they are cheerful and full of hope.

words.tr: adj. 异想天开的；古怪的；反复无常的
words.ex: The little girl wore a whimsical hat with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩戴着一顶带有花朵的古怪帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as whimsical, you mean that they are unusual, playful, and unpredictable, often in a way that you find charming or amusing.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 政治•经济

words.tr: adj. 飞行的；空运的；空中传播的；
words.ex: The airborne soldiers jumped from the plane.
words.ex_cn: 这些空降士兵从飞机上跳下。
words.en: In the air; flying or transported by air.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: They made a concerted effort to clean the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们共同努力清理了公园。
words.en: A concerted action or effort is done by several people or groups working together.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.ex: The old system is cumbersome and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧系统复杂而低效。
words.en: Something that is cumbersome is large and heavy and therefore difficult to carry, wear, or handle.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.ex: The detective used forensic evidence to solve the case.
words.ex_cn: 侦探使用法医证据破了案。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the application of scientific methods and techniques to the investigation of crime.

words.ex: The company made fraudulent claims about its product.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司对其产品做出了欺诈性的声明。
words.en: A fraudulent activity is deceitful or dishonest.

words.tr:
adj. 无力偿付债务的；破产的
n. 破产者；无力偿还者
words.ex: The company went insolvent after years of financial mismanagement.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在多年的财务管理不善后破产了。
words.en: If a person or organization is insolvent, they do not have enough money to pay their debts.

words.ex: The signature is null without a date.
words.ex_cn: 没有日期的签名是无效的。
words.en: Having no legal or binding force; completely void or invalid.

words.tr:
n. （古罗马的）贵族；名门望族；有教养的人；罗马帝国的地方官
adj. 贵族的；贵族似的；上流社会的
words.ex: She was born into a patrician family.
words.ex_cn: 她出生在一个贵族家庭。
words.en: A patrician is a person of high birth or noble status, especially in ancient Rome.

words.tr: adj. 专卖的；专利的；所有权的
words.ex: The company uses proprietary software to protect its data.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司使用专有软件来保护其数据。
words.en: Relating to an owner or ownership; exclusive rights of possession, use, or control.

words.ex: The court imposed a punitive fine for the violation.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这一违规行为处以惩罚性罚款。
words.en: Punitive actions, laws, or measures are intended to punish someone.

words.tr:
adj. 反动的；保守的
n. 反动派；保守人士
words.ex: The reactionary government banned free speech.
words.ex_cn: 这个反动政府禁止了言论自由。
words.en: A reactionary person or group tries to prevent changes in the political or social system of their country.

words.tr: adj. 皇家的；尊贵的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: The queen wore a regal crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着一顶威严的王冠。
words.en: If you describe something as regal, you mean that it is suitable for a king or queen, because it is very impressive or beautiful.

words.tr:
n. 性别歧视者
adj. 性别歧视的
words.ex: He made a sexist comment about women drivers.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了关于女司机的性别歧视言论。
words.en: A sexist person shows prejudice or discrimination based on a person's sex, especially against women.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 气候•自然

words.tr: adj. 着火的；闪耀的；激动的
words.ex: The house was ablaze at night.
words.ex_cn: 那所房子在夜里着火了。
words.en: If something is ablaze, it is burning very fiercely.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；起破坏作用的
n. 腐蚀性物品
words.ex: The acid is corrosive and can damage metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种酸具有腐蚀性，会损坏金属。
words.en: A corrosive substance is able to destroy solid materials by a chemical reaction.

words.ex: Malaria is endemic in some parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 疟疾在非洲某些地区是地方性的。
words.en: If a disease or condition is endemic in a particular area, it is frequently or regularly found among the people living there.

words.tr:
adj. 红外线的
n. 红外线
words.ex: The remote uses infrared to change the TV channel.
words.ex_cn: 遥控器使用红外线来切换电视频道。
words.en: Infrared refers to the region of the electromagnetic spectrum with wavelengths longer than visible light but shorter than microwaves, often used in technology for night vision and heat sensing.

words.ex: The lush grass looked green after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，葱翠的草地显得格外绿。
words.en: A lush area has a lot of green, healthy plants, grass, and trees.

words.ex: The scientist studied a mutant frog with three legs.
words.ex_cn: 科学家研究了一只有三条腿的突变青蛙。
words.en: A mutant is an organism or a new genetic character arising or resulting from an instance of mutation.

words.ex: The lion is a predatory animal.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种食肉动物。
words.en: Predatory animals live by killing and eating other animals. Predatory people or organizations are eager to gain something out of someone else's weakness or suffering.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.ex: The seismic wave shook the ground.
words.ex_cn: 地震波震动了地面。
words.en: Seismic means relating to or caused by an earthquake or earth vibration.

chapters.name: Level 11 形容词 程度•单位

words.tr:
v. 完成；使完美；圆房
adj. 完美的；至上的；圆满的
words.ex: He consummated the deal with a handshake.
words.ex_cn: 他用握手完成了这笔交易。
words.en: To consummate means to make something complete or perfect, often used in the context of a marriage or an agreement. It can also describe someone who is extremely skilled in a particular area.

words.tr: adj. 使人畏缩的；吓人的； v. “daunt”的现在分词；
words.ex: The math test seemed daunting to him.
words.ex_cn: 这次数学考试让他感到畏缩。
words.en: Something that is daunting makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.ex: He is downright lazy.
words.ex_cn: 他完全懒惰。
words.en: You use downright to emphasize that something is completely the case, especially when you are describing something bad or negative.

words.tr: adj. 光辉的； v. “glow”的现在分词；
words.ex: The glowing sun rose over the hills.
words.ex_cn: 光辉的太阳从山上升起。
words.en: If you describe something as glowing, you mean that it is very positive and enthusiastic.

words.ex: The inexorable flow of time cannot be stopped.
words.ex_cn: 时间不可阻挡地流逝。
words.en: If you describe something as inexorable, you mean that it is impossible to stop or prevent from happening.

words.tr: adj. 非常亮的；浓艳的；苍白的；血红的；可怕的；（故意地）骇人听闻的
words.ex: The lurid neon signs lit up the night street.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的霓虹灯照亮了夜晚的街道。
words.en: If you say that something is lurid, you are critical of it because it involves a lot of violence, sex, or shocking detail.

words.tr:
adj. 杂色的；混杂的
n. 杂色；混杂
words.ex: The motley crowd cheered at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 这群杂乱的人群在游行中欢呼。
words.en: If you describe a group of things or people as motley, you mean that they are very different from each other and do not seem to belong together.

words.tr: adj. 夸张的； v. “overblow”的过去分词；
words.ex: The news report was overblown and not true.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻报道太过夸张，不真实。
words.en: If you describe something as overblown, you mean that it is given more importance or is more elaborate than necessary.

words.tr: adj. 最重要的； v. “override”的现在分词；
words.ex: The overriding goal is to keep everyone safe.
words.ex_cn: 最重要的目标是确保每个人的安全。
words.en: An overriding issue or feeling is more important than any other.

words.tr:
n. 恳求；答辩状；诉状
adj. 恳求的
v. 恳求；辩护；答辩；以…为理由；“plead”的现在分词
words.ex: Her pleading eyes begged for mercy.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求的眼神乞求着怜悯。
words.en: Pleading is the act of making an emotional appeal or a legal argument in court.

words.tr: adj. 惊人的；巨大的；奇异的；巨大的；
words.ex: He showed a prodigious memory for names.
words.ex_cn: 他对名字有着惊人的记忆力。
words.en: If you describe something as prodigious, you are emphasizing that it is very large or impressive.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；充满…的
words.ex: Rumors are rife in the town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在镇上到处流传。
words.en: If you say that something, usually something bad, is rife in a place or that the place is rife with it, you mean that it is very common.

words.ex: That paper was a seminal work in computer science.
words.ex_cn: 那篇论文是计算机科学领域一部影响深远的著作。
words.en: Seminal is used to describe things such as books, works, events, and people that have a great influence in a particular field.

words.ex: He bought a sizable house with a big garden.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一所很大的房子，带一个大花园。
words.en: Something that is sizable is fairly large.

words.ex: He gave a stellar performance in the play.
words.ex_cn: 他在剧中表现出色。
words.en: Of or relating to stars; outstanding or excellent.

words.ex: Children are susceptible to colds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子容易感冒。
words.en: If you are susceptible to something or someone, you are very likely to be influenced by them.

words.tr: v. 扫；“sweep”的现在分词； adj. 全面的；
words.ex: He sweeping the floor every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上扫地。
words.en: If you describe something as sweeping, you mean it is very extensive or has a very wide effect.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.tr: adj. 真实的；确实的；真正的
words.ex: It was a veritable treasure trove of old books.
words.ex_cn: 那是一个真正的旧书宝库。
words.en: You use veritable to emphasize the size, amount, or nature of something.

chapters.name: Level 11 副词 时间•频率

words.ex: He started his project anew after the failure.
words.ex_cn: 失败后，他重新开始了他的项目。
words.en: If you do something anew, you do it again, often in a different way from before.

chapters.name: Level 11 副词 程度

words.ex: The food was amply provided for all guests.
words.ex_cn: 所有客人的食物都充足地提供了。
words.en: If something is amply demonstrated, proved, or rewarded, it is shown, proven, or rewarded in a very obvious and satisfactory way.

words.ex: He is overly careful with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱过于谨慎。
words.en: To an excessive degree.

chapters.name: Level 12 状态•存在类动词

words.ex: He used artifice to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计赢得了比赛。
words.en: Clever or cunning devices or expedients, especially as used to trick or deceive others.

words.ex: The wind began to abate after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风开始减弱。
words.en: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.

words.ex: He feels sick because of too much bile.
words.ex_cn: 他因为胆汁过多而感到恶心。
words.en: Bile is a bitter, yellow-green fluid that is produced by the liver and helps in the digestion of fats.

words.tr: n. 苏丹（某些穆斯林国家统治者的称号）
words.ex: The sultan ruled the land with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 苏丹以智慧统治着这片土地。
words.en: A sultan is a ruler in some Muslim countries.

words.ex: The king decided to abdicate in favor of his son.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定退位，让位给他的儿子。
words.en: If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen.

words.tr: n. 损害；身体上的伤害
words.ex: The doctor found a lesion on his skin.
words.ex_cn: 医生在他的皮肤上发现了一个病灶。
words.en: A lesion is an area of damage to the body, such as a wound, ulcer, or tumor.

words.ex: He was late due to traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他因为交通堵塞迟到了。
words.en: If an event is due to something, it happens or exists as a direct result of that thing.

words.tr: v. 同意；继承；即位；加入
words.ex: He acceded to their request.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了他们的请求。
words.en: If you accede to someone's request, you do what they ask.

words.ex: The duke rules a small duchy in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 公爵统治着一座山中的小公国。
words.en: A duchy is the territory of a duke or duchess.

words.ex: They chose arbitration to solve their dispute.
words.ex_cn: 他们选择了仲裁来解决他们的纠纷。
words.en: Arbitration is a process in which a disagreement between two people or groups is settled by an arbitrator.

words.ex: She sang softly to allay his fears.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声唱歌以缓解他的恐惧。
words.en: If you allay someone's fears or doubts, you stop them feeling afraid or doubtful.

words.tr:
n. 体内大出血；严重流失
v. 体内大出血；（使）严重流失
words.ex: The patient suffered a severe hemorrhage after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 病人在事故后发生了严重的出血。
words.en: A hemorrhage is a severe loss of blood from a burst blood vessel, either inside or outside the body.

words.ex: The two companies will amalgamate next month.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司下个月将合并。
words.en: If two or more organizations amalgamate, they join together and become one organization.

words.ex: The states formed a confederation to share power.
words.ex_cn: 这些州组成了一个联盟来分享权力。
words.en: A confederation is an organization which consists of a number of parties or groups united in an alliance.

words.ex: The army stopped the incursion at the border.
words.ex_cn: 军队在边境阻止了入侵。
words.en: An incursion is a sudden attack on or invasion of a place.

words.tr: v. 消灭；歼灭；彻底击败
words.ex: The bomb will annihilate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To annihilate something means to destroy it completely.

words.ex: The annexation of the small country by its neighbor caused international protest.
words.ex_cn: 邻国对这个小国的吞并引发了国际抗议。
words.en: The act of annexing, especially territory.

words.ex: The municipality cleaned the streets last week.
words.ex_cn: 这个自治市上周清理了街道。
words.en: A municipality is a city or town that has its own government to manage local affairs.

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.ex: The charity aims to alleviate destitution among the elderly.
words.ex_cn: 该慈善机构旨在减轻老年人的贫困。
words.en: Destitution is the state of having no money or possessions.

words.ex: His pride begets conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他的骄傲招致了冲突。
words.en: To beget means to cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: The judge condemned the iniquity of the corrupt system.
words.ex_cn: 法官谴责了腐败制度的邪恶。
words.en: Iniquity refers to gross immorality or injustice.

words.tr: n. 礼貌得体；适宜的举止
words.ex: He maintained decorum during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间保持了得体的行为。
words.en: Decorum is behavior that is controlled, calm, and polite, especially in formal situations.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.ex: The boat docked at the quay.
words.ex_cn: 船停在了码头。
words.en: A quay is a long platform beside the sea or a river where boats can be tied up and loaded or unloaded.

words.tr:
n. 巨浪；如巨浪翻腾的东西
v. （像巨浪般）汹涌；翻腾
words.ex: The billow crashed against the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 巨浪拍打着岩石。
words.en: A billow is a large wave or surge of water. It can also refer to the act of swelling or rolling like a wave.

words.tr: adj. 变化无常的；任性的
words.ex: He is capricious and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他喜怒无常，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is capricious often changes their mind unexpectedly.

words.ex: The dark clouds bode a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something bodes ill, it makes you think that something bad will happen in the future. If something bodes well, it makes you think that something good will happen.

words.ex: It was an auspicious day for their wedding.
words.ex_cn: 那天是他们婚礼的吉日。
words.en: If you describe something as auspicious, you mean that it is a sign of future success.

words.ex: He climbed mt. fuji last summer.
words.ex_cn: 他去年夏天爬了富士山。
words.en: Abbreviation for 'mountain' or 'mount' (used in geographical names).

words.ex: The plot involved subversion of the government.
words.ex_cn: 这个情节涉及对政府的颠覆。
words.en: Subversion is the act of trying to destroy or damage an established system or government.

words.ex: The axe will cleave the wood in two.
words.ex_cn: 斧头会把木头劈成两半。
words.en: To split or sever something, especially along a natural line or grain; to adhere firmly and closely or loyally and unwaveringly to something.

words.ex: The iris of her eye is blue.
words.ex_cn: 她的眼睛虹膜是蓝色的。
words.en: The iris is a flat, colored, ring-shaped membrane behind the cornea of the eye, with an adjustable circular opening (pupil) in the center.

words.ex: The snake constricts its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇缠住它的猎物。
words.en: If something constricts you, it limits your actions so that you cannot do what you want to do.

words.ex: The iron fence will corrode in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 铁栅栏在雨中会生锈。
words.en: If metal or stone corrodes, or if something corrodes it, it is gradually destroyed by a chemical reaction.

words.ex: The ship's keel was damaged in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船的龙骨在风暴中受损了。
words.en: The keel is the central structural basis of a ship or boat, running along the bottom from the bow to the stern. It is the first part of a ship's hull to be constructed and is the primary structural element that provides stability and strength to the vessel.

words.tr: n. 无篷小艇；小舟；救生筏；
words.ex: They rowed the dinghy to the island.
words.ex_cn: 他们划着无篷小艇去了岛上。
words.en: A dinghy is a small boat that you sail or row.

words.ex: The company wants to decentralize its operations.
words.ex_cn: 公司希望将运营去中心化。
words.en: To decentralize means to distribute the administrative functions or powers of (a central authority) over a less concentrated area.

words.tr:
n. 周边地区；附近
v. 包围；环绕；“environ”的第三人称单数
words.ex: The city's environs are filled with charming villages.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的郊区充满了迷人的村庄。
words.en: The area surrounding a place; the outskirts.

words.ex: Farmers use insecticide to kill bugs on crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用杀虫剂来杀死作物上的害虫。
words.en: A substance used for killing insects.

words.tr: v. 大批杀死；大量毁灭
words.ex: The storm decimated the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个村庄。
words.en: To decimate something such as a group of people or animals means to destroy a very large number of them.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.ex: The smoke from the factory is noxious.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟雾是有害的。
words.en: Something that is noxious is harmful or poisonous.

words.tr: adj. 俗艳的；花哨的；过分装饰的
words.ex: The room was decorated in a garish pink that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间被装饰成刺眼的粉红色，令人眼睛不适。
words.en: If you describe something as garish, you mean that it is excessively bright, colorful, or elaborate in a way that is considered tasteless or unattractive.

words.ex: His rude words detract from the beauty of the speech.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话贬损了演讲的优美。
words.en: If one thing detracts from another, it makes it seem less good or impressive.

words.tr: n. 圆形剧场；竞技场；梯形教室
words.ex: The students watched a play in the old amphitheater.
words.ex_cn: 学生们在旧的圆形剧场里观看了戏剧。
words.en: An amphitheater is a large open area surrounded by rows of seats sloping upwards. Amphitheaters were used in ancient Greece and Rome for public entertainments.

words.ex: Arsenic is a poisonous element found in some water.
words.ex_cn: 砷是一种存在于某些水源中的有毒元素。
words.en: A very poisonous metallic element that has three allotropic forms; arsenic and arsenic compounds are used as herbicides and insecticides and various alloys; found in arsenopyrite and orpiment and realgar

words.ex: The doctor used drops to dilate her pupils.
words.ex_cn: 医生用了滴眼液来扩大她的瞳孔。
