words.en: If you dilate something such as a part of your body, or if it dilates, it becomes larger or wider.

words.ex: The blood vessel carries blood to the heart.
words.ex_cn: 血管将血液输送到心脏。
words.en: A blood vessel is a tube in the body through which blood flows.

words.ex: The sorcerer conjured a spell to protect the village.
words.ex_cn: 男巫施了一个保护村庄的咒语。
words.en: A sorcerer is a person who claims or is believed to have magic powers; a wizard.

words.ex: The wizard waved his wand and made the ball disappear.
words.ex_cn: 巫师挥动他的魔杖，让球消失了。
words.en: A wand is a thin, straight stick that is used by magicians to perform magic tricks or by conductors to direct an orchestra.

words.tr: adj. 铅灰色的；铅制的；沉闷的；铅一般重的; vt. 使沉重；使懒散；使呆滞
words.ex: The leaden sky made everyone feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 灰暗的天空让每个人都感到悲伤。
words.en: Something that is leaden is made of lead or is a dull, heavy, or grey color, or it is used to describe something that is very slow or lacking in energy.

words.tr: v. 驱散；消散；浪费；挥霍
words.ex: The fog will dissipate by noon.
words.ex_cn: 雾将在中午前消散。
words.en: If something dissipates or is dissipated, it becomes less or becomes less strong until it disappears or goes away completely.

words.tr:
v. （使）滴下；流口水；运球
n. 点滴；少量；口水
words.ex: The tap continues to dribble water.
words.ex_cn: 水龙头一直在滴水。
words.en: If a liquid dribbles somewhere, or if you dribble it, it drops down slowly or flows in a thin stream. In sports such as football and basketball, if you dribble the ball, you keep kicking or tapping it in order to keep it moving.

words.ex: The pig eats from the wooden trough.
words.ex_cn: 猪从木槽里吃东西。
words.en: A long, narrow open container for animals to eat or drink from; a period of low economic activity.

words.ex: Many families live in a small tenement in the city.
words.ex_cn: 许多家庭住在城市里的一间廉价公寓里。
words.en: A tenement is a large old building which is divided into a number of individual flats.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.tr:
v. 下毛毛雨；（毛毛雨似的）洒落
n. 毛毛细雨
words.ex: It is drizzling outside.
words.ex_cn: 外面正在下毛毛雨。
words.en: Light rain falling in very fine drops.

words.ex: The armistice was signed to end the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 停战协议的签署结束了冲突。
words.en: An armistice is a formal agreement of warring parties to stop fighting. It is not necessarily the end of a war, since it might be just a cessation of hostilities while an attempt is made to negotiate a lasting peace.

words.ex: The law will emancipate slaves.
words.ex_cn: 法律将解放奴隶。
words.en: To emancipate someone means to set them free from something that restricts their freedom to do what they want.

words.tr: n. 采伐森林；森林开伐；
words.ex: Deforestation is killing many animals.
words.ex_cn: 采伐森林正在杀死许多动物。
words.en: The act of cutting down or burning all the trees in an area.

words.tr: v. 侵入；侵占；侵犯；侵蚀
words.ex: The new building encroaches on the park.
words.ex_cn: 新建筑侵占了公园。
words.en: To gradually take something such as power or authority from someone else, often in a way that is not fair or legal.

words.ex: The small village lies on the periphery of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄位于城市的外围。
words.en: The outer limits or edge of an area or object.

words.ex: The depletion of natural resources is a serious problem.
words.ex_cn: 自然资源的损耗是一个严重的问题。
words.en: The act of reducing something by a large amount so that there is not enough left.

words.ex: Poverty can engender crime.
words.ex_cn: 贫困会引起犯罪。
words.en: To cause a feeling, situation, or condition to exist.

words.ex: The ozone layer protects us from the sun's harmful rays.
words.ex_cn: 臭氧层保护我们免受太阳有害射线的伤害。
words.en: The ozone layer is a layer in the Earth's stratosphere that contains a high concentration of ozone (O3) molecules, which absorb most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

words.tr: adj. 肮脏的；污秽的；卑劣的
words.ex: The squalid apartment had dirty floors and broken windows.
words.ex_cn: 这间肮脏的公寓地板很脏，窗户也破了。
words.en: If you describe a place as squalid, you mean that it is dirty, untidy, and in bad condition.

words.ex: He has a little stubble on his chin.
words.ex_cn: 他的下巴上有一点胡茬。
words.en: Stubble refers to the short, stiff stalks of grain or other crops left in a field after harvesting, or to the short, stiff hairs on a man's face when he has not shaved for a few days.

words.tr: v. 作…的摘要；成为…的缩影；概括；集中体现
words.ex: This painting epitomizes the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画概括了自然的美。
words.en: If you say that something or someone epitomizes a particular thing, you mean that they are a perfect example of it.

words.ex: The vagabond sleeps under the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 这个流浪汉睡在桥下。
words.en: A vagabond is someone who wanders from place to place without a home or job.

words.ex: The flowers exude a sweet smell.
words.ex_cn: 花朵散发出甜美的香味。
words.en: If someone exudes a quality or feeling, or if it exudes, they show that they have it to a great extent.

words.ex: The stench from the trash made me sick.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的臭味让我恶心。
words.en: A strong, very unpleasant smell.

words.ex: The precipitation increased last week.
words.ex_cn: 上周降水增加了。
words.en: Precipitation is rain, snow, sleet, or hail — any kind of weather condition where something's falling from the sky.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.tr:
n. 没收物；罚金
v. 丧失；被没收
words.ex: He had to pay a forfeit for breaking the rule.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规定不得不支付没收物。
words.en: If you forfeit something, you lose it or are forced to give it up because you have broken a rule or done something wrong.

words.ex: He is the breadwinner in his family.
words.ex_cn: 他是家里的经济支柱。
words.en: A breadwinner is a person who earns money to support their family.

words.ex: He lost his life in the car accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在车祸中丧生了。
words.en: To die, especially in a sudden or violent way.

words.ex: She bought a pink orchid for her mother.
words.ex_cn: 她为母亲买了一朵粉色的兰花。
words.en: A plant with complex flowers that are often brightly coloured, grown especially for its beautiful flowers.

words.ex: The seeds germinate in warm soil.
words.ex_cn: 种子在温暖的土壤中发芽。
words.en: To germinate means to begin to grow or develop, especially for a seed or spore.

words.ex: The plants grow in the conservatory.
words.ex_cn: 植物在温室里生长。
words.en: A conservatory is a room with glass walls and a glass roof, which is built on the side of a house. It is used as a sun lounge or for growing plants. It can also refer to a school where people are trained in music or acting.

words.ex: The sword slid easily into its sheath.
words.ex_cn: 剑很容易地滑入鞘中。
words.en: A sheath is a close-fitting cover for the blade of a knife or sword, or a similar protective covering for something else.

words.tr: adj. 嵌入的；镶嵌的；镶饰的； v. “inlay”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The table has an inlaid wooden design.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子有嵌入的木制图案。
words.en: Inlaid is the past tense and past participle of inlay, which means to embed pieces of a material into a surface to create a decorative pattern.

words.tr:
v. 闪亮；闪光
n. 闪亮；闪光
words.ex: The sun made the knife glint.
words.ex_cn: 阳光使刀子闪亮。
words.en: If something glints, it produces or reflects a quick flash of light.

words.ex: The box is inlaid with gold.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子镶嵌着金子。
words.en: To decorate an object by embedding pieces of a different material in it, so that they form a pattern or picture.

words.tr:
v. 汩汩地流；作咯咯声
n. 汩汩声；咯咯声
words.ex: The stream gurgles over the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 小溪在石头上汩汩流淌。
words.en: To make a bubbling sound, typically as a result of liquid flowing irregularly or of a person making a similar sound.

words.ex: They stood at the edge of the vale and said their goodbyes.
words.ex_cn: 他们站在溪谷边，互相道别。
words.en: A vale is a valley, used in poetry or in the names of places.

words.ex: The new law impinges on people's privacy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律侵犯了人们的隐私。
words.en: To impinge means to have an effect or influence, especially a negative one, on someone or something.

words.ex: The concept of oneness is central to many spiritual beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 统一性的概念是许多精神信仰的核心。
words.en: The state or quality of being one; singleness or unity.

words.tr: n. 神经症；神经衰弱症
words.ex: He has a neurosis about being late.
words.ex_cn: 他对迟到有一种神经症般的焦虑。
words.en: A neurosis is a mental illness that causes feelings of fear and worry, often leading to unreasonable behavior.

words.ex: He entered a deep hypnosis during the therapy.
words.ex_cn: 他在治疗过程中进入了深度催眠状态。
words.en: Hypnosis is a state in which a person seems to be asleep but can still see, hear, or respond to things said to them.

words.tr:
v. （使）连锁；（使）相互扣住
n. 互锁设备
words.ex: The puzzle pieces interlock tightly.
words.ex_cn: 拼图块紧密地互锁在一起。
words.en: To interlock means to fit together firmly or closely, or to cause things to fit together in this way.

words.ex: The car took a precipitous turn on the mountain road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在山路上急转弯。
words.en: A precipitous slope or cliff is very steep and often dangerous.

words.tr: adv. 仅仅；就；只是；刚刚；恰好；
words.ex: He just wants to sleep.
words.ex_cn: 他仅仅想睡觉。
words.en: Used to indicate that something is exactly the case or is happening at this moment.

words.tr:
adj. 僻静的；隐僻的； 退隐的
v. 隔离；隔绝；隐居；“seclude”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is secluded in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋坐落在树林中，十分僻静。
words.en: A secluded place is quiet, private, and not near people or things that disturb you.

words.ex: The house has good insulation to keep warm in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有良好的绝缘层以在冬天保暖。
words.en: Insulation is a material or substance that is used to stop heat, electricity, or sound from going from one place to another.

words.tr: v. 使声音降低；压抑（声音）；蒙住；裹
words.ex: He muffled his laugh with a pillow.
words.ex_cn: 他用枕头捂住笑声。
words.en: To muffle a sound is to make it quieter or less clear, often by covering it or wrapping it in something.

words.tr: v. 使残废；使残缺不全；毁伤
words.ex: The accident mutilated his hand.
words.ex_cn: 事故使他的手残废了。
words.en: To mutilate something or someone means to damage them severely, for example by cutting off or destroying part of them.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.tr:
v. 滴嗒地响；发出急速轻拍声
n. （急促的）啪嗒声；急速的轻拍声
words.ex: The rain patters on the roof.
words.ex_cn: 雨滴嗒地响在屋顶上。
words.en: If something patters, it makes a series of quick, light, tapping sounds.

words.ex: The airplane was parked in the hangar for maintenance.
words.ex_cn: 飞机被停在机库中进行维修。
words.en: A hangar is a large building in which aircraft are kept.

words.ex: He faced ostracism from his classmates for speaking up.
words.ex_cn: 他因为发声而遭到同学的排斥。
words.en: Ostracism is the act of excluding someone from a group or society by common consent.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.ex: The despotic king ruled with fear.
words.ex_cn: 这位专制的国王用恐惧统治。
words.en: If you say that someone is despotic, you are emphasizing that they use their power over other people in a very unfair or cruel way.

words.ex: He is a jew who celebrates Passover.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位庆祝逾越节的犹太人。
words.en: A Jew is a person whose religion is Judaism, or who is descended from the ancient Hebrew people.

words.ex: The teacher gave a round-up of the week's lessons.
words.ex_cn: 老师对本周的课程做了总结。
words.en: A round-up is a summary or collection of information or news items, or the act of gathering animals or people together.

words.ex: The issue polarized the community into two opposing groups.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题使社区分裂成了两个对立的群体。
words.en: To polarize means to cause something, especially a group or an issue, to divide into two sharply contrasting groups or sets of opinions or beliefs.

words.tr:
adj. 安详的；安静的；镇静的
v. 给…服镇静剂
words.ex: The sedate old man sat quietly by the window.
words.ex_cn: 那位安详的老人安静地坐在窗边。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sedate, you mean that they are quiet, calm, and dignified.

words.tr:
n. 预示；前兆；预感
v. 预示；预兆
words.ex: The dark clouds presage a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something presages a situation or event, it is considered to be a warning or sign of what is about to happen.

words.ex: The earthquake was a sudden cataclysm.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场突如其来的灾难。
words.en: A cataclysm is an event that causes great damage or makes a big change to something.

words.ex: The virus can propagate quickly among people.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以在人群中迅速传播。
words.en: To propagate something means to spread it and encourage more people to believe in it or support it.

words.ex: The lion belongs to the genus Panthera.
words.ex_cn: 狮子属于豹属。
words.en: A genus is a class of things which have common characteristics and which can be divided into subordinate kinds.

words.ex: The garden was filled with the sweet scent of narcissus.
words.ex_cn: 花园里弥漫着水仙花的甜美香气。
words.en: A narcissus is a plant with yellow or white flowers that appear in the spring. It is also used to refer to someone who is excessively self-absorbed.

words.ex: The boat stopped in a small cove near the island.
words.ex_cn: 船停在岛附近的一个小海湾里。
words.en: A cove is a small type of bay or coastal inlet. Coves usually have narrow, restricted entrances, are often circular or oval, and are often situated within a larger bay.

words.ex: The submarine used a periscope to observe the surface.
words.ex_cn: 潜艇使用潜望镜观察水面。
words.en: A periscope is an optical instrument that allows an observer to see things that are not in the direct line of sight, typically used in submarines to see above the water surface.

words.ex: The nail protrudes from the wood.
words.ex_cn: 钉子从木头里凸出来。
words.en: If something protrudes from somewhere, it sticks out.

words.tr: adj. 年老的；衰老的；老糊涂的
words.ex: The senile man forgot his son's name.
words.ex_cn: 这位年老的男子忘记了他儿子的名字。
words.en: If someone is senile, they are behaving in a confused or strange way, and unable to remember things, because they are old.

words.ex: He needs time to recuperate after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他需要时间在手术后恢复。
words.en: To recuperate means to recover from illness or exertion, or to regain or make up for something lost or damaged.

words.tr:
n. 伤寒
adj. 伤寒性的
words.ex: He got typhoid from drinking dirty water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了脏水后得了伤寒。
words.en: Typhoid is an infectious fever caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi, characterized by intestinal inflammation and ulceration.

words.tr: n. 兴致；热情；趣味；（用于调味的）柠檬皮；橙皮
words.ex: He cooks with zest and loves spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他做菜很有激情，喜欢辣的食物。
words.en: Great enthusiasm and energy.

words.tr: v. 使年轻； 使恢复精神； 使复原
words.ex: The new sleep routine helps rejuvenate her energy.
words.ex_cn: 新的睡眠习惯帮助她恢复精力。
words.en: To rejuvenate someone or something means to make them look or feel young, fresh, or lively again.

words.tr: v. （使）复活；（使）恢复知觉；（使）复兴
words.ex: The paramedics tried to resuscitate the man after he collapsed.
words.ex_cn: 当这位男子晕倒后，急救人员试图救活他。
words.en: To resuscitate someone means to bring them back to consciousness or to make them start breathing again after they have stopped.

words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.ex: The coroner examined the body to find the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 法医检查了尸体以确定死因。
words.en: A coroner is an official who is responsible for investigating the deaths of people who have died in a sudden, violent, or unusual way.

words.ex: He likes to seclude himself in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把自己 secluded 在森林里。
words.en: To seclude means to keep someone away from other people, or to keep something away from other things.

words.ex: The fir trees are tall and green in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 森林里的冷杉树高大而翠绿。
words.en: A fir is a type of evergreen tree that has needle-like leaves and produces cones.

words.tr:
v. 闷烧；冒烟；郁积
n. 闷烧
words.ex: The fire still smolders in the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 火还在壁炉里闷烧。
words.en: To burn slowly with smoke but without flame, or to exist in a suppressed state.

words.tr:
n. 草地；草坪；草皮
v. 铺草皮于
words.ex: The children played on the sod after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在草地上玩耍。
words.en: Sod refers to a piece of grassy turf or the act of covering the ground with such turf.

words.tr: v. （使）停滞；不发展；因不流动而变得污浊
words.ex: The economy began to stagnate after the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 经济在危机后开始停滞。
words.en: If something such as a business or project stagnates, it stops developing or making progress.

words.ex: The city showed signs of decadence after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这座城市显示出衰败的迹象。
words.en: Decadence is a situation in which a society or institution is becoming less moral and less satisfactory.

words.ex: He lives by hedonism, seeking pleasure every day.
words.ex_cn: 他奉行享乐主义，每天追求快乐。
words.en: Hedonism is the belief that gaining pleasure is the most important thing in life.

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.ex: His frugality helped him save money for years.
words.ex_cn: 他的节俭让他多年都存下了钱。
words.en: Frugality is the quality of being careful with money or food, so that you only spend what is necessary.

words.tr:
adj. 用柏油覆盖的
v. 耽搁；逗留
words.ex: The workers tarry at the road, waiting for the asphalt to dry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在道路上耽搁，等着沥青变干。
words.en: To tarry means to stay longer than intended or to delay leaving a place.

words.tr:
n. 泊位；（船上的）卧铺
v. 停泊；占铺位
words.ex: The ship found a berth at the dock.
words.ex_cn: 船在码头找到了停泊位。
words.en: A berth is a bed on a boat, train, or other vehicle, or a place where a boat or ship can be tied up in a harbor.

words.tr: n. 骑士精神；骑士制度；
words.ex: He showed chivalry by helping the lady carry her bags.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助那位女士提包，展现了骑士精神。
words.en: Chivalry is a set of qualities such as bravery, courtesy, honor, and gallantry toward women, associated with the medieval institution of knighthood.

words.ex: Strong foundations underpin the building.
words.ex_cn: 坚固的地基支撑着这栋建筑。
words.en: To support, strengthen, or provide a foundation for something.

words.ex: The soldier was honored for his valor in battle.
words.ex_cn: 这位士兵因在战斗中的英勇表现而受到表彰。
words.en: Valor is great courage, especially in a battle or war.

words.ex: He uses kerosene to light the lamp.
words.ex_cn: 他用煤油来点灯。
words.en: Kerosene is a type of fuel oil that is used in lamps, heaters, and jet engines.

words.tr:
v. 吹拂；（随风）飘荡；使飘荡
n. 一股（在空气中飘荡的味或烟）；风信旗；飘荡
words.ex: The smell of bread wafted from the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味从厨房里飘来。
words.en: If sounds or smells waft through the air, or if something such as a light wind wafts them, they move gently through the air.

words.ex: The city has recently installed a new incinerator to dispose of waste.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市最近安装了一台新的焚化炉来处理废物。
words.en: An incinerator is a large machine designed to burn waste materials at high temperatures, reducing them to ash and other residues.

words.ex: She is weaning her baby off milk.
words.ex_cn: 她正在让宝宝戒掉牛奶。
words.en: To wean someone off something means to make them gradually stop using or depending on it, especially something harmful or unnecessary.

words.ex: The company operates under the aegis of the government.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是在政府的保护下运营的。
words.en: The protection, backing, or support of a particular person or organization.

words.tr: phrase. 是时候做某事了；该做……了
words.ex: It's time to go to bed now.
words.ex_cn: 现在是睡觉的时间了。
words.en: A phrase indicating that the appropriate moment for a specific action has arrived.

chapters.name: Level 12 沟通类动词

words.ex: His domicile is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他的住所位于纽约。
words.en: A domicile is the place where a person lives or has their home.

words.ex: She beseeched him to stay with her.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下来陪她。
words.en: If you beseech someone to do something, you ask them very eagerly and anxiously.

words.tr:
n. 堤坝；排水沟
v. 筑堤；开排水沟
words.ex: The dike was built to prevent flooding.
words.ex_cn: 修建堤坝是为了防止洪水泛滥。
words.en: A dike is a long wall or embankment built to prevent flooding from the sea or a river.

words.tr: n. 演说者；演讲者；雄辩家；
words.ex: He is a famous orator who speaks at large events.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位在大型活动中演讲的著名演说者。
words.en: An orator is a person who delivers speeches or lectures, especially one who is skilled at doing so.

words.ex: The team canvass voters for their opinions.
words.ex_cn: 团队征询选民的意见。
words.en: To canvass means to ask people for their votes or opinions, especially in a political context, or to examine something carefully.

words.tr: n. 平民制定法；公民投票
words.ex: The government decided to hold a plebiscite to decide the future of the region.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定举行公民投票来决定该地区的未来。
words.en: A plebiscite is a direct vote by the electorate on an important public question such as a change in the constitution.

words.tr: phrase. 恳求；呼吁；请求帮助或支持
words.ex: They appeal for help from the government.
words.ex_cn: 他们向政府求助。
words.en: To make a serious or urgent request to the public for help, money, information, etc.

words.ex: The teacher chastised the boy for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为男孩在课堂上说话而责备了他。
words.en: To chastise someone means to punish or criticize them severely.

words.ex: The company paid indemnity for the damaged car.
words.ex_cn: 公司为损坏的汽车支付了保险赔偿。
words.en: If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss, especially in the form of a legal agreement.

words.ex: The serviceman returned home after the war.
words.ex_cn: 这名军人在战争结束后回到了家。
words.en: A serviceman is a man who is a member of the armed forces.

words.ex: He condescended to explain the simple math to his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他屈尊向弟弟解释了简单的数学。
words.en: If someone condescends to do something, they agree to do it in a way which shows that they think they are superior to the people they are doing it for.

words.tr: n. 游牧民；流浪者；游牧生活；流浪生活
words.ex: The nomad walks with his sheep across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 游牧民带着他的羊群穿越沙漠。
words.en: A nomad is someone who has no permanent home and moves according to the seasons from place to place in search of food, water, and grazing land.

words.tr: n. 阐述者；拥护者；代表者；指数
words.ex: He is the exponent of modern education reform.
words.ex_cn: 他是现代教育改革的阐述者。
words.en: An exponent is someone who supports and explains a particular idea, theory, or system, or a symbol that shows how many times a number is to be multiplied by itself.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.tr: n. 沙文主义；盲目的爱国心
words.ex: He shows chauvinism by thinking men are better than women.
words.ex_cn: 他认为男人比女人更好，表现出大男子主义。
words.en: Chauvinism is the strong and unreasonable belief that your own country or race is the best or most important.

words.ex: She embellished the dress with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用花朵装饰了这条裙子。
words.en: To embellish something means to make it more attractive by adding decorative details or features.

words.ex: He showed filial love by taking care of his old parents.
words.ex_cn: 他通过照顾年迈的父母表现出子女的孝心。
words.en: Filial is used to describe the relationship between children and their parents, especially emphasizing the duty and respect that children should show towards their parents.

words.ex: The story is an allegory about kindness.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是一个关于善良的寓言。
words.en: An allegory is a story, poem, or picture which can be interpreted to reveal a hidden meaning, typically a moral or political one.

words.ex: The judge enjoin him from selling the house.
words.ex_cn: 法官禁止他出售这所房子。
words.en: If a judge enjoins someone from doing something, they order them not to do it. If a judge enjoins an action, they order people not to do it.

words.tr: n. 要求者；索偿人；原告
words.ex: The claimant asked for money after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 索赔人在事故发生后要求赔偿。
words.en: A claimant is a person who makes a claim, especially in a legal case or for a state benefit.

words.tr: v. （清楚地）发音；清楚地表明；阐明
words.ex: He tries to enunciate each word clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他努力清晰地发出每个单词的音。
words.en: To enunciate means to pronounce words clearly and distinctly, or to state something clearly and in detail.

words.ex: He spoke with clear diction.
words.ex_cn: 他说话吐字清晰。
words.en: Diction refers to the choice and use of words and phrases in speech or writing, or the manner in which words are pronounced.

words.ex: He expounded his ideas clearly in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上清楚地阐述了他的观点。
words.en: To expound means to explain something in detail, especially a theory, idea, or point of view.

words.tr: n. 赞美诗；（圣经中的）诗篇
words.ex: He sang a psalm in church on Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他在周日的教堂里唱了一首赞美诗。
words.en: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, in particular any of those contained in the biblical Book of Psalms and used in Christian and Jewish worship.

words.tr:
adj. 道德败坏的；堕落的；腐化的
v. 使堕落；使腐化；使败坏；“deprave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The movie showed a depraved man who hurt others.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一个堕落的人，他伤害了别人。
words.en: If you describe someone as depraved, you mean that they are morally very bad or evil.

words.ex: He is a fiend for video games.
words.ex_cn: 他是个视频游戏迷。
words.en: A fiend is a very wicked or cruel person, or someone who is extremely enthusiastic about something.

words.ex: The teacher imbues her students with confidence.
words.ex_cn: 老师赋予学生信心。
words.en: If someone or something is imbued with a particular quality, feeling, or value, they are filled with it or characterized by it.

words.ex: His argument is based on a fallacy.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点基于一个谬误。
words.en: A fallacy is an idea which many people believe to be true, but which is in fact false because it is based on incorrect information or reasoning.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 莽撞的；有勇无谋的
words.ex: He made a foolhardy decision to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个有勇无谋的决定，独自去爬山。
words.en: If you describe behavior or an action as foolhardy, you mean that it is very risky because it shows a lack of thought or care for the possible consequences.

words.tr: phrase. 犯抢劫罪；实施抢劫
words.ex: He will commit a robbery if he is not stopped.
words.ex_cn: 如果没有人阻止他，他就会抢劫。
words.en: To perform the act of stealing from someone or somewhere, especially using force or the threat of force.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄
n. 嘲笑；讥笑的言语
words.ex: The crowd began to jeer at the losing team.
words.ex_cn: 观众开始对落败的队伍嘘声四起。
words.en: To jeer means to laugh at someone or shout rude remarks at them in order to show that you do not respect them.

words.ex: He wore formal attire to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了正式服装去参加婚礼。
words.en: Clothes, especially fine or formal ones.

words.ex: He tried to pacify the crying baby with a toy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个玩具让哭闹的婴儿安静下来。
words.en: If you pacify someone who is angry, upset, or not pleased, you make them calm or content.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；坏脾气的；乖戾的
words.ex: She had a peevish tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种易怒的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as peevish, you mean that they are easily irritated by unimportant things.

words.ex: He gave a conciliatory smile to calm the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他露出和解的微笑来平息争执。
words.en: If you are conciliatory, you show that you are willing to end a disagreement with someone by doing or saying things that will please them.

words.tr:
v. 假定；要求
n. 假定；假设
words.ex: He postulates that all humans are equal.
words.ex_cn: 他假定所有人都是平等的。
words.en: If you postulate something, you suggest it as the basis for a theory, argument, or calculation.

words.ex: The experience was a salutary lesson in the importance of preparation.
words.ex_cn: 这次经历是一个关于准备重要性的有益教训。
words.en: A salutary experience or warning is one that has a good effect or influence, especially by showing you the bad results of a particular action or behaviour.

words.ex: The teacher learned new pedagogy from the workshop.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师从研讨会中学到了新的教学法。
words.en: The method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject or theoretical concept.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.tr: n. 意志力；自愿选择；自行决断
words.ex: He did it of his own volition.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于自己的意愿做的。
words.en: The power to make your own decisions or choices.

words.tr: n. 投票；选举权；参政权
words.ex: Women won suffrage in 1920.
words.ex_cn: 女性在1920年获得了选举权。
words.en: Suffrage is the right to vote in political elections.

words.tr: adj. 愉快活泼的；轻快的；精力充沛的；精神矍铄的
words.ex: The old man walks sprightly every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人每天早上都轻快地走路。
words.en: Someone who is sprightly is lively and active, especially in a way that makes you feel happy.

words.ex: We sit together and reminisce about old times.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在一起回忆过去的时光。
words.en: If you reminisce about something from your past, you write or talk about it, often with pleasure.

words.tr: n. 纪念品；用以回忆的东西
words.ex: She keeps a photo as a memento of her trip.
words.ex_cn: 她保留了一张照片作为旅行的纪念品。
words.en: A memento is an object which you keep because it reminds you of a person or a special event.

words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.ex: They had an altercation over the parking space.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为停车空间发生了争吵。
words.en: An altercation is a noisy argument or disagreement, especially in public.

words.tr:
v. 轻拳出击；拌嘴
n. 粗杆；桅
words.ex: He sparred with his friend in the boxing ring.
words.ex_cn: 他在拳击台上和朋友进行了对练。
words.en: To spar means to engage in boxing or to argue. As a noun, it can refer to a mast of a ship or a type of mineral.

words.tr: adj. 固执己见的；顽固的
words.ex: He is opinionated and never changes his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很有主见，从不改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as opinionated, you mean that they have very strong opinions and refuse to accept that they may be wrong.

words.tr:
v. 吱吱喳喳；嘁嘁喳喳地讲
n. 叽叽喳喳的叫声
words.ex: The birds twitter in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在早晨吱吱喳喳地叫。
words.en: If a bird twitters, it makes a series of short, high sounds.

words.ex: The meeting felt interminable.
words.ex_cn: 这场会议感觉没完没了。
words.en: If you describe something as interminable, you are emphasizing that it continues for a very long time and indicating that you find it boring or annoying.

words.tr: phrase. 不停地；持续不断地；没完没了地
words.ex: The rain went on and on all night.
words.ex_cn: 雨整晚不停地下。
words.en: Continuing without stopping or pausing.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr:
n. 性格外向者；爱交际的人
adj. 外向的
words.ex: He is an extrovert who loves talking to people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的人，喜欢和人交谈。
words.en: An extrovert is someone who is very outgoing, sociable, and enjoys being around other people.

words.tr: v. 担保；保证；确定；断言；
words.ex: I will vouch for his honesty.
words.ex_cn: 我为他的诚实作担保。
words.en: If you vouch for someone, you provide evidence or assurance of their good character or the truth of their statements.

chapters.name: Level 12 动作类动词

words.ex: The cavalry charged quickly across the field.
words.ex_cn: 骑兵迅速冲过田野。
words.en: The cavalry refers to the part of an army that originally fought on horseback, now typically used in modern armies to refer to units that are mobile and intended for rapid deployment.

words.tr:
v. 缓行；溜蹄
n. 溜蹄；缓行漫步
words.ex: He amble through the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里缓行。
words.en: To walk at a slow, relaxed pace, especially for pleasure.

words.ex: The main thoroughfare was closed for the parade.
words.ex_cn: 主要大道因游行而关闭。
words.en: A thoroughfare is a main road or public path that is used by a lot of people and vehicles.

words.ex: He lives in a quiet borough of New York.
words.ex_cn: 他住在纽约的一个安静的行政区。
words.en: A borough is a town, or a district within a large city, that has its own local government.

words.tr:
n. 船长；运动队队长
v. 担任船长、球队队长等
words.ex: The skipper guided the boat safely through the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船长带领船只安全地穿过了风暴。
words.en: The person who is in charge of a ship or boat.

words.tr: n. 板条；曲尺；扣板；小方材; vt. 在……钉扣板；养肥；装条板; vi. 长胖；贪吃; n. ...
words.ex: He used a nail to batten the loose board.
words.ex_cn: 他用钉子把松动的木板钉牢。
words.en: To fasten or secure with battens; a strip of wood or other material used to fasten or secure something.

words.tr: adj. 颤抖的；战栗的；畏缩的
words.ex: Her voice was tremulous when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时声音颤抖。
words.en: If someone's voice, smile, or actions are tremulous, they are unsteady because the person is uncertain, afraid, or upset.

words.ex: The dog cowers when the thunder sounds.
words.ex_cn: 当雷声响起时，狗会蜷缩起来。
words.en: To crouch down in fear.

words.tr: adj. 又黑又脏的；昏暗的；肮脏的
words.ex: The room was dingy and small.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间又脏又小。
words.en: If you describe a place or thing as dingy, you mean that it is rather dull and depressing to look at, and perhaps also dirty.

words.tr:
adj. 臭虫多的
n. 轻型马车；婴儿车
words.ex: The old cabin is buggy after the summer rain.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧小屋在夏雨后虫子很多。
words.en: A buggy is a small, lightweight vehicle, often open and with four wheels, used for recreation or transportation over rough terrain.

words.tr:
n. 咯吱声或叽嘎声
v. 发出咯吱声或叽嘎声
words.ex: The door creaked when he opened it.
words.ex_cn: 他开门时，门发出了吱呀声。
words.en: If something creaks, it makes a short, high-pitched sound when it moves.

words.ex: We took a detour to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们绕道以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A detour is a longer, less direct way to go somewhere, used to avoid a problem or to visit something along the way.

words.ex: The door handle was unobtrusive and blended with the wall.
words.ex_cn: 门把手不显眼，与墙壁融为一体。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unobtrusive, you mean that they are not easily noticed or do not draw attention to themselves.

words.tr: n. 护士长；女舍监；已婚妇女
words.ex: The matron checked on the sick children at night.
words.ex_cn: 女管理员晚上查看生病的孩子们。
words.en: A matron is a woman in charge of domestic and medical arrangements in a boarding school, hospital, or other institution.

words.ex: He cringed when he heard the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到巨大的噪音时，他畏缩了。
words.en: If you cringe at something, you feel embarrassed or disgusted, and perhaps show this feeling in your expression or by making a slight movement.

words.tr:
n. 骑士；勋章获得者；骑士风度的男子
adj. 傲慢的；豪强的；（对女人）献殷勤的；大方的
words.ex: The knight rode on a horse like a cavalier.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士骑着马，像个骑士一样。
words.en: If you describe someone as cavalier, you are criticizing them because you think that they do not consider other people's feelings or take account of the seriousness of a situation.

words.tr:
n. 钩针编织品
v. 钩织
words.ex: She spent the afternoon crocheting a scarf.
words.ex_cn: 她整个下午都在用钩针编织围巾。
words.en: Crochet is a process of creating fabric by interlocking loops of yarn, thread, or strands of other materials using a crochet hook.

words.ex: She wore a long frock to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条长连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: A frock is a dress, especially one that is worn by women or girls.

words.ex: His visage showed deep sadness.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出深深的悲伤。
words.en: The appearance of the face or facial expression of a person.

words.ex: She daubed the wall with paint.
words.ex_cn: 她在墙上随意涂抹颜料。
words.en: To daub means to spread a substance such as paint, mud, or oil over a surface in a rough or careless way.

words.tr: adj. 亵渎神圣的；大不敬的
words.ex: He made a sacrilegious joke about the church.
words.ex_cn: 他开了一个关于教堂的亵渎神明的玩笑。
words.en: If someone's behaviour or actions are sacrilegious, they show great disrespect towards something holy or something that people think should be respected.

words.ex: He faced public denunciation for his lies.
words.ex_cn: 他因撒谎而遭到公众的谴责。
words.en: Denunciation is the act of criticizing something or someone strongly and publicly.

words.tr: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；吓倒
words.ex: The loud noise did not daunt her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音并没有吓倒她。
words.en: If something daunts you, it makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.tr: n. 讲坛；指挥台；领奖台
words.ex: He stood on the rostrum to give a speech.
words.ex_cn: 他站在讲台上发表演讲。
words.en: A rostrum is a raised platform on which someone stands to make a public speech, receive an award or medal, or conduct an orchestra.

words.tr: v. 浸入水中；泼上水；熄灭
words.ex: He doused the burning log in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把燃烧的木头浸入水中。
words.en: To douse something means to quickly throw water over it in order to put out a fire, or to pour a lot of liquid over it.

words.ex: The corn has a dry husk around it.
words.ex_cn: 玉米外面有一层干外壳。
words.en: The outer covering of some fruits and seeds, especially when it is dry and hard.

words.ex: Workers excavate the old ruins with shovels.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用铲子挖掘古代遗址。
words.en: To excavate means to dig in the ground in order to find things that have been buried there, such as archaeological remains.

words.tr: n. 首饰盒，匣子，<美>棺材
words.ex: She kept her most precious jewels in a small casket.
words.ex_cn: 她把她最珍贵的珠宝放在一个小匣子里。
words.en: A casket is a box used for holding the body of a dead person for burial, or a small box for keeping valuable items such as jewelry.

words.ex: He helped extricate the car from the mud.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助把车从泥里解脱出来。
words.en: If you extricate someone or something from a place where they are trapped or caught, you succeed in freeing them.

words.ex: The children played on the big dune near the sea.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在海边的大沙丘上玩耍。
words.en: A dune is a hill of sand near the sea or in a desert, formed by the wind.

words.tr:
n. 连枷
v. 用连枷打；胡乱摆动；用力地挥动
words.ex: The farmer flails the wheat to separate the grains.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用连枷打小麦以分离谷粒。
words.en: A flail is a tool used for threshing grain, consisting of a long handle with a freely swinging stick or bar attached to it. As a verb, to flail means to wave or swing wildly; to thrash about.

words.tr: n. 精神错乱；谵妄；极度兴奋
words.ex: The patient was in a state of delirium after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 手术后，病人处于精神错乱的状态。
words.en: A state of wild excitement or mental confusion, often accompanied by hallucinations.

words.ex: He didn't flinch when the needle touched his skin.
words.ex_cn: 当针碰到他的皮肤时，他没有退缩。
words.en: If you flinch, you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.

words.tr:
v. 发出砰的一声
n. 重击声；砰的一声
words.ex: The book fell to the floor with a thud.
words.ex_cn: 书掉到地板上，发出一声闷响。
words.en: A thud is a dull sound, such as that which a heavy object makes when it hits something soft.

words.tr:
v. 轻快地掠过；突然换位；搬家
n. 掠过；迅速飞过；偷偷搬家
words.ex: The butterfly flits from flower to flower.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶在花朵间飞舞。
words.en: To move quickly and lightly from one place to another.

words.ex: She wore a wreath of fresh sprigs around her head.
words.ex_cn: 她在头上戴了一个新鲜小枝编成的花环。
words.en: A small shoot or twig of a plant, especially one cut from a plant for decoration or planting.

words.tr: 短语，从一枝到另一枝，形容植物间细小部分的连续或传递，常用于诗意或比喻语境中
words.ex: The rabbit jumped from sprig to sprig.
words.ex_cn: 兔子从一簇嫩枝跳到另一簇嫩枝。
words.en: From one small shoot or branch to another; covering a complete cycle or range.

words.ex: Owls are nocturnal animals.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰是夜间活动的动物。
words.en: Nocturnal means happening in the night or active at night.

words.ex: The lynx lives in cold forests.
words.ex_cn: 猞猁生活在寒冷的森林中。
words.en: A lynx is a wild animal that is similar to a large cat and has thick fur, long legs, and a short tail. Lynxes are known for their keen eyesight.

words.ex: The lion returned to its lair at night.
words.ex_cn: 狮子晚上回到了它的兽穴。
words.en: A lair is a place where a wild animal lives, often hidden or difficult to find.

words.tr:
v. 搜寻；（动物）觅食；
n. 饲料；草料；
words.ex: The bear forages for berries in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这只熊在森林里搜寻浆果。
words.en: If you forage, you search for food or other supplies. Forage can also refer to food for animals, especially when it is grown or collected.

words.tr:
v. （在食物上）加装饰菜；装饰
n. （食物上的）装饰菜；装饰
words.ex: She puts a lemon slice to garnish the drink.
words.ex_cn: 她放一片柠檬来装饰这杯饮料。
words.en: To garnish something means to decorate it with something, especially food with small amounts of different foods.

words.ex: The hunter bagged a pheasant for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 猎人捕获了一只雉鸡作为晚餐。
words.en: A pheasant is a large bird with a long tail, often hunted for sport or food.

words.ex: He ate a ripe persimmon for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一个熟透的柿子。
words.en: A persimmon is a soft, orange fruit that is sweet when ripe and grows on a tree.

words.tr:
v. 磨碎；磨擦；（使）烦躁；发出磨擦声
n. 炉栅；炉箅
words.ex: The food was grated into small pieces.
words.ex_cn: 食物被擦成了小块。
words.en: To grate means to reduce food to small shreds by rubbing it on a grater. It can also mean to make a harsh, scraping sound or to cause irritation or annoyance.

words.ex: The boy caught a squid at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在海滩上抓到一只鱿鱼。
words.en: A squid is a sea creature with a long soft body and many tentacles around its mouth.

words.ex: He had a loud hiccup during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间打了个响亮的嗝。
words.en: A hiccup is an involuntary spasm of the diaphragm and respiratory organs, with a sudden closure of the glottis and a characteristic sound.

words.ex: He is a glutton who eats too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他是个贪吃糖的暴食者。
words.en: A glutton is a person who eats and drinks excessively or voraciously.

words.ex: The workers used a hoist to lift the heavy beams.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用吊升机械吊起沉重的梁。
words.en: To hoist something means to lift or pull it up to a higher position, usually using some kind of equipment such as a crane or pulley.

words.tr: n. 冒充内行者；庸医；骗子
words.ex: He is a charlatan who pretends to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: A charlatan is someone who pretends to have skills or knowledge that they do not really possess.

words.ex: He tried to impersonate a police officer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图冒充一名警察。
words.en: To impersonate someone means to pretend to be that person, either to deceive people or to entertain them.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.ex: The nave of the church is long and bright.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的中殿又长又明亮。
words.en: The central part of a church building, intended to accommodate most of the congregation. In traditional Western churches, the nave extends from the entrance to the chancel and is flanked by lower aisles.

words.ex: He inscribes his name on the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在石头上。
words.en: To write, mark, or engrave (words, symbols, etc.) on a surface, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.tr:
adj. 镀金的；烫金的
v. 给…镀金；涂金于…；“gild”的过去式和过去分词
n. 镀金部分；金边证券
words.ex: The frame was covered with gilt.
words.ex_cn: 这个框架被镀上了金。
words.en: Something that is gilt is covered with a thin layer of gold or gold paint.

words.ex: Her infatuation with the movie star lasted only a few weeks.
words.ex_cn: 她对那位电影明星的迷恋只持续了几个星期。
words.en: An infatuation is an intense but short-lived passion or admiration for someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 挤；推；撞；争夺
n. 挤拥；推撞
words.ex: People jostle in the crowded market.
words.ex_cn: 人们在拥挤的市场里推挤。
words.en: To jostle someone means to push or knock against them, usually in a crowd.

words.ex: The queen was resplendent in her golden crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着金色王冠，光彩夺目。
words.en: Something that is resplendent is very bright and attractive, often because it is richly decorated or very colorful.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；轻浮的；不严肃的
words.ex: His flippant remarks annoyed everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他轻率的言论让会议上的每个人都感到恼火。
words.en: If you describe a person or what they say as flippant, you are criticizing them because you think they are not taking something as seriously as they should.

words.ex: He is loitering near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他正在公园附近闲逛。
words.en: If someone loiters somewhere, they remain there or walk up and down without any real purpose.

words.ex: He buys lunch in the school canteen.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校食堂买午餐。
words.en: A canteen is a place in a factory, office, or school where meals are served, often at a lower cost than in restaurants. It can also refer to a small container for carrying water or other drinks.

words.tr: adj. 郁闷的；抑郁的；孤僻的
words.ex: He was morose after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得忧郁。
words.en: If you describe someone as morose, you mean that they are very unhappy, bad-tempered, and unwilling to talk or be sociable.

words.ex: Oil helps to lubricate the engine parts.
words.ex_cn: 油有助于润滑发动机部件。
words.en: To apply a substance such as oil or grease to (something) in order to minimize friction and allow smooth movement.

words.tr:
n. 车床
v. 用车床加工
words.ex: He uses a lathe to shape wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用车床加工木材。
words.en: A lathe is a machine tool that rotates a workpiece about an axis of rotation to perform various operations such as cutting, sanding, knurling, drilling, or deformation with tools that are applied to the workpiece to create an object with symmetry about that axis.

words.tr:
n. 猛冲；冲刺；扑
v. 猛冲；冲刺；扑
words.ex: He made a sudden lunge at the ball.
words.ex_cn: 他突然向前扑向球。
words.en: If you lunge in a particular direction, you move in that direction suddenly and forcefully.

words.ex: The bison walks slowly across the grassland.
words.ex_cn: 野牛慢慢地走过草原。
words.en: A bison is a large, wild animal that is related to the cow and is native to North America and Europe. Bison have a large head, a humped back, and are covered with thick, shaggy hair.

words.ex: He threw the javelin farther than anyone else.
words.ex_cn: 他投出的标枪比任何人都远。
words.en: A javelin is a light spear designed primarily for casting as a ranged weapon.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；（危险而愚蠢的）冒险行为
words.ex: His funny escapade made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他那滑稽的淘气行为让大家都笑了。
words.en: An escapade is an exciting and somewhat dangerous adventure, especially one that is not very sensible or is against the rules.

words.ex: He was arrested for molesting a child.
words.ex_cn: 他因骚扰儿童而被逮捕。
words.en: To molest someone means to assault or harass them, especially sexually.

words.tr: phrase. 涉及；专心； 卷入
words.ex: He is involved in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他参与了学校的戏剧表演。
words.en: To be included or participate in something, especially something that requires a lot of time or effort.

words.ex: The cessation of rain allowed us to go outside.
words.ex_cn: 雨停了，我们就能出去了。
words.en: The fact or process of ending or being brought to an end.

words.tr:
v. 剥...的皮；投掷；急降；急跑
n. 毛皮；投掷；猛落；疾行
words.ex: The hunter pelted the fox after catching it.
words.ex_cn: 猎人抓到狐狸后剥了它的皮。
words.en: The skin of an animal with the fur or hair still on it, or to attack someone by throwing a lot of things at them.

words.tr: adj. 憔悴的；形容枯槁的
words.ex: He looked haggard after working all night.
words.ex_cn: 他熬了一整夜后看起来憔悴不堪。
words.en: Someone who is haggard looks exhausted and unwell, often because they have been through a very difficult or stressful experience.

words.tr:
v. 艰难地行走；吃力地行进
n. 劳苦；沉重的脚步（声）
words.ex: He plodded through the snow with heavy boots.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着沉重的靴子艰难地在雪地中行走。
words.en: To plod means to walk slowly with heavy steps, especially because you are tired or working hard. It can also mean to work slowly and steadily at something, especially something that is boring or difficult.

words.ex: The glacial landscape was covered in snow.
words.ex_cn: 冰河地貌被雪覆盖着。
words.en: relating to, resulting from, or denoting the presence or agency of ice, especially in the form of glaciers.

words.tr: n. 兀鹫；秃鹫；贪得无厌的人
words.ex: The vulture is flying high above the desert.
words.ex_cn: 秃鹫在沙漠上空高飞。
words.en: A vulture is a large bird that lives in hot countries and eats dead animals.

words.tr:
v. 猛扑；突袭；抓住
n. 猛扑
words.ex: The cat will pounce on the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫会扑向老鼠。
words.en: If someone pounces on you, they come up towards you suddenly and take hold of you.

words.ex: The eagle gripped the rabbit with its talon.
words.ex_cn: 老鹰用它的爪子抓住了兔子。
words.en: The claw of a bird of prey.

words.ex: She bought a wicker basket for the picnic.
words.ex_cn: 她为野餐买了一个柳条篮子。
words.en: Wicker is the material made from weaving thin branches or twigs, especially from willows, used to make baskets, furniture, etc.

words.tr:
n. 雪橇
v. 乘雪橇
words.ex: The children enjoyed riding on the sleigh.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢乘雪橇。
words.en: A sleigh is a vehicle which slides over snow, usually pulled by a horse.

words.tr:
n. 噘嘴；发脾气；大头鱼类
v. 撅嘴
words.ex: The child made a pout when he didn't get candy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子没得到糖果时撅起了嘴。
words.en: If someone pouts, they stick out their lips, usually in order to show that they are annoyed or to make themselves sexually attractive.

words.ex: The fishermen caught a large mackerel.
words.ex_cn: 渔夫捕获了一条大鲭鱼。
words.en: A mackerel is a sea fish with a greenish-blue back and silvery sides, often used as food.

words.ex: The cat sleeps in the nook by the window.
words.ex_cn: 猫在窗边的角落睡觉。
words.en: A nook is a small, sheltered, and secluded place.

words.tr:
v. （猫等满足地）发出呼噜声；（机器等）发出隆隆声；（人）轻柔地说话
n. （猫发出的）咕噜声；（机器等）颤动声
words.ex: The cat purrs when she is happy.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫在开心时会发出呼噜声。
words.en: When a cat purrs, it makes a low, continuous, vibrating sound that shows it is contented.

words.tr: phrase. 躺倒在…里；在…中躺下
words.ex: He lies down in bed when he feels tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到累的时候，他就躺在床上。
words.en: To recline or place oneself horizontally on a surface.

words.ex: He sent a letter of condolence to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他给朋友寄了一封慰问信。
words.en: An expression of sympathy, especially on the occasion of a death.

words.tr:
adj. 丧失近亲的；丧失密友的
v. 夺去；使丧失；“bereave”的过去式
words.ex: The bereaved mother cried quietly at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 这位失去孩子的母亲在葬礼上静静地哭泣。
words.en: If someone is bereaved, a relative or close friend has just died.

words.tr:
v. （声音）颤抖
n. 颤抖的声音
words.ex: His voice quavers when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他的声音会颤抖。
words.en: If someone's voice quavers, it is unsteady because the person is uncertain, nervous, or upset.

words.tr: 短语动词. 表示哀悼，表示慰问（通常在某人去世后向其家属表示同情）
words.ex: He called to express his condolences after hearing about the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他打电话来对事故发生表示哀悼。
words.en: To express sympathy or sorrow for someone who has experienced a loss, especially by death.

words.ex: The window was covered with a lattice of iron bars.
words.ex_cn: 窗户被铁条格子覆盖。
words.en: A lattice is a structure consisting of strips of wood or metal crossed and fastened together with square or diamond-shaped spaces left between.

words.ex: The thieves ransacked the house for money.
words.ex_cn: 小偷把房子翻了个底朝天找钱。
words.en: To search a place thoroughly, often causing disorder or damage.

words.ex: The otter swam quickly in the river.
words.ex_cn: 水獭在河里快速游动。
words.en: An otter is a furry aquatic mammal that is known for its playful behavior and ability to swim gracefully.

words.ex: He recoiled when he saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到蛇时，他退缩了。
words.en: If something makes you recoil, you move your body quickly away from it because it frightens, offends, or hurts you.

words.ex: The hedgehog walks slowly in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 刺猬在花园里慢慢走。
words.en: A hedgehog is a small, nocturnal mammal with a coat of sharp spines, which it uses for protection against predators.

words.ex: He screamed at the sight of a snake.
words.ex_cn: 他一看到蛇就尖叫了。
words.en: Upon seeing something or someone, immediately.

words.tr: adj. 有狂风暴雨的；狂暴的
words.ex: The tempestuous sea made the voyage dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨的海面使得航行变得危险。
words.en: If you describe a relationship or a situation as tempestuous, you mean that it is full of strong emotions, especially anger or passion.

words.tr:
n. 褶边；褶饰
v. 弄皱；弄乱；扰乱
words.ex: The dress has a pink ruffle at the bottom.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子的底部有一条粉色的褶边。
words.en: To ruffle something means to disturb its smoothness or neatness, making it uneven or messy.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；乖戾的；傲慢的
words.ex: The surly man refused to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 那个脾气暴躁的人拒绝打招呼。
words.en: If someone is surly, they are unfriendly and bad-tempered.

words.ex: He gave her a scowl when she was late.
words.ex_cn: 她迟到时，他皱了皱眉。
words.en: When someone scowls, they look at someone or something with an angry or irritated expression.

words.ex: His antic behavior made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的行为让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as antic, you mean that it is strange and foolish in a way that is amusing.

words.tr: v. （忙乱地）扒寻，摸索；（为了找到或抓牢）抓，摸；（动物）用爪子乱抓，挣扎；乱涂；在……上乱扒；...
words.ex: He scrabbled through the drawer to find his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他忙乱地在抽屉里翻找他的钥匙。
words.en: If you scrabble for something, you make hurried movements with your fingers to try to get hold of it.

words.tr: n. 有围栏的幼儿床；轻便小床；
words.ex: The baby sleeps in a cot beside the bed.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿睡在床边的婴儿床里。
words.en: A cot is a small bed for a baby, with high sides to prevent the baby from falling out.

words.tr:
n. 挂锁；扣锁
v. 用挂锁锁上
words.ex: He secured the gate with a padlock.
words.ex_cn: 他用挂锁锁住了大门。
words.en: A padlock is a lock which is used for fastening two things together, for example two parts of a door or a lid on a container. It consists of a block of metal with a U-shaped bar attached to it. One end of the bar is released by turning a key in the lock.

words.ex: The wind began to slacken after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风速开始减缓。
words.en: If something slackens or if you slacken it, it becomes slower, less active, or less intense.

words.tr: n. 倾斜度；坡度；梯度；斜坡
words.ex: The hill has a steep gradient.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一个陡峭的坡度。
words.en: A gradient is a slope or a degree of inclination, especially in a road or railway.

words.ex: The snake slithered through the grass.
words.ex_cn: 蛇在草丛中滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and quietly with a twisting or oscillating motion, like a snake.

words.tr:
n. 丛；笨重的脚步声；土块
v. 使成一丛；凝结成块；拖着沉重的步子走
words.ex: The grass formed a clump near the fence.
words.ex_cn: 草在篱笆附近长成了一簇。
words.en: A clump of things such as trees or plants is a small group of them growing together. A clump of earth or mud is a small, solid mass of it.

words.ex: She snip the paper with scissors.
words.ex_cn: 她用剪刀剪纸。
words.en: To cut something with scissors in a quick, small movement.

words.tr: n. 细须；连鬓胡子；略微
words.ex: The cat's whisker touched the edge of the bowl.
words.ex_cn: 猫的细须碰到了碗的边缘。
words.en: A whisker is one of the long stiff hairs that grow near the mouth of a cat, mouse, or other mammal.

words.ex: He snoozed for ten minutes after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后小睡了十分钟。
words.en: If you snooze, you sleep lightly for a short period of time.

words.ex: The guests waited in the anteroom before being called for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 客人们在被叫去吃饭之前在前厅等候。
words.en: A small room leading to a main one, often used as a waiting area.

words.ex: He used tongs to pick up the hot bread.
words.ex_cn: 他用夹子夹起热面包。
words.en: A tool consisting of two movable arms joined at one end, used for picking up and holding things.

words.tr:
v. 蹲；蹲坐；擅自占住
n. 蹲；偷住的房子；蹲坐
adj. 矮而宽的；矮胖的
words.ex: He does a squat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做深蹲。
words.en: If you squat, you lower yourself towards the ground, balancing on your feet with your legs bent.

words.ex: The child squirted water from the hose.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从软管里喷出水。
words.en: To squirt means to force out liquid in a thin fast stream or to be forced out in this way.

words.tr: n. 鸟舍；大鸟笼；鸟类饲养场
words.ex: The aviary was filled with a variety of exotic birds.
words.ex_cn: 这个大型鸟舍里充满了各种珍奇的鸟类。
words.en: An aviary is a large enclosure for keeping birds in, which allows them to fly around freely.

words.ex: The doctor used antiseptic cream on the cut.
words.ex_cn: 医生在伤口上用了防腐药膏。
words.en: An antiseptic is a substance that prevents the growth of disease-causing microorganisms.

words.tr: v. 装载；装填；妥善放置
words.ex: He stowed the boxes in the truck.
words.ex_cn: 他把箱子装上了卡车。
words.en: To stow something means to pack it or store it neatly in a particular place.

words.ex: The ship took on ballast to stay stable in rough water.
words.ex_cn: 船为了在恶劣水域中保持稳定，装载了压舱物。
words.en: Ballast is heavy material that is carried in a ship or hot-air balloon to make it more stable.

words.tr: v. （使）窒息而死；使呼吸困难；闷死
words.ex: The smoke is suffocating him.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾正在让他窒息。
words.en: To cause someone to die or to make it difficult for someone to breathe by preventing air from reaching the lungs.

words.tr: n. 抽搐；痉挛；动乱；骚动
words.ex: The child had a convulsion after the fever spiked.
words.ex_cn: 孩子发烧突然升高后发生了抽搐。
words.en: A convulsion is a medical condition where the body shakes uncontrollably because of a disturbance in the brain.

words.ex: He has epilepsy and takes medicine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他患有癫痫，每天服药。
words.en: A neurological disorder characterized by sudden recurrent episodes of sensory disturbance, loss of consciousness, or convulsions, associated with abnormal electrical activity in the brain.

words.ex: The angler sits by the river and waits for fish.
words.ex_cn: 钓鱼的人坐在河边等待鱼上钩。
words.en: An angler is someone who fishes with a fishing rod as a hobby or sport.

words.tr:
v. 抽打；连续击打；翻来覆去；击溃
n. 快节奏重金属摇滚乐；聚会；连续击打
words.ex: The teacher used a stick to thrash the naughty boy.
words.ex_cn: 老师用棍子抽打了那个调皮的男孩。
words.en: To beat someone or something violently and repeatedly.

words.tr:
v. 扭打；混战
n. 扭打；混战
words.ex: The two boys had a scuffle over the ball.
words.ex_cn: 两个男孩为了球打了一架。
words.en: A scuffle is a short, confused fight or struggle at close quarters.

words.tr: v. 蹒跚；踉跄；摇摇欲坠
words.ex: The old man totters when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人走路时摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move in a feeble or unsteady way.

words.ex: The eagle unfurled its wings and soared into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 鹰展开翅膀，翱翔于天空。
words.en: If you unfurl something rolled or folded such as an umbrella, sail, or flag, you open it, so that it is spread out. You can also say that it unfurls.

words.ex: The main purpose of nuclear weapons is deterrence.
words.ex_cn: 核武器的主要目的是威慑。
words.en: Deterrence is the prevention of something, especially war or crime, by making someone fear the consequences.

words.ex: Smoking is a detriment to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that causes damage, harm, or loss.

words.tr: adj. 五花八门的； v. “variegate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The garden has variegated flowers in many colors.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有五花八门的彩色花朵。
words.en: Having patches, stripes, or marks of different colors; diversified in appearance.

words.tr:
v. （鸟）啼啭；用颤音唱
n. 啼啭；颤音
words.ex: The warble of the songbird filled the morning air.
words.ex_cn: 歌鸟的啭鸣声充满了清晨的空气。
words.en: To warble means to sing with trills, quavers, or melodic embellishments, often used to describe the sound made by birds. It can also refer to the act of singing in a trilling or quavering voice.

words.ex: The chickens roost on the branch at night.
words.ex_cn: 鸡晚上栖息在树枝上。
words.en: A roost is a place where birds rest or sleep. As a verb, to roost means for birds to settle or rest, typically for the night.

words.ex: The old man is infirm and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人身体虚弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: If someone is infirm, they are weak or ill, and often old.

words.tr:
v. 喘息；喘鸣；发出呼哧呼哧的声音
n. 喝哧喝哧喘息声
words.ex: The old man wheezes when he walks fast.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人快走时会喘息。
words.en: To breathe with difficulty and with a whistling sound.

words.ex: He suffers from a bad cold.
words.ex_cn: 他患了重感冒。
words.en: If you suffer from an illness or from a medical condition, you are badly affected by it.

words.tr:
v. 呜咽；啜泣
n. 呜咽；啜泣
words.ex: The dog whimpered when it saw the storm.
words.ex_cn: 狗看到风暴时呜咽起来。
words.en: If someone whimpers, they make quiet unhappy or frightened sounds, as if they are about to start crying.

words.ex: The mortuary was filled with the bodies of the victims.
words.ex_cn: 停尸房里堆满了受害者的尸体。
words.en: A mortuary is a building or a room in a hospital where dead bodies are kept before they are buried or cremated.

words.tr:
v. 夺取；费力取得；歪曲
n. 扭；拧
words.ex: He wrests the ball from his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他从对手那里抢走球。
words.en: To wrest something from someone means to take it from them with a lot of effort, often because they do not want to give it to you.

words.ex: He used a hatchet to cut wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用斧头砍木头。
words.en: A hatchet is a small axe with a short handle, used for chopping wood.

words.tr: adj. 愚笨的；癫狂的；痴傻的
words.ex: He wore a daft hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶傻气的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as daft, you mean that they are silly, foolish, or crazy.

words.tr:
n. 蠕动；扭动；蜿蜒
v. 蠕动；扭动；蜿蜒前进
words.ex: The worm made a small wriggle in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 这条蠕虫在泥土中蠕动了一下。
words.en: To move or cause to move with short, quick twisting or turning motions.

words.ex: The old castle has a deep moat around it.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡周围有一条深深的护城河。
words.en: A moat is a deep, wide ditch that is dug around a place such as a castle and is usually filled with water, in order to protect the place from attack.

words.ex: He hurt his shin while kicking the ball.
words.ex_cn: 他踢球时伤到了胫部。
words.en: The front part of the leg below the knee.

words.tr:
n. 长矛；狗鱼
v. 用长矛刺
words.ex: The soldier held a sharp pike in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 士兵手里拿着一把锋利的长矛。
words.en: A pike is a long thrusting spear formerly used in European warfare from the Late Middle Ages and most of the Early Modern Period, and were wielded by foot soldiers deployed in pike square formation, and it is also a large predatory freshwater fish with a long body and large mouth.

words.tr:
v. 扭动；翻滚；苦恼
n. 扭动；翻滚
words.ex: The child writhe in pain after falling.
words.ex_cn: 孩子摔倒后痛苦地扭动。
words.en: If you writhe, your body twists and turns violently backwards and forwards, usually because you are in great pain or discomfort.

chapters.name: Level 12 行为类动词

words.tr: n. 市政府参事;市议员
words.ex: The alderman was responsible for overseeing the city's budget.
words.ex_cn: 这位市议员负责监督城市的预算。
words.en: An alderman is a member of a municipal legislative body, in many jurisdictions, a municipal official elected to represent a district in a city.

words.ex: The meeting will adjourn at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 会议将在下午5点休会。
words.en: If a meeting or trial is adjourned, or if it adjourns, it is stopped for a short time.

words.ex: The functionary's job is to ensure that the procedures are followed correctly.
words.ex_cn: 这位公职人员的工作是确保程序正确执行。
words.en: A functionary is a person who has to perform official functions or duties; an official.

words.tr: n. 流动小贩；商贩；传播者
words.ex: The peddler sells toys on the street.
words.ex_cn: 小贩在街上卖玩具。
words.en: A peddler is someone who goes from place to place trying to sell small goods.

words.ex: The teacher will appraise my essay next week.
words.ex_cn: 老师下周会评价我的作文。
words.en: If you appraise something or someone, you consider them carefully and form an opinion about them.

words.ex: The stallion runs fast in the field.
words.ex_cn: 这匹公马在田野里跑得很快。
words.en: A stallion is an adult male horse that has not been castrated, especially one kept for breeding.

words.tr: v. 攻击；困扰；抨击；袭击
words.ex: The storm assailed the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴袭击了这个小村庄。
words.en: If someone assails you, they attack you violently, either physically or with words.

words.ex: The old citadel stands on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 古老的城堡矗立在山上。
words.en: A citadel is a fortress, typically on high ground, protecting or dominating a city.

words.ex: The lighthouse stands on a promontory overlooking the sea.
words.ex_cn: 灯塔建在俯瞰大海的岬角上。
words.en: A promontory is a high point of land or rock projecting into a body of water; a headland.

words.tr:
n. 试验；化验；定量分析
v. 试验；化验；定量分析
words.ex: The lab will assay the blood sample tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实验室明天将检测这个血液样本。
words.en: An assay is a test to determine the presence, absence, or quantity of one or more components.

words.ex: Toothpaste contains fluoride to protect teeth.
words.ex_cn: 牙膏含有氟化物以保护牙齿。
words.en: Fluoride is a chemical compound that contains fluorine. It is often added to water and toothpaste to help prevent tooth decay.

words.ex: The parson delivered a sermon on the importance of charity.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在布道中讲述了慈善的重要性。
words.en: A parson is a priest in the Church of England who is in charge of a parish.

words.ex: The bandit stole money from the bank.
words.ex_cn: 强盗从银行偷了钱。
words.en: A bandit is a person who robs people, especially one of a group of people who attack travelers.

words.ex: He tried to atone for his mistakes by working harder.
words.ex_cn: 他通过更加努力工作来弥补自己的错误。
words.en: If you atone for something that you have done, you do something to show that you are sorry you did it.

words.tr: v. 遗赠；遗留；把…传下去
words.ex: He bequeathed his house to his daughter.
words.ex_cn: 他把房子遗赠给了他的女儿。
words.en: If you bequeath your money or property to someone, you legally state that they should have it when you die.

words.tr: adj. 各种各样的；杂七杂八的
words.ex: He bought sundry items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了各种物品。
words.en: If someone refers to sundry people or things, they are referring to several people or things that are all different from each other.

words.tr: n. 古董；珍品; n. （Curio）人名；（意）库里奥
words.ex: He bought a curio at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个奇珍异品。
words.en: A curio is an object that is interesting because it is unusual, rare, or old.

words.tr: n. 大会；宗教会议；教会法院
words.ex: The synod met last week to discuss church rules.
words.ex_cn: 上次会议，主教会议讨论了教会的规则。
words.en: A synod is a council of a church, usually convened to decide on issues of doctrine, administration or application.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.ex: The laity do not understand the church rules.
words.ex_cn: 俗人不明白教会的规则。
words.en: The laity refers to all the people in a religious group who are not clergy or who do not have a professional role in that religion.

words.tr: n. 土窖；地穴；教堂地下室
words.ex: He found a crypt under the old church.
words.ex_cn: 他在旧教堂下面发现了一个地窖。
words.en: A crypt is a room or chamber beneath a church, used as a burial place.

words.ex: She coddles her little brother too much.
words.ex_cn: 她太宠着她的弟弟了。
words.en: To treat someone in an indulgent or overprotective way.

words.ex: He is bashful when he speaks in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 当他当着大家说话时，他很害羞。
words.en: If someone is bashful, they are shy and easily embarrassed.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.ex: He is an atheist who does not believe in God.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名不信神的无神论者。
words.en: An atheist is a person who believes that there is no God or gods.

words.ex: The Jews observe the Sabbath from Friday evening to Saturday evening.
words.ex_cn: 犹太人从星期五晚上到星期六晚上守安息日。
words.en: The Sabbath is a day of rest and worship observed by Jews and some Christians, typically on Saturday by Jews and on Sunday by Christians.

words.ex: They keep the sabbath by resting and going to church.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过休息和去教堂来守安息日。
words.en: To observe the Sabbath as a day of rest and worship, according to religious tradition.

words.tr: v. 安抚；讨好；使息怒；调和
words.ex: He tried to conciliate his angry neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他试图安抚他生气的邻居。
words.en: If you conciliate someone, you try to end a disagreement with them by doing or saying things that will make them less angry or more friendly.

words.tr:
n. 诉讼当事人
adj. 有关诉讼的
words.ex: The litigant spoke clearly in court.
words.ex_cn: 这位诉讼当事人在法庭上清晰地发言。
words.en: A litigant is a person who is involved in a lawsuit.

words.ex: The preparation for the exam took two weeks.
words.ex_cn: 考试的准备花了两周时间。
words.en: Preparation is the process of getting something ready for use or for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The onlooker watched the accident quietly.
words.ex_cn: 旁观者安静地看着这起事故。
words.en: A person who watches something happening without taking part in it.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: The impact caused significant damage to the fuselage.
words.ex_cn: 这次撞击对机身造成了严重的损坏。
words.en: The main body of an aircraft, to which the wings and tail are attached.

words.tr: v. 奉为神圣；贡献；奉献
words.ex: They consecrate the church with prayer and song.
words.ex_cn: 他们用祈祷和歌声将教堂奉为神圣。
words.en: To consecrate something means to officially declare it to be holy and to be used for religious purposes.

words.tr: n. （犹太史）五十年节（每五十年举行一次庆祝希伯来奴隶的解放）；大赦年（天主教每二十五年一次的）；...
words.ex: The city celebrated its 50th anniversary with a grand jubilee.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市以盛大的庆典庆祝其50周年。
words.en: A jubilee is a special anniversary of an event, especially one celebrating twenty-five or fifty years of a reign or activity.

words.tr: phrase. 银禧纪念，指在位或结婚25周年的纪念
words.ex: The king celebrated his silver jubilee after fifty years on the throne.
words.ex_cn: 国王在位五十年后庆祝了他的银禧纪念。
words.en: A 25th anniversary celebration, traditionally associated with silver.

words.ex: He quit his job because of coercion from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因为老板的强迫而辞了工作。
words.en: The act of persuading someone to do something by using force or threats.

words.ex: He contravenes the school rules by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: To contravene a law or rule means to do something that is forbidden by it.

words.tr: n. 估价员；（资产）评估师；评分者
words.ex: The assessor evaluated the property's value for tax purposes.
words.ex_cn: 评估员为征税目的评估了房产的价值。
words.en: An assessor is a person whose job is to calculate the value of something or the amount of money that should be paid, for example in tax.

words.tr: v. 浪费时间；拖延；玩弄；调情
words.ex: He dallys with his homework instead of finishing it.
words.ex_cn: 他浪费时间在作业上，而不是完成它。
words.en: To dally means to act or move slowly, or to spend time idly or in trifling.

words.ex: He writes all the money in the ledger.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都记在账本上。
words.en: A ledger is a book or collection of accounts in which account transactions are recorded.

words.tr: phrase. 填（写）； 填满；替代
words.ex: Please fill in the blanks with the correct words.
words.ex_cn: 请用正确的单词填空。
words.en: If you fill in a form or other document requesting information, you write information in the spaces on it.

words.tr: n. 单调乏味的苦差事
words.ex: He hates the drudgery of washing dishes every day.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌每天洗碗的枯燥工作。
words.en: Hard, menial, or dull work.

words.tr: n. 接触传染病；传染；歪风；蔓延
words.ex: The contagion spread quickly among the children.
words.ex_cn: 这种传染病在孩子们中迅速传播。
words.en: A contagion is the spreading of a disease, especially one that is caused by bacteria or viruses, from one person or animal to another by direct or indirect contact.

words.tr: v. 使士气低落；使失去斗志
words.ex: The bad news demoralized the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队士气低落。
words.en: If something demoralizes someone, it makes them lose so much confidence in what they are doing that they want to give up.

words.ex: He used a stick to dislodge the rock from the path.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子把石头从路上移出。
words.en: To dislodge something means to remove it from a place where it is fixed or held.

words.tr:
n. 浮渣；泡沫；社会渣滓
v. 去除浮渣
words.ex: The scum on the pond's surface was disturbing.
words.ex_cn: 池塘表面的浮渣令人不安。
words.en: A layer of dirt or froth on the surface of a liquid.

words.ex: Rivers carry sediment to the sea.
words.ex_cn: 河流把沉积物带到大海。
words.en: Material that settles to the bottom of a liquid; matter that has been deposited by some natural process.

words.tr:
n. 闸门
v. 冲洗
words.ex: The sluice gate was opened to release the water.
words.ex_cn: 水闸门被打开以释放水流。
words.en: A sluice is a channel that is used to control the flow of water, especially in a river or a stream. It can also mean to wash or rinse something with a large amount of water.

words.ex: The teacher asked us to dissect the poem line by line.
words.ex_cn: 老师让我们逐行仔细分析这首诗。
words.en: To dissect something means to cut it into pieces in order to examine its structure, or to study something in great detail.

words.tr:
n. 肌腱；力量的来源
v. 给…以力量
words.ex: The sinew held the muscle to the bone.
words.ex_cn: 肌腱将肌肉连接到骨头。
words.en: A sinew is a tendon, the strong tissue that connects muscles to bones, or it can refer to the strength and energy that makes someone able to do something difficult.

words.ex: The teacher gave an exhortation to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师鼓励学生努力学习。
words.en: An exhortation is a speech or written passage intended to persuade, encourage, or urge someone to do something.

words.ex: Good teachers edify their students with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 好老师用智慧启发学生。
words.en: To edify someone means to improve their mind or character by teaching them something.

words.tr:
adj. 沮丧的；低落的；垂头丧气的
v. 使…情绪低落；使沮丧；“deject”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt dejected after failing the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格后感到沮丧。
words.en: If you are dejected, you feel miserable or unhappy, especially because you have just been disappointed by something.

words.ex: The veterinarian helps sick animals.
words.ex_cn: 兽医帮助生病的动物。
words.en: A veterinarian is a person who is qualified to treat sick or injured animals.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.ex: The dog has rabies.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗得了狂犬病。
words.en: Rabies is a serious disease that affects the brain and nerves, usually caught from the bite of an infected animal.

words.ex: He embezzled money from his company.
words.ex_cn: 他从公司贪污了钱。
words.en: To embezzle means to steal or misappropriate money placed in one's trust or belonging to one's employer.

words.tr: n. 回扣；佣金；强烈的反应；不良后果
words.ex: He got a kickback for choosing the expensive supplier.
words.ex_cn: 他因为选择了昂贵的供应商而收到了回扣。
words.en: A kickback is a sum of money that is paid to someone illegally in return for providing help, especially in business or politics.

words.tr: v. 置入神龛中；入庙祀奉；奉为神圣；珍藏
words.ex: They enshrined the ancient statue in a golden shrine.
words.ex_cn: 他们把这尊古代雕像置入了一个金色神龛中。
words.en: If something such as a tradition or a right is enshrined in something such as a constitution or law, it is protected by it.

words.ex: The goblin hid under the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 小妖精躲在桥下。
words.en: A goblin is a small, ugly creature that is often mischievous or evil. In folklore, goblins are often associated with causing trouble or playing tricks on people.

words.tr: n. 护身符；驱邪物；能产生奇迹的东西；法宝
words.ex: He wears a talisman for good luck.
words.ex_cn: 他戴一个护身符以求好运。
words.en: A talisman is an object which is believed to have magic powers to protect its owner or to bring good luck.

words.ex: The landlord will evict the tenant for not paying rent.
words.ex_cn: 房东会因为租客不付房租而将他驱逐。
words.en: To evict someone means to force them to leave a house or piece of land, usually because they have not paid the rent or have broken the law.

words.ex: He drove on the turnpike to save time.
words.ex_cn: 他走收费公路以节省时间。
words.en: A turnpike is a road that drivers must pay to use, especially in the past. It is also a gate or barrier set across a road to stop traffic until a toll is paid.

words.tr: v. 驱（魔）；除去（痛苦的想法等）
words.ex: The priest tried to exorcise the demon from the house.
words.ex_cn: 牧师试图将恶魔从房子里驱逐出去。
words.en: To exorcise means to drive out or attempt to drive out (a supposed evil spirit) from a person or place.

words.ex: The malevolent wizard cast a dark spell.
words.ex_cn: 那个有恶意的巫师施了一个黑暗咒语。
words.en: Having or showing a wish to harm others; malicious.

words.ex: An apparition appeared in the dark hallway.
words.ex_cn: 一个幽灵出现在黑暗的走廊里。
words.en: An apparition is a ghost or ghostlike image of a person.

words.ex: He wants to expedite the process.
words.ex_cn: 他想加快这个过程。
words.en: To expedite something means to make it happen or be done more quickly.

words.ex: The river overflowed and broke the embankment.
words.ex_cn: 河水泛滥，冲垮了堤坝。
words.en: An embankment is a thick wall of earth that is built to carry a road or railway over an area of low ground, or to prevent water from a river or the sea from flooding an area.

words.ex: The country will extradite the suspect to Canada.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家将把嫌疑人引渡到加拿大。
words.en: If someone is extradited, they are officially sent back to their own or another country to be tried for a crime that they have been accused of.

words.tr:
adj. 巡回的；流动的
n. 四处奔波的人；流浪者
words.ex: The itinerant worker moves from town to town for jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这位流动工人为了工作从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: Someone who is itinerant travels from place to place, usually because they have no permanent home or job, or because they are involved in a particular activity that requires this.

words.tr: n. 擅自占用他人房子（或土地）的人； adj. “squat”的比较级；
words.ex: The squatter lived in the abandoned house for years.
words.ex_cn: 这个擅自占用者在废弃的房子里住了好几年。
words.en: A squatter is someone who lives in an unused building without permission and without paying rent.

words.tr: n. 转移; 移交，授权; 授权代理
words.ex: The government gave more power to local areas through devolution.
words.ex_cn: 政府通过权力下放将更多权力交给地方。
words.en: The transfer or delegation of power to a lower level, especially by central government to local or regional administration.

words.tr: v. （因抵押人未如期还贷）取消赎回权；排除；妨碍
words.ex: The bank foreclosed on the house after the owner defaulted on the mortgage.
words.ex_cn: 房主在抵押贷款违约后，银行取消了房屋的赎回权。
words.en: If the person or organization that lent someone money forecloses, they take possession of a property that was bought with the borrowed money, for example because regular repayments have not been made.

words.tr: n. [法] 原告；发牢骚的人；抱怨者
words.ex: The complainant provided evidence to support their case.
words.ex_cn: 原告提供了证据来支持他们的案件。
words.en: A complainant is a person who makes a formal complaint in a court of law.

words.ex: He girded his waist with a strong belt.
words.ex_cn: 他用一条结实的腰带束紧腰部。
words.en: To gird means to encircle or secure something with a belt or band, or to prepare oneself for a task or challenge.

words.ex: He gave a strong rebuttal to the claim.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个说法给出了有力的反驳。
words.en: A rebuttal is a statement or piece of evidence that contradicts or opposes a previous statement or evidence.

words.ex: The doctor will immunize the child against measles.
words.ex_cn: 医生会给这个孩子接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To immunize someone or something means to protect them against a disease by giving them a vaccine.

words.ex: He had mumps last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周得了腮腺炎。
words.en: Mumps is a contagious disease that causes swelling of the salivary glands and can lead to more serious complications.

words.tr: n. （尤指依法从房屋或土地上）驱逐；
words.ex: The landlord filed for eviction after the tenant refused to pay rent.
words.ex_cn: 租客拒绝支付租金后，房东申请了驱逐。
words.en: The act of expelling someone, especially a tenant, from a property; expulsion.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.tr: v. 清算；变卖；消除；铲除
words.ex: The company will liquidate its assets to pay debts.
words.ex_cn: 公司将变卖资产来偿还债务。
words.en: To liquidate a company means to sell its assets in order to pay its debts, or to sell an asset for cash.

words.tr: adj. 衰老的；老朽的；破旧的
words.ex: The old house is decrepit and needs repair.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老房子破旧不堪，需要修理。
words.en: Something that is decrepit is old and in poor condition.

words.ex: He works in a foundry that makes metal parts.
