words.en: A harrow is a piece of farm equipment that is used to break up and smooth out the surface of the soil.

words.ex: The potter fired the clay in a kiln.
words.ex_cn: 陶匠把陶土放在窑里烧制。
words.en: A kiln is a type of oven that is used to bake clay and pottery in order to make them hard.

words.tr:
n. 制模；成型
v. 制模；塑造；“mold”的现在分词
words.ex: The intricate molding on the ceiling added a touch of elegance to the room.
words.ex_cn: 天花板上复杂的嵌线为房间增添了一丝优雅。
words.en: Molding refers to the process of shaping a liquid or malleable material by using a rigid frame or model called a mold. It can also refer to a decorative strip of material, such as wood or plaster, used to finish or embellish a surface.

words.tr:
n. 抛射物；射弹；发射物；自动推进武器
adj. 发射的；射弹的；推进的
words.ex: The boy threw a projectile into the air.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把一个抛射物扔向空中。
words.en: A projectile is an object that is thrown or shot forwards, such as a bullet fired from a gun.

words.ex: The helicopter's rotor began to spin rapidly.
words.ex_cn: 直升机的旋翼开始快速旋转。
words.en: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine or device, especially in motors, turbines, and helicopters.

words.ex: The captain turned the rudder to change the ship's direction.
words.ex_cn: 船长转动舵来改变船的方向。
words.en: A rudder is a flat piece of wood or metal at the back of a boat or aircraft that is used for steering.

words.tr:
n. 筛子；滤器
v. 筛；滤
words.ex: He used a sieve to separate sand from pebbles.
words.ex_cn: 他用筛子把沙子和石子分开。
words.en: A sieve is a tool consisting of a wire or plastic mesh held in a frame, used for separating solids from liquids or larger particles from smaller ones.

words.ex: Her story inspires me to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的故事激励我更加努力。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

words.ex: He wore a thimble on his finger to sew.
words.ex_cn: 他戴顶针在手指上缝衣服。
words.en: A thimble is a small hard pitted cup worn for protection on the finger that pushes the needle in sewing.

words.tr: n. 三叉戟；三叉戟式飞机
words.ex: The statue held a trident in its right hand.
words.ex_cn: 雕像的右手握着一把三叉戟。
words.en: A trident is a three-pronged spear, especially as an attribute of Poseidon (Neptune) or Britannia.

words.tr: n. 室内装饰；室内装璜品
words.ex: He bought new upholstery for his old chair.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的旧椅子买了新的坐垫面料。
words.en: The materials used to cover furniture, especially seats, or the work of covering furniture with these materials.

words.tr: n. 叶片；[气象]风向标；风信旗; n. （Vane）人名；（老）万；（塞、芬）瓦内；（英）文；（...
words.ex: The wind turned the vane on the roof.
words.ex_cn: 风把屋顶上的风向标吹转了。
words.en: A flat or curved object that is attached to a wheel or rotor and that causes the wheel or rotor to turn when wind or water flows against it.

words.ex: He poured wine into a large vat.
words.ex_cn: 他把葡萄酒倒进一个大桶里。
words.en: A vat is a large container used for holding liquids, especially in industrial processes.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 位置关系•相对关系

words.tr:
n. 附属物；
adj. 附属的；
words.ex: The printer is an adjunct to the computer.
words.ex_cn: 打印机是电脑的附属物。
words.en: Something that is added or attached to something else but is not essential to it.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 后勤人员；附加项目
words.ex: The ancillary staff help the doctors in the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 辅助人员在医院里帮助医生。
words.en: Ancillary means providing necessary support to the primary activities or operation of an organization, system, etc.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 辅助物；附属物；助动词
words.ex: He used an auxiliary verb to form the past tense.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个助动词来构成过去时。
words.en: An auxiliary is a person or thing that provides additional help or support.

words.tr:
adj. 对角线的；斜的
n. 对角线；斜线
words.ex: The square has two diagonal lines.
words.ex_cn: 这个正方形有两条对角线。
words.en: A diagonal line or movement goes in a sloping direction, for example, from one corner of a square across to the opposite corner.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr: adj. 分歧的；发散的；趋异的；
words.ex: The two friends had divergent opinions about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这两个朋友对这部电影的看法不同。
words.en: If two things diverge, they are different from each other, or they become different from each other.

words.tr: adj. 不合适的；不相称的；不协调的；
words.ex: His funny hat was incongruous with the formal suit.
words.ex_cn: 他的滑稽帽子与正式西装不搭配。
words.en: Something that is incongruous is strange when considered together with other aspects of a situation.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.ex: He bought some miscellaneous items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店里买了一些各种各样的东西。
words.en: Consisting of a variety of ingredients or parts.

words.tr: adj. 间接的；不直截了当的；
words.ex: He gave an oblique answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个间接的回答。
words.en: If you describe a statement as oblique, you mean that is not expressed directly or openly, often because it is difficult or embarrassing.

words.ex: His ostensible reason for leaving was sickness.
words.ex_cn: 他离开的表面原因是生病。
words.en: An ostensible reason or purpose seems to be the real one, but it is not.

words.tr:
adj. 垂直的；笔直的
n. 垂直线
words.ex: The lines are perpendicular to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些线互相垂直。
words.en: At right angles to the plane of the horizon or a base line; vertical.

words.tr:
adj. 零碎的；
adv. 零碎地；
words.ex: He fixed the car piecemeal, one part at a time.
words.ex_cn: 他一点一点地修理汽车，一次修一个零件。
words.en: If you describe a change or process as piecemeal, you disapprove of it because it happens gradually, usually at irregular intervals, and is probably not satisfactory.

words.ex: The builder used a plumb to check if the wall was straight.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工人用铅锤检查墙是否垂直。
words.en: To measure the depth of water with a plumb line; to explore or understand something deeply; exactly vertical; completely or directly.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 学问•文化•宗教

words.tr: adj. 隐秘的；秘密的；隐晦的
words.ex: He gave a cryptic answer and left.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个神秘的回答，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something as cryptic, you mean that it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.tr:
adj. 辩证的
n. 辩证法
words.ex: He uses dialectic to find the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他用辩证法来寻找真理。
words.en: Dialectic is a method of argument or exposition that systematically weighs contradictory facts or ideas with a view to the resolution of their real or apparent contradictions.

words.tr: adj. （基督教）教会的；传教士的
words.ex: He wears an ecclesiastical robe.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件教会的长袍。
words.en: Relating to the Christian Church or its clergy.

words.ex: The book contains esoteric ideas that only experts understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了只有专家才能理解的深奥思想。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest.

words.tr: adj. 各学科间的；跨学科的；
words.ex: The project is interdisciplinary, combining biology and chemistry.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目是跨学科的，结合了生物学和化学。
words.en: Involving two or more academic, scientific, or artistic disciplines.

words.ex: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这道数学题做了一个易懂的解释。
words.en: If someone is lucid, they are able to understand things clearly and think clearly, especially when they have been very ill or confused.

words.tr:
adj. 僧侣的；修道院的；宁静简朴的
n. 僧侣；修道士
words.ex: He lives a monastic life in the old monastery.
words.ex_cn: 他在古老的修道院里过着修道般的生活。
words.en: Relating to monks, nuns, or others living under religious vows, or the buildings in which they live.

words.tr:
adj. 未决议的；有讨论余地的
v. 提出…供讨论
words.ex: The issue is still a moot point.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题仍然是未决的。
words.en: If a plan, idea, or subject is mooted, it is suggested or introduced for discussion.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；无所不能的
words.ex: The god is omnipotent.
words.ex_cn: 这个神是无所不能的。
words.en: Having unlimited power, able to do anything.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.ex: He gave a pedantic answer about grammar rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对语法规则给出了一个迂腐的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as pedantic, you mean that they are too concerned with unimportant details or traditional rules, especially in connection with academic subjects.

words.tr:
adj. 多种语言的；通晓数种语言的
n. 通晓数种语言的人
words.ex: He is a polyglot who speaks five languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位会说五种语言的多语者。
words.en: A polyglot is a person who knows and is able to use several languages.

words.tr: adj. 沉重的；笨重的；沉闷的
words.ex: He carried a ponderous box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他搬着一个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: Something that is ponderous is very heavy or is very slow and clumsy because of its weight or size.

words.ex: He drew a simple schematic of the circuit.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个电路的简单示意图。
words.en: A schematic diagram or representation is a simple drawing that uses symbols to show the parts of something and how they are connected.

words.ex: The word 'bank' has different semantic meanings.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'bank' 有不同的语义含义。
words.en: Semantic is used to describe something that relates to the meanings of words and sentences.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 身体•健康

words.ex: He felt pain in his abdominal area.
words.ex_cn: 他感到腹部疼痛。
words.en: Relating to the abdomen.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.tr:
adj. 散乱的；乱蓬蓬的；衣冠不整的
v.  使蓬乱；使凌乱；使弄皱；“dishevel”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She looked disheveled after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长时间的飞行后，她看起来很凌乱。
words.en: If you describe someone's hair, clothes, or appearance as disheveled, you mean that it is very untidy.

words.ex: The distal end of the bone is broken.
words.ex_cn: 骨头的远端断了。
words.en: Situated away from the center of the body or from the point of attachment.

words.ex: He is an equestrian rider who trains every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天早上训练的骑马者。
words.en: An equestrian is someone who rides horses, especially as a sport or a profession.

words.ex: He has flabby arms from not exercising.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不锻炼，手臂松软。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as flabby, you are criticizing them for being soft and loose rather than firm and strong.

words.ex: The old man looked gaunt after his illness.
words.ex_cn: 这场病后，老人显得消瘦。
words.en: If someone looks gaunt, they look very thin, usually because they have been ill or worried.

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.ex: The kinetic energy of the moving ball is high.
words.ex_cn: 运动的球的动能很高。
words.en: Relating to or resulting from motion.

words.tr: adj. 慵懒的；没精打采的；懒洋洋的
words.ex: He felt lethargic after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you are lethargic, you do not have much energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He felt listless after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病后感到无精打采。
words.en: If someone is listless, they lack energy or enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；生气勃勃的；健壮的
words.ex: The young man sang a lusty song at the party.
words.ex_cn: 那个年轻人在派对上唱了一首嘹亮的歌。
words.en: If you describe someone as lusty, you mean that they are strong and healthy and full of energy.

words.tr: adj. 病理学的；病理的；病态的
words.ex: The doctor found a pathological change in the tissue.
words.ex_cn: 医生在组织中发现了一种病理性的变化。
words.en: Pathological means relating to pathology, which is the study of diseases, or it can describe a behavior or condition that is extreme and not normal, often in a way that is harmful or undesirable.

words.tr:
adj. 俯卧的；平卧的；给（悲伤等）压倒的
v. 使俯伏；使拜倒
words.ex: He fell prostrate on the ground after the race.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，他瘫倒在了地上。
words.en: If you prostrate yourself, you lie down flat on the ground, usually in front of someone, as a way of showing respect or submission. It can also mean to be extremely tired or emotionally drained.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；红的；淡红色
words.ex: Her complexion was ruddy from the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 她的脸色因寒冷的天气而变得红润。
words.en: Having a healthy red color, especially in the face.

words.tr: adj. 需要久坐的；惯于久坐不动的；不爱活动的；
words.ex: His sedentary job makes him sit all day.
words.ex_cn: 他的久坐工作让他整天坐着。
words.en: Someone who has a sedentary lifestyle or job sits down a lot of the time and does not take much exercise.

words.ex: He is a stocky man with strong arms.
words.ex_cn: 他是个身材敦实、手臂强壮的人。
words.en: A stocky person is broad and solidly built.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 感情•感觉

words.tr: adj. 可恶的；令人憎恶的；令人痛恨的
words.ex: He finds lying to friends abhorrent.
words.ex_cn: 他认为对朋友撒谎是令人厌恶的。
words.en: If something is abhorrent to you, you hate it very much, often because you think it is immoral or wrong.

words.tr: adj. 辛辣的；苦涩的；刺激的；尖刻的
words.ex: The smoke from the fire had an acrid smell.
words.ex_cn: 火灾的烟雾有一种刺鼻的气味。
words.en: An acrid smell or taste is strong and sharp, and usually unpleasant. It can also describe a manner or expression that is bitter or harsh.

words.ex: He is averse to changing his routine.
words.ex_cn: 他反对改变自己的日常安排。
words.en: If you say that someone is averse to something, you mean they dislike it or have a strong opposition to it.

words.tr:
adj. 震耳欲聋的；极喧闹的
v. 使聋；使听不见；“deafen”的现在分词
words.ex: The crowd's deafening cheers filled the stadium.
words.ex_cn: 人群震耳欲聋的欢呼声充满了整个体育场。
words.en: If you say that a noise is deafening, you mean that it is so loud that it makes it difficult to hear anything else.

words.tr: adj. 应受严厉谴责的；可悲的；极糟糕的
words.ex: The living conditions in the slums were deplorable.
words.ex_cn: 贫民窟的生活条件非常糟糕。
words.en: If you say that something is deplorable, you think that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: He gave a derisive laugh when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时，他发出了一声嘲笑的笑。
words.en: expressing contempt or ridicule.

words.ex: His derogatory remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他毁谤的言辞伤害了她的感情。
words.en: If you make a derogatory remark or comment about someone or something, you say something that shows you have a low opinion of them.

words.tr: adj. 沮丧的；泄气的；失望的
words.ex: He became despondent after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得沮丧。
words.en: If you are despondent, you are very unhappy because you have been experiencing difficulties that you think you will not be able to overcome.

words.ex: He is diffident when he speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时很腼腆。
words.en: If you are diffident, you are rather shy and do not enjoy talking about yourself or being noticed by other people.

words.ex: The downcast eyes of the boy showed he was sad.
words.ex_cn: 男孩低垂的眼睛显示出他很难过。
words.en: If you are downcast, you are feeling sad and without hope.

words.tr: adj. 冒泡的；起泡的；活泼的
words.ex: The champagne was effervescent and bubbled in the glass.
words.ex_cn: 香槟在杯中冒泡沸腾。
words.en: If you describe someone as effervescent, you mean that they are lively, entertaining, enthusiastic, and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 爱开玩笑的；乱引人发笑的
words.ex: He gave a facetious answer when asked about his age.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到年龄时，他给出了一个开玩笑的回答。
words.en: If you say that someone is being facetious, you are criticizing them because they are making humorous remarks or saying things that they do not mean in a situation where they ought to be serious.

words.tr: adj. 爱挑剔的；过分讲究的
words.ex: He is fastidious about keeping his room clean.
words.ex_cn: 他非常讲究保持房间整洁。
words.en: Very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail.

words.tr: adj. 平民的；卑贱的；卑鄙的；不光彩的
words.ex: He came from an ignoble family, but worked hard to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他出身于平民家庭，但努力工作以取得成功。
words.en: If you describe something as ignoble, you mean that it is bad and something to be ashamed of.

words.ex: He remained impassive when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个坏消息时，他依然面无表情。
words.en: If someone is impassive, they do not show any emotion.

words.tr: adj. 不注意的；疏忽的；非故意的
words.ex: He made an inadvertent mistake while typing.
words.ex_cn: 他在打字时不小心犯了个错误。
words.en: If something bad is inadvertent, it is done without realizing that it is wrong or that it could have bad consequences.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.tr: adj.  快活的；愉快的；高兴的
words.ex: His jovial nature made him popular among his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他天性快活，这使他在同事中很受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone as jovial, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 无精打采的；疲倦无力的
words.ex: He gave a languid smile before lying down.
words.ex_cn: 他躺下前给了一个慵懒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as languid, you mean that they show little energy or interest and are very slow and casual in their movements.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 若无其事的；不在乎的；冷淡的
words.ex: He was nonchalant about the test result.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试结果表现得漫不经心。
words.en: If you describe someone as nonchalant, you mean that they appear not to worry or care about things and that they seem very calm.

words.tr:
adj. 无可名状的；难以区别的；无特征的；极普通的
n. 无以名状；不属任何类型的人
words.ex: The building was nondescript, with no special features.
words.ex_cn: 这栋建筑无可名状，没有任何特别的特征。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as nondescript, you mean that their appearance is rather dull, and not at all interesting or attractive.

words.ex: The phone is expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机很贵。
words.en: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

words.ex: The child's petulant behavior was a result of his frustration.
words.ex_cn: 孩子暴躁的行为是因他的沮丧所致。
words.en: If you describe someone as petulant, you mean that they get angry or annoyed in a childish or unreasonable way.

words.ex: The violin played a plaintive melody.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴演奏了一首哀伤的旋律。
words.en: A plaintive sound or voice expresses sadness.

words.ex: The sponge is porous and absorbs water easily.
words.ex_cn: 海绵是多孔的，容易吸水。
words.en: If something is porous, it has a lot of tiny holes in it that allow water or air to pass through slowly.

words.tr: adj. 枯燥的；乏味的；平淡无奇的
words.ex: His prosaic speech bored everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他平淡无奇的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as prosaic, you mean that it is ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 刺鼻的；一语道破的
words.ex: The cheese has a pungent smell.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪有刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的；专心致志的
words.ex: The children were rapt during the story.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们全神贯注地听故事。
words.en: If someone is rapt, they are so interested in or fascinated by what they are seeing or hearing that they do not pay attention to anything else.

words.ex: We use a repellent to keep mosquitoes away.
words.ex_cn: 我们使用驱虫剂来驱赶蚊子。
words.en: A repellent is a substance that is used to keep insects or animals away from something. It can also refer to something that is extremely unpleasant or disgusting.

words.tr: adj. 易恶心的；易受惊的；神经质的；过于拘谨的
words.ex: She was too squeamish to watch the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 她太容易呕吐了，不敢看手术过程。
words.en: If you are squeamish, you are easily upset by unpleasant sights or situations.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

words.tr: adj. 激起性欲的；满足感官的；撩人的
words.ex: The painting showed a voluptuous woman with flowing curves.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一位身材性感、曲线优美的女人。
words.en: If you describe a woman as voluptuous, you mean that she has large breasts and hips and is considered sexually attractive.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 形状•性质•外观•状态

words.ex: The jar is airtight, so the food stays fresh.
words.ex_cn: 这个罐子是密封的，所以食物能保持新鲜。
words.en: If something is airtight, it is completely sealed so that no air can get in or out.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；苛性的；尖酸刻薄的
n. 腐蚀剂
words.ex: The caustic liquid burned through the metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种腐蚀性的液体腐蚀了金属。
words.en: A caustic substance is able to burn or destroy organic tissue by chemical action. Caustic remarks are extremely critical, sarcastic, or bitter.

words.tr: adj. 贞洁的；忠贞的；朴素的
words.ex: She remained chaste despite the pressure.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有压力，她依然保持贞洁。
words.en: If you describe someone as chaste, you mean that they do not have sex with anyone, or they only have sex with their husband or wife.

words.ex: The spoon has a concave surface.
words.ex_cn: 勺子有一个凹的表面。
words.en: A concave surface is curved inward, like the inside of a bowl.

words.ex: The old factory is now a derelict building.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧工厂现在是一座破败的建筑。
words.en: If a building or a piece of land is derelict, it is not cared for and is in bad condition. A derelict person or thing is one that has been abandoned or neglected.

words.ex: The pot is made of earthen material.
words.ex_cn: 这个罐子是土制的。
words.en: Made of earth or clay; relating to or resembling earth.

words.ex: The cat has a fluffy tail.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫有一条蓬松的尾巴。
words.en: Something that is fluffy is soft and light, with many small, loose pieces or parts.

words.ex: He gave a furtive look around before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前偷偷看了一眼四周。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as furtive, you disapprove of them behaving as if they want to keep something secret or hidden.

words.ex: The grubby child came in with dirty hands.
words.ex_cn: 那个脏兮兮的孩子带着脏手进来了。
words.en: If you describe something as grubby, you mean that it is dirty.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；陈词滥调的；老生常谈的
words.ex: His jokes are hackneyed and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话陈腐又无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as hackneyed, you mean that it is unoriginal and has been used so often that it is no longer interesting.

words.ex: The mixture is homogeneous and looks the same throughout.
words.ex_cn: 这种混合物是均一的，看起来处处都一样。
words.en: Something that is homogeneous is uniform in nature or character throughout.

words.ex: His daily routine is humdrum.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活很单调。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as humdrum, you mean that they are ordinary, dull, or boring.

words.tr: adj. 清洁的；无瑕疵的；无过失的
words.ex: The kitchen was immaculate after she cleaned it.
words.ex_cn: 她打扫后，厨房非常干净。
words.en: If you describe something as immaculate, you mean that it is extremely clean, tidy, or neat.

words.tr: adj. 不能渗透的；不受影响的
words.ex: The coat is impervious to rain.
words.ex_cn: 这件外套不透水。
words.en: If you are impervious to someone's actions, you are not affected or influenced by them.

words.ex: The incandescent bulb gives off a warm light.
words.ex_cn: 白炽灯发出温暖的光。
words.en: Emitting light as a result of being heated.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；难以理解的；神秘莫测的
words.ex: His expression was inscrutable.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情难以捉摸。
words.en: If someone or something is inscrutable, it is impossible to understand or know what they are thinking or feeling.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.ex: The handwriting is legible and easy to read.
words.ex_cn: 字迹清晰，容易辨认。
words.en: If writing or print is legible, it is clear enough to read.

words.tr: adj. 易弯的；柔软的；动作轻盈的
words.ex: The dancer is lithe and moves gracefully.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者身材柔韧，动作优雅。
words.en: A person or animal that is lithe is thin, supple, and graceful.

words.tr: adj. 仆人的；枯燥的；琐碎的
words.ex: He did menial work to earn money.
words.ex_cn: 他做琐碎的工作来赚钱。
words.en: A menial task is one that is considered to be lowly or degrading, often involving physical work and requiring little skill or education.

words.tr: adj. 炫耀的；浮华的；卖弄的
words.ex: He wore an ostentatious gold watch to show off his wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一块华丽的金表来炫耀他的财富。
words.en: If you describe something as ostentatious, you disapprove of it because it is expensive and is intended to impress people.

words.tr: adj. 辛辣的；胡椒味的；暴躁的
words.ex: The soup has a peppery taste.
words.ex_cn: 这汤有辛辣的味道。
words.en: Having the hot, spicy flavor of pepper; easily irritated or angered.

words.tr: adj. 私下参与的；私下的；秘密的
words.ex: He is privy to the secret plan.
words.ex_cn: 他知道这个秘密计划。
words.en: If you are privy to something secret, you have been allowed to know about it.

words.tr: adj. 淫乱的；滥交的；杂乱的
words.ex: He was criticized for his promiscuous behavior.
words.ex_cn: 他因淫乱的行为而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe someone as promiscuous, you disapprove of them because they have sexual relationships with many people. In a more general sense, promiscuous can describe something that is not selective or is mixed without order.

words.ex: The table was replete with food.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上摆满了食物。
words.en: If you are replete with something, you have a lot of it and it fills you up.

words.ex: The salient point in the report is the cost increase.
words.ex_cn: 报告中最显著的要点是成本上升。
words.en: The most noticeable or important.

words.ex: The sodden clothes stuck to her skin.
words.ex_cn: 湿透的衣服贴在她的皮肤上。
words.en: Something that is sodden is extremely wet.

words.ex: The bread became soggy after sitting in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 面包在雨中放了一会儿后变得湿软。
words.en: Something that is soggy is unpleasantly wet.

words.tr: adj. 假的；伪造的；欺骗性的；谬误的
words.ex: The data is spurious and cannot be trusted.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据是虚假的，不可信。
words.en: Something that is spurious seems to be genuine, but is false.

words.tr: adj. 偷偷摸摸的；不声张的；秘密的
words.ex: The thief moved with stealthy steps.
words.ex_cn: 小偷蹑手蹑脚地移动。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as stealthy, you mean that they are quiet and secret in what they do, often because they do not want to be seen or heard.

words.ex: The room was stuffy and hard to breathe in.
words.ex_cn: 房间闷热得让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a place as stuffy, you mean that it is unpleasantly warm and has no fresh air.

words.ex: His coat is threadbare from many years of use.
words.ex_cn: 他的外套因为用了多年而变得破旧。
words.en: Worn out by overuse; shabby and old.

words.ex: His speech was full of trite phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了陈腐的表达。
words.en: If you say that something such as an idea, remark, or story is trite, you mean that it is dull and boring because it has been said or told too many times.

words.ex: The ungainly boy tripped over his own feet.
words.ex_cn: 这个笨拙的男孩被自己的脚绊倒了。
words.en: If you describe a person, animal, or vehicle as ungainly, you mean that they look awkward or clumsy, often because they are big.

words.tr: adj. 不整洁的；凌乱的；不修边幅的
words.ex: Her hair was unkempt and her clothes were disheveled.
words.ex_cn: 她的头发蓬乱，衣服也凌乱不堪。
words.en: If you describe someone's hair or appearance as unkempt, you mean that it is untidy or messy.

words.tr: adj. 没有受伤的；未受损害的；
words.ex: He walked away from the crash unscathed.
words.ex_cn: 他从车祸中安然无恙地走开了。
words.en: If someone is unscathed after a dangerous experience, they have not been injured or harmed by it.

words.tr: adj. 温文儒雅的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: He is an urbane man who speaks politely.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个举止文雅、说话有礼貌的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as urbane, you mean that they are polite, confident, and comfortable in social situations.

words.tr: adj. 分泌毒液的；有毒的；恶毒的
words.ex: The snake is venomous.
words.ex_cn: 这条蛇是有毒的。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as venomous, you mean that they show great bitterness and anger toward someone.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 数量•时间•频率

words.tr:
n. 前情；先行词；祖先（常复）
adj. 在 ... 之前的
words.ex: The word 'dog' is the antecedent of 'it' in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 在这句话中，'dog' 是 'it' 的先行词。
words.en: An antecedent is a thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.

words.ex: The computer uses binary code to process data.
words.ex_cn: 计算机使用二进制代码来处理数据。
words.en: Relating to, composed of, or involving two things.

words.tr:
adj. 双眼的；两眼用的
n. （通常用复数）双筒望远镜
words.ex: He uses binocular to watch birds in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他用双筒望远镜在公园里看鸟。
words.en: An optical instrument, such as a pair of field glasses or opera glasses, designed for simultaneous use by both eyes and consisting of two small telescopes joined together.

words.ex: The embryonic stage is the earliest phase of development.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎阶段是发育的最早时期。
words.en: In an early stage of development; rudimentary.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 过度的；过高的；过分的；
words.ex: The restaurant charged an exorbitant price for a small salad.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅对一份小沙拉要了过高的价格。
words.en: If you describe something such as a price or fee as exorbitant, you are emphasizing that it is much higher than it should be.

words.tr: adj. 即席的；临时的；无准备的；不用讲稿的
words.ex: He gave an extemporaneous speech at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上做了一次即兴演讲。
words.en: spoken or done without preparation

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；一阵阵的
words.ex: He had fitful sleep last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚睡得断断续续。
words.en: Something that is fitful happens for irregular periods of time or occurs at irregular times, rather than being continuous.

words.ex: This custom has existed from time immemorial.
words.ex_cn: 这个习俗从远古时代就存在了。
words.en: Something that is immemorial has existed or been happening for such a long time that it cannot be remembered.

words.ex: He made an impetuous decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他冲动地决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impetuous, you mean that they are likely to act quickly and suddenly without thinking or being careful.

words.tr: adj. 无法改变的；不能取消的
words.ex: The decision was irrevocable.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是不可撤销的。
words.en: If a decision, action, or process is irrevocable, it cannot be changed or reversed.

words.tr: adj. 死后的；死后出版的；遗腹的
words.ex: He received a posthumous award for his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢而被追授了奖项。
words.en: Posthumous means occurring, awarded, or appearing after the death of the originator.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；远古的；最初的
words.ex: The primordial soup formed the first life on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 原始汤形成了地球上的最初生命。
words.en: Primordial means existing at or from the beginning of time; primeval.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.tr: adj. 迟的；缓慢的；迟缓的
words.ex: He is tardy for school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上学都迟到。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tardy, you think that they are later than they should be or later than expected.

words.ex: The joy was transitory, and soon he felt sad again.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是暂时的，不久他又感到悲伤了。
words.en: Something that is transitory lasts only for a short time.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 性格•倾向

words.ex: The cat is agile and jumps high.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳得很高。
words.en: Someone who is agile can move quickly and easily.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.tr: adj. 漫不经心的；无忧无虑的
words.ex: He gave a blithe smile and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他漫不经心地笑了笑，然后走开了。
words.en: If you describe someone as blithe, you mean that they are carefree and cheerful.

words.ex: He was circumspect before signing the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在签署合同之前非常谨慎。
words.en: If you are circumspect, you think carefully about something before doing it, because there may be risks involved.

words.ex: The child was compliant and followed all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子很顺从，遵守了所有规则。
words.en: If someone or something is compliant, they act in accordance with rules, standards, or laws.

words.tr: adj. 娴静的；端庄的；假装矜持的
words.ex: She is a demure girl who never speaks loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个文静的女孩，从不大声说话。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a young woman, as demure, you mean they are quiet, shy, and behave so that they do not attract attention to themselves.

words.tr: adj. 有辨别力的；能洞悉的；眼光敏锐的； v. “discern”的现在分词；
words.ex: She is a discerning shopper who always finds the best quality.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有辨别力的购物者，总是能找到最好的质量。
words.en: If you describe someone as discerning, you mean that they are able to judge which things of a particular kind are good and which are bad.

words.ex: He is fussy about his food.
words.ex_cn: 他对食物很挑剔。
words.en: Someone who is fussy is very concerned with unimportant details and is difficult to please.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；无礼的；不相干的
words.ex: He gave an impertinent answer to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他给了老师一个鲁莽的回答。
words.en: If someone talks or behaves in a rather impolite and disrespectful way, especially towards someone who is older or in a position of authority, you can describe that person or their behaviour as impertinent.

words.ex: He looked incredulous when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他一脸难以置信。
words.en: If someone is incredulous, they are unable to believe something because it is very surprising or shocking.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；懒散的；好逸恶劳的
words.ex: He is indolent and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as indolent, you mean that they are lazy.

words.ex: The pope is considered infallible in matters of faith by some Catholics.
words.ex_cn: 一些天主教徒认为教皇在信仰问题上是一贯正确的。
words.en: If a person or thing is infallible, they are never wrong or never fail.

words.ex: The inquisitive child asked many questions about the stars.
words.ex_cn: 这个好奇的孩子问了很多关于星星的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as inquisitive, you mean that they are interested in a lot of different things and want to find out more about them.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；无礼的；侮慢的
words.ex: The insolent boy talked back to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个无礼的男孩顶撞了老师。
words.en: If you say that someone is insolent, you mean they are rude and do not show respect for people in positions of authority.

words.tr: adj. 海岛的；孤立的；思想褊狭的
words.ex: The insular village has no bridge to the mainland.
words.ex_cn: 这个海岛村庄没有桥通向大陆。
words.en: If you describe someone as insular, you are being critical of them because they are unwilling to meet new people or to consider new ideas.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.ex: The loud speaker is too obtrusive.
words.ex_cn: 这个扬声器太突兀了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is obtrusive, you mean they are noticeable in an unwelcome or inappropriate way.

words.ex: His overbearing boss always tells him what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他专横的老板总是告诉他该做什么。
words.en: If you describe someone as overbearing, you mean that they behave in a very unpleasant way because they are too confident of their own importance.

words.tr: adj. 别致的；时髦的；小巧玲珑的；活泼的；无礼的；唐突的
words.ex: She gave a pert reply to the interviewer's question.
words.ex_cn: 她对采访者的问题给出了无礼的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as pert, you mean that they are lively and confident, and perhaps slightly disrespectful.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；自命不凡的；浮华的
words.ex: He gave a pompous speech with big words.
words.ex_cn: 他用华丽的词藻做了一番自大的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as pompous, you mean that they behave or speak in a very serious way because they think they are more important than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.tr: adj. 精明练达的；有远见的；有洞察力的
words.ex: He is a sagacious man who always makes wise choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睿智的人，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; shrewd.

words.tr: adj. 屈从的；奴隶的；逢迎的
words.ex: He gave a servile answer to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他向老板给出了卑躬屈膝的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as servile, you disapprove of them because they are too eager to obey someone or do things for them.

words.tr: adj. 不修边幅的；邋遢的
words.ex: He wore slovenly clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着邋遢的衣服去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as slovenly, you disapprove of them because they are careless and untidy in their appearance or habits.

words.tr:
n. 云杉；云杉木
adj. 整洁漂亮的
v. 弄整洁；打扮漂亮
words.ex: The forest is full of tall spruce trees.
words.ex_cn: 森林里长满了高大的云杉树。
words.en: A spruce is a type of evergreen tree with needle-like leaves. As an adjective, it describes something neat and trim in appearance. As a verb, it means to make someone or something neat and smart in appearance.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.tr:
n. 逃学者；旷课者
adj. 逃学的；怠惰的
v. 逃学；旷课
words.ex: He is truant from school today.
words.ex_cn: 他今天逃学了。
words.en: A truant is a student who stays away from school without permission.

words.ex: He made an uncouth remark at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚餐时说了句粗俗的话。
words.en: If you describe a person as uncouth, you mean that their behavior is vulgar, rude, or socially unacceptable.

words.ex: The valiant soldier fought bravely to protect his team.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的士兵英勇战斗以保护他的队友。
words.en: Someone who is valiant is very brave and determined, especially in a difficult situation.

words.tr: adj. 有男子气概的；阳刚的；强有力的
words.ex: He is a virile man who works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的男子，每天努力工作。
words.en: If you describe a man as virile, you mean that he has the qualities that a man is traditionally expected to have, such as strength and sexual power.

words.ex: She is a vivacious girl who laughs loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个活泼的女孩，笑得很响亮。
words.en: If you describe someone as vivacious, you mean that they are lively, exciting, and attractive.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 政治•经济

words.ex: The refugees lived in abject poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这些难民过着凄惨的贫困生活。
words.en: Abject means extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading.

words.ex: The country has an agrarian economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家有一个农业经济。
words.en: Relating to land, especially agricultural land, or to the ownership or division of such land.

words.ex: He believes in an egalitarian society where everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一个人人平等的平等主义社会。
words.en: Egalitarian is used to describe something that is based on the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities.

words.tr:
n. 权宜之计；应急办法
adj. 权宜的
words.ex: Closing the factory was an expedient to save money.
words.ex_cn: 关闭工厂是为了省钱的权宜之计。
words.en: An expedient action or solution to a problem is one that is convenient or practical, although it may not be morally right.

words.tr: adj. 不合格的；不符合资格的
words.ex: He is ineligible to vote because he is under 18.
words.ex_cn: 他因为未满18岁而没有资格投票。
words.en: If someone is ineligible for something, they are not allowed to have it or do it because they have broken a rule or do not reach the standard that is needed.

words.ex: The onerous workload made her tired every day.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量让她每天都很累。
words.en: If you describe a task as onerous, you dislike having to do it because you find it difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.tr: adj. 难以捍卫的；站不住脚的；不堪一击的
words.ex: His excuse was untenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口站不住脚。
words.en: If an argument, theory, or position is untenable, it cannot be defended or supported against criticism.

words.ex: He invested money in a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他投资了一笔钱在一家小企业上。
words.en: If you invest in something, or if you invest a sum of money, you use your money in a way that you hope will increase its value, for example by paying it into a bank, or buying shares or property.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 气候•自然

words.ex: The land is arable and good for growing wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这块地是可耕的，适合种植小麦。
words.en: Arable land is land that is suitable for growing crops.

words.tr:
adj. 牛的；似牛的；迟钝的
n. 牛；牛科动物
words.ex: The bovine grazed quietly in the field.
words.ex_cn: 那头牛在田野里安静地吃草。
words.en: Relating to or resembling cattle; slow or dull in manner.

words.ex: The cactus has succulent leaves to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有多汁的叶子来储存水分。
words.en: (of food) tender, juicy, and tasty; (of a plant) having thick, fleshy tissues adapted to water storage.

words.tr: adj. 闷热的；性感的；撩人的
words.ex: The sultry weather made everyone feel tired.
words.ex_cn: 闷热的天气让每个人都感到疲惫。
words.en: Sultry weather is hot and damp in a way that makes you feel uncomfortable.

chapters.name: Level 12 形容词 程度•单位

words.tr: adj. 匆匆的；粗略的；仓促的
words.ex: He gave the report a cursory look.
words.ex_cn: 他粗略地看了看这份报告。
words.en: A cursory glance or examination is a quick one that is not very thorough.

words.ex: This lock is foolproof and easy to use.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁是万无一失的，而且容易使用。
words.en: A foolproof plan, system, or method is so well designed that it cannot go wrong or be used wrongly.

words.tr: adj. 无故的；无必要的；无偿的；免费的
words.ex: He made a gratuitous comment about her clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的衣服做了毫无必要的评论。
words.en: If you describe something as gratuitous, you mean that it is unnecessary, and often harmful or upsetting.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.tr: adj. 非物质的；无形的；不重要的
words.ex: The color is immaterial to the function.
words.ex_cn: 颜色对功能无关紧要。
words.en: If you say that something is immaterial, you mean that it is not important or not relevant.

words.tr: adj. 无法克服的；难以解决的；不可逾越的
words.ex: The problem seemed insurmountable.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题似乎无法克服。
words.en: If you describe something as insurmountable, you mean that it is so great or severe that it cannot be dealt with.

words.tr: adj. 不能赎回的；不能兑现的；不可救药的
words.ex: The bond is irredeemable and will never be paid back.
words.ex_cn: 这种债券是不能赎回的，永远不会被偿还。
words.en: If you describe something as irredeemable, you mean that it is so bad or undesirable that there is no way to improve it or make it acceptable.

words.ex: His laudable effort helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他值得赞美的努力帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Deserving praise and commendation.

words.ex: Bears are omnivorous animals.
words.ex_cn: 熊是杂食动物。
words.en: An omnivorous animal or person eats both plants and meat.

words.ex: This is the optimal time to plant flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这是种植花卉的最佳时间。
words.en: Most favorable or desirable; best.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.ex: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地点了点头，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something that is done as perfunctory, you mean that it is done as a duty or a formality, without much care or interest.

words.tr:
adj. 全体参加的；无限的；完全的
n. 全会；全体会议
words.ex: The plenary session started at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 全体会议在上午九点开始。
words.en: A plenary session or meeting is one that is attended by everyone who has the right to attend.

words.ex: The residual water dried up quickly.
words.ex_cn: 残留的水很快就干了。
words.en: Remaining after the greater part or quantity has gone.

words.tr: adj. 似是而非的；貌似有理的
words.ex: His argument is specious and misleading.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点看似有理但具有误导性。
words.en: Something that is specious seems to be good, sound, or correct but is actually wrong or false.

words.ex: The view from the mountain was stupendous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: Something that is stupendous is extremely impressive or large.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.ex: He faced undue pressure from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他受到了来自老板的过度压力。
words.en: If you describe something bad as undue, you mean that it is greater or more extreme than you think is reasonable or appropriate.

words.tr: adj. 毫不含糊的；清楚明白的
words.ex: His answer was unequivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答是明确无误的。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude as unequivocal, you mean that it is completely clear and very firm.

words.ex: He made an unscrupulous deal to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了省钱做了不道德的交易。
words.en: If you describe someone as unscrupulous, you are critical of them because they are prepared to act in a dishonest or immoral way in order to get what they want.

words.ex: He gave a vehement reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了激烈的回答。
words.en: If a person or their actions or comments are vehement, the person has very strong feelings or opinions and expresses them forcefully.

words.ex: The wanton destruction of the forest shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对森林的恣意破坏让每个人都感到震惊。
words.en: If someone describes a person or their behaviour as wanton, they are critical of them for behaving in a very uncontrolled or unacceptable way, often without caring about the consequences.

words.tr: contr.contr. 不会，将不（等于 will not）
words.ex: He won't go to school today.
words.ex_cn: 他今天不去学校。
words.en: Won't is the usual spoken form of 'will not'.

chapters.name: Level 12 副词 位置•场所

words.ex: They walked abreast down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他们并肩走在街上。
words.en: If people or things are abreast, they are lined up next to each other, side by side, and often facing the same direction.

words.ex: The boys went afield to hunt birds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们离家远去打猎。
words.en: If you go afield, you go a long way from home or from your usual surroundings.

words.tr:
adv. 向艉部（或机尾）；在艉部（或机尾）
adj. 艉部的
words.ex: The crew moved aft to the engine room.
words.ex_cn: 船员们向船尾的发动机房移动。
words.en: At or towards the stern of a ship or tail of an aircraft.

words.ex: The eastern city has many old temples.
words.ex_cn: 东部的城市有许多古老的寺庙。
words.en: Eastern means in or from the east part of an area.

words.tr: adv. 成碎片地；弄碎地；分离地
words.ex: The kingdom was torn asunder by civil war.
words.ex_cn: 这个王国因内战而被撕裂。
words.en: Into parts or pieces; apart.

words.tr: adv. 在其中；在那里；在那一点上
words.ex: The document outlines the terms and conditions therein.
words.ex_cn: 该文件概述了其中的条款和条件。
words.en: In that place, matter, or respect.

chapters.name: Level 12 副词 时间•频率

words.tr:
adj. 徒步的；在准备中的；在进行中
adv. 徒步地；在准备中地；在进行中
words.ex: The hikers went afoot through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者们徒步穿越了森林。
words.en: If you say that a plan or scheme is afoot, it is already happening or being planned.
